Return Values
If there are no error conditions, the $cm_get_coverage system function returns either a
zero or a positive integer value. You compare this return value with the return value of the

The $cm_get_limit System Function
$cm_get_limit system function. When they return matching positive integer values for a
specific type of coverage and for a matching part of the design, then the current simulation
run yields no more additional coverage data. Without this comparison, which positive
integer is returned from this system function has no particular significance.
When there is an error this system function returns negative integer values. The text
macros for, integer values of, and meaning of the return values are as follows:
'CM_ERROR -1 There is an invalid argument.
‘CM_NOCOV -2 The specified type of coverage data is not available in
this simulation run.
The $cm_get_limit System Function
You use the $cm_get_limit system function to return a value that you compare with the
return value from the $cm_get_coverage system function to determine how close you are
to gathering all the coverage data you can gather in the current simulation of a specified
coverage type and from a specified part of the design.
The return value from this system task is a integer representing how much of the specified
type of coverage information, for the specified part of the design, VCS could gather during
the simulation. In contrast, the return value of the $cm_get_coverage system function is
an integer representing how much coverage information of the specified type VCS has
gathered so far.
The syntax of the $cm_get_limit system function is, with the exception of the system
function name, identical to the syntax of the $cm_get_coverage system function.
$cm_get_limit(type, include_hierarchy,
"module_or_instance",)
The arguments, their text macros, and integer values are identical to those of the
$cm_get_coverage system function. When you use these two system functions as
intended, you use the same arguments to specify the type of coverage, whether to include
the design hierarchy under the specified module definitions and instance hierarchical
names and matching module definitions and instance hierarchical names.
Example 1 shows how to use this API to stop simulation when you have sufficient
coverage data. Example 2shows how to monitor how close you are to full coverage data.
Example 1: Stopping Simulation When You Have Sufficient Coverage Data

‘timescale 1 ns / 1 ns
reg r1,r2;
wire w1, w2;
integer coverage_on_or_off,check_coverage,get_coverage,get_limit;
design design1 (w1,r1);
#0 get_limit=$cm_get_limit(‘CM_SOURCE,‘CM_MODULE,"top.design1");
#5 coverage_on_or_off= $cm_coverage(‘CM_STOP,‘CM_SOURCE,‘CM_HIER,"top");
#5 coverage_on_or_off=
$cm_coverage(‘CM_START,‘CM_SOURCE,‘CM_MODULE,"top.design1");
r1=0;
#1000 $finish;
end
always
#25 r1=~r1;
get_coverage=$cm_get_coverage(‘CM_SOURCE,‘CM_MODULE,"top.design1");
if (get_coverage>=get_limit*0.9)
$finish;
end
In Example 1, the initial block does the following:
1. Assigns to integer get_limit the return value of $cm_get_limit, which represents
how much line coverage data for module instance top.design1 VCS could gather during
the simulation.
2. Turns off line coverage for the entire design after 5 time units. The delay is specified so
that turning off line coverage happens after it is started by the CoverMeter.tasks file.
3. Turns on line coverage 5 time units after that but only for module instance top.design1.
4. Initializes a stimulus reg.
5. Schedules simulation to end at simulation time 1010.

Also in Example 1, the always block does the following:
1. Toggles the stimulus reg.
2. Assigns to integer get_coverage the return value of $cm_get_coverage, which
represents how much line coverage data for module instance top.design1 VCS has
gathered so far.
3. Looks to see if the integer assigned to get_coverage is greater than or equal to 90%
of the integer assigned to get_limit, and if it is, terminates the simulation.
Example 2: Displaying How Close You Are To Full Coverage Data
covdata = $cm_coverage(‘CM_CHECK, ‘CM_SOURCE, ‘CM_HIER, "i1");
$display($time,,"Source coverage check: %d", covdata);
#1; // wait until after the coverage stuff is initialized
covdata = $cm_coverage(‘CM_CHECK, ‘CM_SOURCE, ‘CM_HIER, "i1");
$display($time,,"Source coverage check: %d", covdata);
covdata = $cm_get_limit(‘CM_SOURCE, ‘CM_HIER, "i1");
$display($time,,"Source limit : %d", covdata);
#999;
forever
covdata = $cm_get_coverage(‘CM_SOURCE, ‘CM_HIER, "i1");
$display($time,,"Source coverage : %d", covdata);
#100000;
end
end
In Example 2, the initial block does the following:
1. At time 0, assigns to integer covdata the return value of the $cm_coverage system
function that is checking to see if VCS is gathering line coverage information about
module instance i1 and the hierarchy under i1.
2. Displays the return value.
3. Waits 1 time unit and then once again assigns to integer covdata the return value of
the $cm_coverage system function that is checking for the same thing.
4. Displays the return value again. This value should be different now that the
CoverMeter.tasks file has started VCS for line coverage.
5. Assigns to integer covdata the return value of the $cm_get_limit system function for
the same type of coverage and the same part of the design.
6. Displays the return value from the $cm_get_limit system function.

7. After 999 time units begins a forever loop that does the following:
Assigns to integer covdata the return value of the $cm_get_coverage system function
for the same type of coverage and the same part of the design.
Displays this return value.
Waits 100,000 time units before beginning the loop again.

corresponding test annotations from multiple test runs are also stored in the .vdb

Just as coverage results for multiple test runs are stored in a .vdb database, the
corresponding test annotations from multiple test runs are also stored in the .vdb
database. Each test is assigned a unique location.
You may add the following information to a test run:
• A name that is independent from the test run's directory name (See section Specifying
a Name for a Test Run)
• A test run status, such as passed or failed (See section Adding or Changing the Test
Status of a Test Run)
• Custom annotations, such as a description of the purpose of the test, its owner, and so
on. (See section Support for Adding Custom Annotations)
Specifying a Name for a Test Run
You can specify a name to a test run using one of the following utilities:
• Using the -cm_test Option
• Using the cm_post Command
• Using the $cm_post System Call
Using the -cm_test Option
During runtime, you can use the -cm_test option to specify a name to a test run as
% simv -cm_test " <test_name>" -cm_name <test_to_be_annotated>
where, test_name is the unique name specified for a test.
test_to_be_annotated is the test that needs to be annotated.
The argument given to - cm_test is saved in the test record and does not change even if
the test directory is renamed.

When using -cm_test, you should also use -cm_name to assign a unique
location in the coverage database for your test's results. If you do not provide
-cm_name then the test data location defaults to test. Subsequent simv runs
without -cm_name overwrite the data previously stored in the default test
location.
If a test name is specified for a test run, the test name is displayed in the
tests.txt/tests.html reports in URG along with the directory path name. For example,
consider the following simv command:
simv -cm line+cond+tgl -cm_test "TEST1" -cm_name test11
This simv command generates the tests.html report (see Figure 22). The report shows
that the test location of the test name, TEST1, is simv1/test11. Similarly for TEST2 is
simv1/test11 and so on.
Figure 22 Report Generated Using -cm_test and -cm_name

Using the cm_post Command
The cm_post command enables you to specify a name for a test run. To specify the name
for the test run, use the following syntax:
% cm_post -dir <dir.vdb> … [-test_name test_name]
% cm_post -dir simv1.vdb -test_name test11
If the test run is already assigned a name in the database, the name is overridden with the
new test name.
The coverage data from multiple test runs is merged into a single VDB containing a single
test directory using the -dbname option of URG. You can use the -test_run option to
specify a particular test to be annotated.
For example, if the test contains the data from the test runs simv1/test11 and simv1/
test12, then pass -test_run "simv1/test12" or -test_run "simv/test11" to annotate
the specific test run.
Using the $cm_post System Call
During simulation, the design source code can invoke the $cm_post system call to add
information to the test run’s record. The information can be test name, test status, or
custom annotation. The 'CM_TEST, 'CM_TEST_STATUS, and 'CM_CUSTOM_VALUE macros
are defined in $VCS_HOME/include/CoverMeter.vh, which are included in the design
source code from where $cm_post is invoked.
To specify a name to a test run, include the 'CM_TEST macro, as shown in the following
examples:
$cm_post('CM_TEST, "test_group1");
$cm_post('CM_TEST, "common_test");
Adding or Changing the Test Status of a Test Run
You can change the test run status using one of the following methods:
• Using the cm_post command, you can override the test run status after the simulation
has exited, for example, after comparing the output to expected results. This command
opens the designated VDB for the test and modifies the test record (See section Using
the cm_post Command)
• Using the $cm_post system call (See section Using the $cm_post System Call)

The status recorded for a test that is not obviously failed is unknown. You must explicitly
set the test result to pass via cm_post after they have confirmed that the test did indeed
pass.
You can view test run status in the test reports in URG. For example, Figure 23 shows the
test run status in the STATUS column:
Figure 23 Test Run Status in URG
Using the cm_post Command
After a test run is complete, you can also use the cm_post command to add or change
the status to a test record. To add a status to the test record information, use the following
command:
cm_post [ -test_status "user assigned test status" ] [ -test_name "name
of the test to be annotated" ] -dir dir.vdb
where, status is "pass", "fail", "assert", "warn" or "unknown".
cm_post -test_status "pass" -test_name simv1/test11 -dir simv1.vdb
If the test run is already assigned a status in the database, the status is overridden with
the new test status.
Run cm_post as part of the same script/driver that runs your simulation. This
enables your system to capture the pass/fail status and other properties right
away and to parallelize the cm_post update process. The cm_post process

only takes a few seconds to update a test record, but if done serially on a large
number of tests it can still take time to complete.
Starting with VCS 2025.06, mixed usage of post-processing tools is not
supported. For example, a 32-bit URG or cm_post cannot be used to process
a VDB generated from a 64-bit VCS, and vice versa. If the VDB is generated
using a 64-bit VCS, add the -full64 option to URG or cm_post to ensure
compatibility.
Using the $cm_post System Call
During simulation, the design source code can invoke the $cm_post system call through
the `CM_TEST_STATUS macro to add the status of the simulation run.
To specify the status of the simulation run, include the 'CM_TEST_STATUS macro, as shown
in the following examples:
$cm_post('CM_TEST_STATUS, "pass");
$cm_post('CM_TEST_STATUS, "fail");

To specify the status of the simulation run, include the 'CM_TEST_STATUS macro, as shown
in the following examples:
$cm_post('CM_TEST_STATUS, "pass");
$cm_post('CM_TEST_STATUS, "fail");
If the SystemVerilog $warning, $error, or $fatal system calls are invoked, the
appropriate test status string ("warning", "fail $error ", "fail $fatal ") is saved to the
test record. The order of severity is $fatal > $cm_post > $error > $warning.
The higher severity overrides lower, therefore, if both $warning and $error are called in a
single simulation, the test status is saved as "fail $error ".
If $fatal happens, the status is "fail $fatal ". If the program calls $error, and never
calls $fatal, and if $cm_post is not called after $error, the status is "fail $error ".
If $cm_post is called after $error, then its setting overrides $error.
After the coverage data is dumped, the test status set through $cm_post is reset.
Support for Adding Custom Annotations
You can add annotation to a test run using one of the following methods:
• Using the cm_post Command to Annotate
• Using the $cm_post System Call to Annotate

Using the cm_post Command to Annotate
After a test run is complete, annotations are added to a compile-time VDB or a test run
after executing the cm_post command. The following cm_post command is used to add
annotations to a test run:
% cm_post -dir <dir.vdb> … [-custom_values_file <name_of_the
file>][-test_status <status>][-test_name < test_name>]
If dir.vdb is a compile-time VDB, by default any annotations are placed on the design
even if there is test data present. If there are multiple test runs in the test, pass -test_run
to identify the specific test to be annotated.
For example, if the simv1/merge1 test is a merged test that has the test runs simv1/
test11 and simv/test12, then pass -test_run "simv1/test11" or -test_run" simv1/
test12" to annotate the specific test run.
The list of custom value pairs dumped into an edited test is the combination of the pairs
passed through the command line and those already present in the coverage database.
Adding an annotation overrides any previously existing annotation with the
same key.
These annotations are saved into the compile-time VDB and simv test run records
respectively, and are accessed through the post-processing applications. Test record and
compile-time VDB annotations are automatically displayed in URG reports. For example,
Figure 24 shows the annotations in a test run:
Figure 24 Annotations in a Test Run
Using the $cm_post System Call to Annotate
During simulation, you can add any custom value pair to a test run and can later search
these strings in the post-processing applications. The new `CM_CUSTOM_VALUE macro
enables you to add any custom value pair.

$cm_post('CM_CUSTOM_VALUE, "owner", "xyz");
$cm_post('CM_CUSTOM_VALUE, "no_of_hours_run", "1");
If the value argument is an empty string, VCS deletes the custom value pair, if it already
exists, that has the same key as that of the $cm_post system call. In the following
example, the custom value pair with “owner” key is deleted:
$cm_post('CM_CUSTOM_VALUE, "owner", "");
The list of custom value pairs dumped into a test is the cumulative of the pairs passed
through the command line and those passed through $cm_post. Adding a custom value
pair overrides any previously existing custom value pair with the same key.
Backward Compatibility
This enhancement does not cause the existing VDBs, exclusion files, or any other VCS
coverage files to become incompatible with VDBs containing these enhanced test records.
It enables you to merge the VDBs with existing test records with the VDBs that contain
new-style test records.
cm_post Options
This section describes the various options associated with the cm_post command:
-dir vdbdir : Enables you to specify the VDB directory containing the test to be updated.
-test_name: Enables you to provide the name of the test to be updated.
-test_status statusstring : Enables you to assign a status to the test.
-user_test_name: Enables you to provide a user-defined name to the test.
-test_run: Enables you to provide the name of the test run in merged VDB to be
updated.
-custom_values_file filename : Enables you to apply key and value pairs to the test.
The most common use of cm_post is to apply a test status to a test in a simulation VDB.
For example, the following command assigns the status "pass" to the test simv/test0 in
the VDB directory simv.vdb:
cm_post -dir simv.vdb -test_name simv/test0 -test_status "pass"
The test status strings "pass”, "fail", "assert", "warn", or "unknown" are treated
specially and assign that status to the designated test.

The status value is reported in URG, Verdi, and in HVP tools, is accessible from UCAPI
applications, and is used by features such as URG’s -skip_failed_test option. For
more information, see URG’s test reporting options such as -show testrecords .
You can also designate a special test status with a comment, such as:
cm_post -dir simv.vdb -test_name simv/test0
-test_status "waveform mismatch(pass)"
For your reference, these strings are shown in the reports. However, the strings in
parenthesis are ignored by the tools.
The -user_test_name switch assigns an alternate name to the designated test that can
be seen in URG and Verdi.
The -custom_values_file switch is used to assign arbitrary key/value pairs of data to
a test. This can be useful for flows that use categories to gather information about test
runs, such as seed values, configuration file names, and owner names. The format of the
-custom_values_file file is key:value. The following are the examples for key:value:
owner:xyz
config:preA7
The -test_run option is used to update a test in a VDB that has already been merged.
The use of this option is same as the option -test_name used in a VDB that has not been
merged. For example:
cm_post -dir merged.vdb -test_run rundir/test0

You can access covergroup coverage data during simulation using C code. You need to
add $coverage_dump and $coverage_reset system tasks to the Verilog code to perform
the following tasks:
• Monitor the coverage status periodically and modify external stimuli.
• Clear the coverage data from the simulation state so that any further data collected
starts from scratch.
• Monitoring the Coverage Data
• Resetting the Coverage Data

Monitoring the Coverage Data
You can monitor the coverage data during simulation as follows:
• Invoke a system task inside Verilog to dump the current coverage status to disk.
• Open the dumped database using UCAPI functions and examine the coverage status.
The system task $coverage_dump atomically dumps all coverage data to the specified
test name. You can give a simple test name, mytest, or a composite name mydir/
mytest, and specify where the data will be dumped. For example, a Verilog program could
periodically dump the coverage status as follows:
always@(dump_me) begin
$coverage_dump("mydir/myfile");
$check_my_coverage(…);
end
Using this syntax, you can toggle the signal dump_me to cause the current coverage status
to be dumped to the mydir directory. The snapshot of data that UCAPI calls will be given
the name, myfile. In this example, mydir/mytest is overwritten whenever dump_me is
toggled, but you can write a code to give a different name each time based on a counter.
You can also call $coverage_dump directly using DPI if it is wrapped in a Verilog task.
export "DPI" task dump_cov_data(string s);
task dump_cov_data(string s);
$coverage_dump(s);
endtask
After the dump is complete, the PLI function (in this example, check_my_coverage) will
be invoked, and you can use UCAPI to open the dumped database, check the coverage
status, and take appropriate action. You can use UCAPI to load the data as follows:
covdbHandle design = covdb_load(covdbDesign, NULL, "mydir"); covdbHandle
test = covdb_load(design, design, "mydir/myfile");
From here, the application can iterate through all covergroups, or walk over the design
hierarchy. The $coverage_dump operation is automatic, and there is no opening or closing
of a database. When $coverage_dump is called, the specified database is opened, written,
and closed, in one automatic operation.
As soon as a database is dumped using $coverage_dump, it is accessible.
Do not attempt to access the database until the $coverage_dump operation is
complete.

Resetting the Coverage Data
You can reset the accumulated coverage data using the system task, $coverage_reset.
The system task, $coverage_reset, clears all coverage data for all covergroups in the
current simulation. For example:
always
#10000
$coverage_dump("mydir/myfile");
if ($check_my_coverage(…))
$coverage_reset();
end
If the PLI function, $check_my_coverage, returns true, all functional coverage data
is reset, as if nothing had been covered up to this point. To dump an empty coverage
database, where no bins are marked covered, you can write as follows:
$coverage_reset(); $coverage_dump("mydir/myfile");
The $coverage_reset system task does not remove any covergroups from the current
simulation run. It just resets all the bins’ hit counts to 0. You can only overwrite existing
databases. However, if you want additional data to be merged with an existing database,
you can write it with a new name as follows:
$coverage_dump.

$coverage_dump("mydir/mytest1"); … $coverage_reset(); …
$coverage_dump("mydir/mytest2");
This code writes two different databases to disk – mydir/mytest1 and mydir/mytest2.
You can use UCAPI to load the first one with covdb_load, and merge the second with
covdb_loadmerge, merging the data from the two separate databases. This way, you can
save and merge distinct databases.
Ignoring Coverage Collected During Parts of Simulation
You can ignore any collected coverage data. Consider the following example:
At time N: $coverage_dump("mydir/beforeN");
At time M: $coverage_reset();
In this example, if there is a period between time N and M for which you wish to ignore any
collected coverage data, turn coverage off during this time by writing the coverage status
before time N to one database, then clearing coverage data at time M before allowing
simulation to proceed.
The data collected after time M will be written out when simulation exits (or at the next call
to $coverage_dump) and will include only the data collected since time M. For example, if

test is called “mydir/test.db”, when merged with the data stored in mydir/beforeN, the
effect is as if coverage had been disabled between time N and M.
design = covdb_load(covdbDesign, NULL, "mydir");
test = covdb_load(covdbTest, design, "mydir/beforeN");
test = covdb_loadmerge(covdbTest, test, "mydir/test");
Now the handle “test” contains the coverage data from simulation from time 1 through
N, and from time M through the end of simulation. However, any covergroups instantiated
between time N and M will still be in the final written database (or any database written after
time M). You cannot disable or delete these groups through this interface.
Accessing Coverage Data
The coverage data is accessed during simulation as follows:
1. DPI function is defined and coverage data is dumped on demand.
export "DPI" task dump_cov_data(string s);
export "DPI" task clear_cov_data;
task dump_cov_data(string s);
$coverage_dump(s);
endtask task clear_cov_data;
$coverage_reset();
endtask
2. After simulation begins, coverage is dumped by PLI code calling the DPI-exported.
task dump_cov_data:
… dump_cov_data("mydir/test1"); …
3. The PLI code, which has been linked with UCAPI, then opens the database and looks

coverage_reset();
endtask
2. After simulation begins, coverage is dumped by PLI code calling the DPI-exported.
task dump_cov_data:
… dump_cov_data("mydir/test1"); …
3. The PLI code, which has been linked with UCAPI, then opens the database and looks
for the covergroup of interest (assume tbMetric has already been found).
covdbHandle design = covdb_load(covdbDesign, NULL, "mydir");
covdbHandle test = covdb_load(design, design, "mydir/test1");
covdbHandle group, groups = covdb_qualified_iterate(test, tbMetric,
covdbDefinitions);
while((group = covdb_scan(groups))) { if (this is the group I want …)
{ … check coverage status …
} } covdb_release_handle(groups);
4. Control then returns to the simulation, which continues collecting coverage. At a later
point, the PLI code again causes coverage results to be dumped and checks the
covergroup of interest once more. The new test is loaded and the covergroup handle is
acquired from scratch.
… dump_cov_data("mydir/test2");
design = covdb_load(covdbDesign, NULL, "mydir");
test = covdb_load(design, design, "mydir/test2");
groups = covdb_qualified_iterate(test, tbMetric,
covdbDefinitions);

while((group = covdb_scan(groups))) { if (this is the group I want …)
{ … check coverage status …
} } covdb_release_handle(groups);
5. The coverage data is reset and simulation continues.
clear_cov_data(); return;
6. This iteration is repeated as many times as required.
At any given point, the PLI code can dump coverage, analyze it, reset it, or allow it to
continue without resetting. When simulation exits, coverage data is dumped as normal2
– the $coverage_dump and $coverage_reset system tasks have no effect on the final
database name.
After simulation exits, a standalone UCAPI program can be used to load any of the
databases dumped during simulation (or the name of the final db), using the names
specified when they were dumped, as shown in the example code.
The name specified explicitly at compile time or the name given during simulation using
the SystemVerilog $set_coverage_db_name system task. Because covergroups can
be dynamically instantiated during simulation, the database written at time N may have
fewer groups in it than the database written at a later time N+C. This is because VCS only
collects coverage data for covergroups that are instantiated during simulation.
Thus, there is no guarantee that all databases dumped from a given simulation run will
have the same groups in them. However, these databases can still be merged to create
a single result, just as coverage results from multiple distinct simulation runs that may
instantiate different groups can be merged. Note that there is an existing mechanism that
allows individual covergroups to be disabled and that is using the $cg_coverage_control
system task. The same system task can be used to disable all the covergroups if there is
no covergroup name specified as an argument.

title: 1 for coverage on
text:
group_name is an optional covergroup name. If not given, all covergroups are affected by
the selected mode. If a covergroup is specified, only that group is affected.
Covergroup names are specified with a scope name and a group name separated by the
"::" token. For example, to disable coverage collection for a covergroup cg1 declared in the
module tb, use the following:
$cg_coverage_control(0, "tb::cg1")

Note that if the scope name is not provided along with the covergroup name, VCS gives
the following warning message:
Warning-[FCUDCG] Undefined covergroup
No covergroup exist with the name 'cg1' passed to cg_coverage_control
task.
Therefore, it is mandatory to specify the scope name of the covergroup name as follows:
$cg_coverage_control(0,"tb::cg1");
If all covergroups are not excluded, then it is expected that the excluded covergroups are
shown with their score as zero in URG and Verdi.
There is no additional way to explicitly disable functional coverage. If $coverage_dump
is called from multiple blocks at the same time with the same argument, both calls will
be processed, although the order does not matter since they both will write exactly the
same data to disk. If $coverage_dump is called from multiple blocks at the same time with
different arguments, two identical databases will be written.
If $coverage_dump is called multiple times during simulation with no $coverage_reset,
the databases dumped will have “overlapping” data. For example, if you perform the
following:
$coverage_dump("mydir/test1");
…
more simulation
…
$coverage_dump("mydir/test2");
Then the mydir/test2 directory contains all the coverage data (hit counts, and so on).
from mydir/test1 and the data collected after mydir/test1 is dumped. Thus, if you use
covdb_loadmerge to merge mydir/test1 and mydir/test2, some of the coverage data
in effect is duplicated.
For example, say that when mydir/test1 is dumped, bin B1 had 15 hits. When mydir/
test2 is dumped, B1 will have 25 hits. If you merge mydir/test1 and mydir/test2, B1
will have 40 hits. It is the responsibility of your application to manage the relationship of
these databases, since there is no way for UCAPI to know that mydir/test is really a
subset of mydir/test2.

Configure the urg command-line tool to merge, report, grade, and exclude coverage data
from VCS simulation databases. Option categories span report formatting, code and
functional coverage metrics, database merging (including parallel and flexible merge),
exclusion file management, test grading, and HVP plan annotation. Requires one or more
.vdb coverage databases as input. Operates in batch mode from the command line.
The urg command-line options are grouped into the following categories:

• Exclusion Options

-excl_append_annotation
Keeps multiple exclusion annotations for same object.
-excl_embed
The -excl_embed option is used with the URG tool to embed exclusions from an exclude
file directly into a coverage database (VDB). When you use this option, URG creates a
new VDB that contains the exclusions specified in the exclude files. After the exclusions
are embedded in the VDB, they are marked as unreachable and cannot be undone.
Annotations added to the exclusions are not preserved.
Embedding exclusions instead of loading them from an exclude file can significantly speed
up the VDB loading time in URG and Verdi.
% urg -full64 -dir input_vdb -dbname output_vdb -excl_embed -elfile
exclude_file
Here,
input_vdb: The original coverage database.

output_vdb: The new coverage database with embedded exclusions.
exclude_file: The file containing the exclusions to embed.
This command does not create the URG report and the .html file.
The coverage database does not include -hier exclusions when you use
excl_embed. Use -excl_embed only with -elfile or -elfilelist. If you do
not specify these options, VCS reports an error.
-excl_bypass_checks
By default, when an exclude file is specified to URG, the checksums stored in the exclude
file are compared to the checksums in the design, and if there are mismatches, the
exclusions are not applied.
If the -excl_bypass_checks option is given, those comparisons are not done, and all the
exclusions are applied.
% urg -elfile <elfilename> -excl_bypass_checks
You must specify the -elfile option with the -excel_bypass_checks option, else an
error is generated.
-excl_strict
Does not allow covered objects to be excluded. '-elfile <file>' must be given when this
option is used.

the required exclusions.

create queue for available machine, such as for 2 machines and '-maxjobs
3' 'machine1, machine2, machine1, machine2, machine1, machine2'.

-feature <hvp_feature_name>
Enables you to specify HVP scopes that you want to annotate with a coverage database
or userdata. Its syntax is as follows:
urg -plan <hvp_filename> -feature <hvp_feature_name> -dir
<coverage_database>
or
urg -plan <hvp_filename> -feature <hvp_feature_name> -userdata <file>
urg -plan myplan.hvp -feature Plan.f_block -dir blk.vdb
or
urg -plan myplan.hvp -feature Plan.f_chip -userdata blk.udt
You may specify wildcard in the feature name as follows:
urg -plan myplan.hvp -feature "Plan.*_block" -dir blk.vdb
or
urg -plan myplan.hvp -feature "Plan.*_chip" -userdata blk.udt

You may specify multiple -feature options with URG as follows:
urg -plan myplan.hvp -feature Plan.f_block1 -dir blk1.vdb -userdata
blk1.udt -feature Plan.f_block2 -dir blk2.vdb -userdata blk2.udt
The -feature option enables you to specify which coverage databases are annotated
onto which features in the plan. For example, the data in blk1.vdb and blk1.udt is
annotated onto the Plan.f_block1 feature. Similarly, the data in blk2.vdb and blk2.udt
is annotated onto the Plan.f_block2 feature.
Note that if the -feature/-featurefile option is not used, then all the data from all
coverage databases and userdata files are annotated to every feature in the plan. For
details on -featurefile, see -featurefile <hvp_feature_filename>.

-merge_across_libs
Merges modules across different libraries.
Consider a scenario in which the kp_fsm module is present in two different directories, say
base.vdb and input.vdb, of the same library, say LIB. The number of assertions in the
module is different in both the directories, say N1 in base.vdb and N2 in input.vdb. By
default, VCS merges these modules (N1 union N2) and shows LIB.kp_fsm in the merged
report. If the kp_fsm module exists in two different libraries, say BASE and INPUT, VCS
does not merge these modules and their assertions. It shows two independent modules,
BASE.kp_fsm and INPUT.kp_fsm, in the merged report as follows:

If you want to merge the modules that belong to the different libraries, use the
mege_across_libs switch as follows:
urg -metric assert -dir base.vdb -dir input.vdb -merge_across_libs
-format text
The switch enables you to merge both the modules and displays a merged module
in the merged report. For example, when you use this switch, it merges kp_fsm and
their assertions of both BASE and INPUT. In the merged report, the switch shows the
merged module with the name as kp_fsm instead of showing two individual modules,
BASE.kp_fsm and INPUT.kp_fsm (see the figure below):
Exclusions With -merge_across_libs
You may exclude coverage objects using an exclusion file with -merge_across_libs
to remove library names from the exclusion file. To exclude objects with
-merge_across_libs, generate the merged database with the -dbname option as follows:
urg -metric assert -dir simv.vdb -merge_across_libs -dbname
simv_merge.vdb

Here, simv_merge.vdb is the merged database on which you may use to create
exclusions. After generating the merged database, apply the mod_1.el exclusion file with
-merge_across_libs as follows:
urg -metric assert -dir simv_merge.vdb -merge_across_libs -elfile
mod_1.el

-grade [quick|index|cost|scores|greedy|list][goal R]
[columns][timelimit N] [maxtests N][minincr R][reqtests
file_name][testfile][listonly]
quick
Generates a grading report, displaying cumulative and incremental values of each metric
for each test in the order they are found in the vdbs or in which they are given in a -tests
file (if specified). The quick grading algorithm is linear in the number of tests.
Cumulative value is the coverage score after that test is merged with all previous tests in
the graded list. For each metric, incremental value is the score improvement contributed to
the cumulative value by that test after merging.
index
Produces a report where the tests have been put in best-first order based on usefulness of
the tests. The tests report shows the cumulative, stand-alone, and incremental scores for
each test in the graded list.
Cumulative value is the coverage score after that test is merged with all previous tests in
the graded list. Stand-alone value represents the individual score of that test by itself. For
each metric, incremental value is the score improvement contributed to the cumulative
value by that test after merging. The index argument is the default for the -grade option,
except that if index is given explicitly, covergroups are graded in the ratio mode (see the
-group ratio option). If only -grade is given with no suboption, covergroups are graded
using the LRM algorithm.
cost [cputime|simtime|clocktime]

Places tests in best-first order with the goal of minimizing the total cost (cpu time,
simulation cycles, or clock time) instead of minimizing the total number of tests.
scores [total|test|incr]
Shows the tests in default order and gives their stand-alone scores only. The score
grading algorithm is linear in the number of tests.
The simulation time/random seed for testbench coverage in URG is shown with the
-grade scores option only. The -grade scores option gives information for seed/
time and score for each test, and also lists the tests in the best first order, which is not
expensive.
At least one sub-argument must be given with scores, however one or more sub-
arguments can be given if separated by a + character. For example:
-grade scores total+test+incr
where,
total: Reports total accumulated score for the test.
test: Reports the standalone score of a test for each metric.
incr: Reports the incremental contribution of that test to the total.
greedy
Places tests in best-first order with the goal of minimizing the total number of tests, using
an older, slower algorithm. This option will be deprecated in a future release.
goal R
Stops grading when the selected tests' total cumulative coverage score equals or exceeds
R. If not specified, the program grades all specified tests. Applies to index, cost and
greedy algorithms only.
columns [col1+col2+]
Instead of using the default information columns in the grading report, shows the specified
columns along with the score for each test. The supported columns are:
- simtime : Simulation time
- cputime : CPU time
- clocktime : Clock time
- seed : random seed value
indexlimit N

Tracks at most N covering tests for each coverable object when using index or cost
grading. Higher values will produce more accurate results, but utilize more memory.
timelimit N
Specifies the time limit for the report generator to run before exiting. Only those tests that
are graded before the time limit is hit are included in the graded list.
maxtests N
Specifies the maximum number of tests to be selected in the report. Applies to index, cost
and greedy grading only.
minincr
Stops selecting tests when no additional tests can increase the overall score by at least
minincr. Applies to index, cost and greedy grading only. This value is specified as a real
number between 0.00 and 100.00.
reqtests file_name
Use this option with index, cost, or greedy to specify reading a list of test names from
file_name for inclusion in the grading report. Those tests are included at the top of the
graded list, regardless of their scores or effectiveness for coverage.
testfile
Use this option with -grade to generate the
gradedtests.txt
gradedtests.txt text file, the
gradedtests.txt file contains a simple list of graded tests.
listonly
Use this option with -grade to generate only the tests.txt or tests.html report.

Allows you to specify how coverage data from instance hierarchies in different designs
should be combined when merged.
urg -dir base.vdb -dir input.vdb -mapfile file_name
where, file_name is the mapping configuration file. For more information, see the section
"Mapping Coverage" in the Coverage Technology User Guide.
-map <module_name>
Maps subhierarchy code coverage from one design to another. This option is not available
for assert or group coverage. The full hierarchy is generated in the hierarchy.html file.

-map_merge_union
Enables map-merge for assertion coverage when used in conjunction with either -map or
-mapfile option. Under the -map_merge_union option, the merging semantics used while
map-merging is same as the default mode merge, that is, it accumulates all the assertions
of the module/instance being mapped from all the vdbs. Without this option, the assertions
that are present in the input vdbs, but not present in the base vdb, are ignored.
-flex_merge code_union_strict
This option is similar to code_union, but applies stricter rules regarding source code
consistency. The -flex_merge code_union_strict switch in URG enables a flow where
code coverage from both the base and input VDBs are combined for a module, provided
the source code itself has not changed.
The usage model for code_union_strict is the same as for code_union. To perform a
strict union merge, use the following command:
urg -dir merged1.vdb merged2.vdb -format both -flex_merge
code_union_strict
Merge Rules
• Modules whose source code has not changed can be union merged, where any
differences are due to ifdefs and generates, not due to source edits.
• If the coverage shape for a module has no differences, it is merged using the default
merging rules. But if the shape is different and the source file has changed, it is not
merged.
• Any instance that exists only in the input VDB is not added to the union design if the
module’s source information does not match with the base VDB.
Warning for Source Mismatch
When modules with edited or different source files are merged using the -flex_merge
code_union_strict option, URG issues the following warning:
Warning-[UCAPI-MSRCCHG] Source File Mismatch
Attempting strict union-merge data from 'input.vdb', but the
vdb was not created by simv binaries compiled using the same
version of the source code with other vdbs, as is required for
code_union_strict merging. The file '/remote/vgrnd24/rajuk/
WORK/UCAPI/P80000979-192837_code_union/test3.sv'
which defines 'top.b1'(module 'bot') has different contents or a
different time stamp in 'input.vdb' than it does in other vdbs.
The instance's data in this vdb will be merged with the default
merge rule. To use code_union_strict merge all data must be
created from the same version of the source files.

code_union: Merges/accumulates coverage data for all regions, including those with
changed/edited source code, even if there are shape differences.
code_union_strict: Does not union module/instance data for regions with changed/
edited source code that result in shape differences. Instead, it merges such data using the
default merge rule.
vcs -sverilog test1.sv -cm line+tgl -cm_dir dir1.vdb -R -full64
vcs -sverilog test2.sv -cm line+tgl -cm_dir dir2.vdb -R -full64

urg -dir dir1.vdb -dir dir2.vdb -flex_merge code_union -lca -report
rep_code_union

Reports assertion coverage without loading the design information. This is to improve
performance and memory cost, for example, for sparsely used assertions inside a big
design, you needn’t load the whole design information. When this option is given, urg only

for the instances with no assertions. An instance is taken as a top-level instance if its
parent has no assertion.

Displays the condition IDs in the condition coverage detail report. See the section
Displaying Condition IDs for more information.
-db_max_tests <number | all>
Specifies the maximum number of covering tests to be stored in the database for each
object. The maximum number of tests stored determines how many covering tests can be
shown for each object when you generate a report from the merged vdb, and affects the
accuracy of test grading done on the merged vdb.
The -db_max_tests option accepts the keyword "all" as a value. When you specify
-db_max_tests all , URG collects test correlation information for all available tests,
regardless of the number of actual tests present in the coverage database. This eliminates
the need to estimate or specify a large number to ensure all tests are captured.
Using all when there are a large number of tests can significantly increase
URG memory use and the disk space required for the resulting merged VDB.
-diff
Compares two databases and generates a difference report. Only supported for assertion
and testbench coverage. For more details on the -diff option, see "Difference Reports
for Functional Coverage" in Chapter 10, "Viewing and Analyzing Coverage Reports Using
Unified Report Generator" of the Coverage Technology User Guide.
-echo
Generates Echo bias file based on the holes in the given coverage database. The
suboptions are:
help — shows this description.
gen_bias N — splits uncovered holes into N bias files (a positive integer must be given to
enable Echo).
max_hole_size N — specifies the maximum number of bins that can be grouped in single
hole (optional - the default is 10).
gen_bias_dir path — generates bias files in the given path (optional - the default path is
echoBiasConfigs/).

Echo is an LCA feature. For more information about Echo, see the LCA category in the
VCS Online Documentation.
-f <file_name>
Specifies multiple directories for source data in a file. You can also specify the -f option
when there are multiple coverage directories.
For example, you can use the following command line options to generate the URG report:
% urg -dir ./simv1.vdb ./simv2.vdb ./simv3.vdb
The size of the command line might exceed the RHEL32 limits while adding more and
more coverage databases to the URG command line. In such cases, the -f option would
suffice the requirement.
% urg -dir ./simv1.vdb -f file_list
Here, file_list (./simv1.vdb ./simv2.vdb ./simv3.vdb) contains the databases. These
coverage databases can be mentioned either with the absolute or the relative path in
file_list. You should at least pass one directory (./simv1.vdb) if you are using the -dir
option.
% urg -f file_list
Here, file_list contains all the databases (./simv1.vdb ./simv2.vdb ./simv3.vdb)
mentioned either with the absolute or the relative path.
You can use the double slash // as a comment and in a directory path. If it is
used as a comment, use the empty space(s) as a separator. For example, in
the code statement below, the first double slash is used as part of the directory
path and the second double slash is used as a comment:
/usr//simv.vdb //comment
The same behavior is applicable for “/*”. If there is no space before /*, it is
considered as part of the directory, otherwise it is considered as a comment.

Does not report FSM sequences.
-fsm disable_loop
Does not report FSM sequences containing loops.

-full64
Runs URG in 64-bit mode. However, URG auto invokes the 64-bit URG binary if the
following conditions are met:
• The -full64 option is not specified in the urg command-line.
• $VCS_HOME includes the 64-bit URG installation.
• At least one of the coverage databases passed to the urg command-line is generated
in the 64-bit VCS mode.
If you do not pass the -full64 option for $VCS_HOME that includes only 64-bit
installation and if at least one of the coverage databases is generated in the 64-bit VCS
mode, 64-bit URG is auto invoked.
If you do not pass the -full64 option for $VCS_HOME that includes only 32-bit
installation and if at least one of the coverage databases is in the 64-bit VCS mode, 32-bit
URG is invoked.

reporting option for urg or for Verdi cov (%verdi -cov -hier hfile1 ).
The urg -hier filename option has the same format as that of the file used at compile

When the -skip_failed_test switch is used during merging, a test that is marked as

The output looks like this:

With the -cm_dir option,

Therefore, the default name of the directory will be simv.vdb.

• wildcard characters can be given in the URG command-line. Some examples of valid
usage are:
urg -dir *.vdb

Using the -tests feature in the URG command line
• The test names which are given in a testList file ( urg -dir abc -tests <testList> ),
should contain abc/test or abc.vdb/test if -cm_dir abc was given in the vcs/
simv command line.
• Old db behavior remains unchanged. Use urg -show availabletests to get list of
valid test names.
With the -dbname option,

line results in an error.

Improving URG and Verdi Load Performance With Optimized
Database Files
The -dbname_opt tglbitarray feature in URG optimizes the internal structure of
certain coverage database files. It significantly reduces the load time for large coverage
databases, especially when complex hierarchy or module tree files are present. It is
possible to achieve a performance improvement of up to five times in some scenarios. By
generating these files in a more efficient format, you can accelerate report generation and
analysis in URG and Verdi, leading to faster coverage review cycles.
Enabling Optimized Database File Generation
Step 1: Run URG with the -dbname_opt tglbitarray Option
To generate a new, optimized coverage database, use the -dbname_opt tglbitarray
switch together with the -dbname option in your URG command. This instructs URG to
write the internal files in a more efficient format.
Example: Optimizing a Single VDB
urg -dir simv.vdb -dbname new.vdb -dbname_opt tglbitarray
Example: Optimizing Multiple VDBs
urg -dir simv1.vdb simv2.vdb simv3.vdb -dbname new.vdb -dbname_opt
tglbitarray
Step 2: Use the Optimized VDB in Verdi or URG
After generating the optimized VDB, use it as you would any other coverage database for
report generation or GUI analysis.
Merging and Mapping
When using the -dbname and -dbname_opt tglbitarray options during merging or
mapping, the generated files correspond to the merged design.
flex_merge tgl
The number of entries in the bitarray should match the flex-merged VDB.
flex_merge code_union/modules
With union merging enabled by -flex_merge code_union or flex_merge modules ,
additional instances might be created because the hierarchy is merged across all relevant
modules. Additionally, -flex_merge code_union also union merge toggle shapes if
applicable, which might result in extra bits due to the union merging of signals.
Mapping

Mapping, or map-merging, merges a hierarchy from the input VDB into a different
hierarchy in the base VDB, even if the top-level names differ. Unreachable data for signals
is also included in the map-merge, and the resulting VDB reflects the hierarchy of the base
VDB along with the mapped unreachable data. The modtreefile option is currently not
supported with mapping.
Redirecting All the Temporary Files Generated By urg -parallel
Option
By default, urg -parallel operation generates the temporary files in the present working
directory.
Temporary_URG_db_{process id}_{hostname}_{timestamp} : temporary db
directoryTemporary_URG_scripts_{process id}_{hostname}_{timestamp}:
script directory For example,

Temporary_URG_scripts_20817_peemt503_Thu_Oct_11_00:15:10_2012
With this enhancement, you can redirect temporary files generated by urg -parallel to a

% urg -parallel -parallel_temproot temprootdiradditional_options
You can use this additional option along with urg -parallel to redirect temporary files

• urg -parallel -parallel_temproot userlocation -lca -format both
It creates a directory with name userlocation in the present working directory and
redirects all the temporary files inside it.
• urg -parallel -parallel_temproot ~/userlocation -lca -format both
It creates a directory with name userlocation in your home directory and redirects all
the temporary files inside it.
• urg -parallel -parallel_temproot ~/mydir1/mydir2/userlocation -lca
-format both
It creates a directory with name userlocation under ~/mydir1/mydir2 located in
your home directory and redirects all the temporary files inside it.

Make sure that ~/mydir1/mydir2 directory hierarchy is already present else
you will see unexpected behavior during the urg -parallel operation in this
case.
1. The special characters, such as #, @, &, _, cannot be used while providing directory
name where all the temporary directories are going to redirect.
2. You cannot provide hierarchies of directories name (while providing directory name
where all temporary directories are going to redirect) which do not exist in that path.

Merge Covergroups Across Scopes
If a module containing a covergroup instance is instantiated multiple times, then
for each elaborated module instances, a covergroup shape is created. The results
are not automatically accumulated into a single shape or score. If you want to know
the overall score for a covergroup definition, you can use the URG option -group
merge_across_scopes.
This technique is useful in cases where you have defined similar covergroups in different
tests, but the program-name is different. So even though two tests may have exactly the
same covergroup (both name and definition), since enclosing program is different they are
not merged.

Merge Covergroups Across Scopes
Using the -group merge_across_scopes option, you can merge across shape and
across the program scope. It allows the reduction of shape creation for groups that are
otherwise the same but at a different scope.
Merge Across-Shape
Suppose there is a covergroup "cg", in a module "M" as follows:
module M;
covergroup cg; endgroup
cg cg1 = new;
Suppose module "M" is instantiated twice in the top-module "top" as follows:
M I1();
M I2();
Then, two covergroup instances are created at runtime, one through "top.I1" and the other
through "top.I2". Two covergroup shapes are created for "cg", with shape-scope as "top.I1"
and "top.I2".
When "across-shape-scope" merging is enabled, the scope-name of these two shapes is
removed, and these two shapes are merged into one.
The prerequisite for this kind of merging is that both these shapes should have the same
bin-space. If bin-spaces of these two shapes are not same, then these two shapes are not
merged (though scope-name would still be removed).
Merge Across-Program-Scope
If two programs or modules have a covergroup with the same name, and same set of
coverpoints/crosses, then they are merged into one covergroup and their shapes are also
merged.
Suppose there is a covergroup "cg", in a module "M" as follows:
module M1;
covergroup cg; endgroup
cg cg1 = new;

module M2;
covergroup cg; endgroup
cg cg2 = new;

Instance Coverage Score Option
In this case, both M1::cg and M2::cg are renamed to unified_prog::cg. If both of them
have the same coverpoints and crosses, then they are merged into one covergroup. In
that case, the shapes corresponding to M1::cg1 and M2::cg2 are also merged if their bin-
spaces are same.
Suppose the covergroup has multiple shapes; say M1::cg has three shapes namely
S1, S2, S3; M2::cg has two shapes namely S4 and S5. Suppose S1 and S5 have the
same bin-space, and S2 and S4 also have the same bin-space. So, after using the
merge_across_scopes option, you have a covergroup unified_prog::cg with three shapes,
S1_5, S2_4 and S3, where S1_5 is a merged copy of S1 and S5, and so on.
For example, consider that a unit level testbench has a covergroup named
"sb_usbspeed_cov" (coverage database is usbvip.vdb):
Group : test_top.TestProgram::Scoreboard::sb_usbspeed_cov
While the system level also has the same covergroup, but different hierarchy (coverage
database is usbvmm.vdb):
Group : test_usb_top.tb::Scoreboard::sb_usbspeed_cov
To merge these two coverage results, use the -group merge_across_scopes URG
command as follows:
urg -dir usbvmm.vdb usbvip.vdb -group merge_across_scopes
The merged result would be:
unified_prog::Scoreboard::sb_usbspeed_cov
Instance Coverage Score Option
By default, URG computes the overall score for a test from the cumulative coverage
score for each of the cover groups in that test. This can be misleading in situations where
you have enabled instance coverage for a particular covergroup. While the cumulative
coverage for a covergroup that is instantiated more than once might be 100%, the
coverage score for individual instances can be well below that. The final overall test score,
which does not take into account the instance coverage, can different from the score for
instance-based coverage.
The urg command -group instcov_for_score option invokes a coverage score
computation that involves the instance coverage:
%urg -group instcov_for_score

Instance Coverage Score Option
With the -group instcov_for_score option, the overall score for a test takes into
account cumulative coverage and instance coverage scores (for covergroups with
instance coverage enabled), to provide a better picture of the coverage results:
Example 48 Sample Code for Cumulative vs. Instance-Only Coverage Score
class ex {
bit a;
covergroup cov {
cumulative = 0;
sample_event = @(posedge CLOCK);
sample a;
}
}
covergroup t_cov {
…
}

covergroup p_cov {
…
}
program test {
ex ex1 = new;
ex ex2 = new;
t_cov cov1 = new;
p_cov cov2 = new;
….
ex1.a = 0;
ex2.a = 1;
@(posedge CLOCK);
…
}
In Example 48, assume that the cumulative coverage for t_cov and p_cov is 40% and
100% respectively. The instance coverage for both instances of ex::cov is 50% but
the cumulative coverage for ex::cov is 100%: Each possible value for the a bit was hit
once in each of the two instances of ex::cov. This means that, individually, ex1 has 50%
coverage on ex:cov and ex2 has 50% coverage on ex:cov. However, the cumulative
coverage of ex:cov is 100% because it has reached both possible values.
The overall (cumulative) score for the test is computed as:
(cumulative_score(t_cov) + cumulative_score(p_cov) + cumulative_score(ex::cov))/3
or
(40 + 100 + 100)/3
By this calculation, the overall score is 80%. This hides the fact that ex1.a was never 1
and ex2.a was never 0.

Covergroup Scores Computation
For a better indication of the overall coverage, use the -group instcov_for_score
option to compute the overall score for ex::cov. For Example 48, the overall cumulative
coverage score for the test, using the instance coverage of each instance of the ex::cov
covergroup, is computed as:
(cumulative_score(t_cov) + cumulative_score(p_cov) + instance_coverage(ex1) +
instance_coverage(ex2) )/4
or
(40 + 50 + 50 + 100)/4
By this calculation, the overall score is 60%. This method assigns equal importance to
each instance of the covergroup ex::cov.

need not specify the -dir option with each directory name, as follows:

specified with text/both argument.

Monitors the execution of procedural statements in a design.

-fsm

-branch

-elfile <file>
Excludes coverable objects specified in <file> for code/assertion/group coverage. For
example:
urg -dir … -elfile filename.el
Elfiles can be created interactively from Verdi, or manually (see -dump
full_exclusions). For more information about elfiles, see Chapter, "Exclusion
Management" in the Coverage Technology User Guide.
-elfilelist <filelist>
Specifies a file containing a list of exclude files to be loaded. For example, a file 'testfile'
with these lines in it:
elfile1.el
elfile2.el

could be passed to URG as follows:
% urg -elfilelist testfile …
Both elfile1.el and elfile2.el would be loaded as if they had been passed to the -elfile
option directly. The exclude files are loaded in the order in which they are specified in the
argument to -elfilelist:
% urg -elfilelist <elfilelist_filename>
• You can specify one elfile name per line.
• You can include comment lines that begin with '#'.
• You can specify an elfile at each line and add comments which can begin with ‘#’.
• You can specify the provided elfile with either a full path name or relative path name.
Environment variable substitutions are not supported.
testfile
------------------------
elfile1.el
elfile2.el
dir1/dir2/file1.el
dir1/dir2/file2.el
/home/dir1/dir3/file3.el # for line coverage exclusion
File4.el # current directory

-excl_append_annotation
Keeps multiple exclusion annotations for same object.
-excl_embed
The -excl_embed option is used with the URG tool to embed exclusions from an exclude
file directly into a coverage database (VDB). When you use this option, URG creates a
new VDB that contains the exclusions specified in the exclude files. After the exclusions
are embedded in the VDB, they are marked as unreachable and cannot be undone.
Annotations added to the exclusions are not preserved.
Embedding exclusions instead of loading them from an exclude file can significantly speed
up the VDB loading time in URG and Verdi.
% urg -full64 -dir input_vdb -dbname output_vdb -excl_embed -elfile
exclude_file
Here,
input_vdb: The original coverage database.

output_vdb: The new coverage database with embedded exclusions.
exclude_file: The file containing the exclusions to embed.
This command does not create the URG report and the .html file.
The coverage database does not include -hier exclusions when you use
excl_embed. Use -excl_embed only with -elfile or -elfilelist. If you do
not specify these options, VCS reports an error.
-excl_bypass_checks
By default, when an exclude file is specified to URG, the checksums stored in the exclude
file are compared to the checksums in the design, and if there are mismatches, the
exclusions are not applied.
If the -excl_bypass_checks option is given, those comparisons are not done, and all the
exclusions are applied.
% urg -elfile <elfilename> -excl_bypass_checks
You must specify the -elfile option with the -excel_bypass_checks option, else an
error is generated.
-excl_strict
Does not allow covered objects to be excluded. '-elfile <file>' must be given when this
option is used.
-dump full_exclusions
Dumps metric specific exclusion files at instance-level and module level. Each metric
specific exclusion file includes the exclusion entries for all the corresponding objects that
can be covered for each instance and module of a design, commented out. The intent is
that you can generate these files and edit them either manually or with a script to create
the required exclusions.

-parallel <machine_file>
Specifies merging the results from multiple tests in parallel. For more information, see the
section "Parallel Merging" in the Coverage Technology User Guide.
-parallel -maxjobs <Number>
Sets the maximum number of jobs that run at the same time. It works in both single and
multi-machine mode, but not in LSF or Grid mode. It also works for both level1 and other
high level jobs.
In the single machine mode, the default value is 10. Only 10 jobs will be running at the
same time in a local machine. In the multi-machine mode, the default value is 1. Each
machine in machine list file runs one URG job.
Following is the algorithm for -maxjobs in multi-machine:
create queue for available machine, such as for 2 machines and '-maxjobs
3' 'machine1, machine2, machine1, machine2, machine1, machine2'.
Remove one from this queue to launch a job and push back the machine name when one
job is finished.
Limitation:
The jobs across levels do not run at the same time. You need to finish all level1 jobs, then
start to launch level2 jobs.
-show tests
Lists all the tests that covered a given object.
When you have multiple test files (intermediate results files) from multiple simulations,
URG merges the coverage results so that if something is covered in one, but not all the
test files, URG reports it as covered.
You can have URG to indicate in the modinfo.txt/mod*.html pages which test covered each
object.

-hvp_disable_wildcards_in_cgshapeparam
This switch disables “*”, “/” and “?” wildcards in an expression of a covergroup shape.
Group : test::cg::SHAPE{(this.arg11_0_cg_init *
this.arg12_0_cg_init)=3,(this.arg13_0_cg_init **
this.arg14_0_cg_init)=1,(this.arg1_0_cg_init **
this.arg2_0_cg_init)=1,(this.arg3_0_cg_init *
this.arg4_0_cg_init)=2,(this.arg5_0_cg_init **
this.arg6_0_cg_init)=1,(this.arg7_0_cg_init *
this.arg8_0_cg_init)=2,(this.arg9_0_cg_init **
this.arg10_0_cg_init)=2}.*
Inside the expression of test::cg::SHAPE none of the “*” are treated as wildcards.
However, the “*” that is provided after the covergroup shape expression is treated as
wildcard.
-hvp_score_missing
Enables unmatched coverage sources to affect plan scores. Unmatched coverage sources
are scored as zero by default.
-hvp_no_score_missing
Disables unmatched coverage sources to affect plan scores. No score for unmatched
coverage source.

text:
The only attributes that appear in the report are those that were specified in the
file, cols. Also, note the order in which the attributes appeared. Earlier, it was
SCORE, LINE, COND, and so on. Now, it is SCORE, COND, LINE, and FSM.
-userdata <file>
Reads HVP data for annotation from the specified 'file'. The -plan option must also be
given.
-userdatafile <file>
Specifies a file containing HVP data file names for annotation. The -plan option must also
be given.
-feature <hvp_feature_name>
Enables you to specify HVP scopes that you want to annotate with a coverage database
or userdata. Its syntax is as follows:
urg -plan <hvp_filename> -feature <hvp_feature_name> -dir
<coverage_database>
or
urg -plan <hvp_filename> -feature <hvp_feature_name> -userdata <file>
urg -plan myplan.hvp -feature Plan.f_block -dir blk.vdb
or
urg -plan myplan.hvp -feature Plan.f_chip -userdata blk.udt
You may specify wildcard in the feature name as follows:
urg -plan myplan.hvp -feature "Plan.*_block" -dir blk.vdb
or
urg -plan myplan.hvp -feature "Plan.*_chip" -userdata blk.udt

title: 1 for coverage on
text:
You may specify multiple -feature options with URG as follows:
urg -plan myplan.hvp -feature Plan.f_block1 -dir blk1.vdb -userdata
blk1.udt -feature Plan.f_block2 -dir blk2.vdb -userdata blk2.udt
The -feature option enables you to specify which coverage databases are annotated
onto which features in the plan. For example, the data in blk1.vdb and blk1.udt is
annotated onto the Plan.f_block1 feature. Similarly, the data in blk2.vdb and blk2.udt
is annotated onto the Plan.f_block2 feature.
Note that if the -feature/-featurefile option is not used, then all the data from all
coverage databases and userdata files are annotated to every feature in the plan. For
details on -featurefile, see -featurefile <hvp_feature_filename>.
-featurefile <hvp_feature_filename>
Enables you to provide a text file that contains feature names. Its syntax is as follows:
urg -plan <hvp_filename> -featurefile <hvp_feature_filename> -dir
<coverage_database>
or
urg -plan <hvp_filename> -featurefile <hvp_feature_filename> -userdata
<file>
urg -plan myplan.hvp -featurefile myfile1 -dir blk.vdb
or
urg -plan myplan.hvp -featurefile myfile2 -userdata blk.udt
Here, myfile1 and myfile2 may have the following content:
cat myfile1
Plan.f_block Plan.f2_block
cat myfile2
Plan.f_chip.funcCov1 Plan.f_chip.funcCov2 Plan.f_chip.bugNum
-group db_edit_file <file>
Specifies the filename for editing the covergroup database.
-group flex_merge_drop
Enables flexible merging for covergroups. For more information, see the section "Flexible
Merging" in the Coverage Technology User Guide.
-group instcov_for_score
Compute scores using coverage of each instance for covergroups with instance coverage
enabled. For more information, see the section Instance Coverage Score Option.

-group maxmissing N
Shows at most N uncovered bins for any coverpoint or cross in group coverage reports.
The default value is 256.
-group merge_across_scopes
Merges the functional coverage data from different coverage databases having same
covergroup but with different hierarchy. For more information, see the section Merge
Across-Shape.
-group ratio
Instructs URG to compute covergroup scores and overall group scores as a simple ratio
of the number of bins covered over the total number of coverable bins. The result is an
average score of its variants and this option is shown in the dashboard.html page.
For more information on -group ratio , see Covergroup Scores Computation.
-group show_bin_values
Displays the value ranges for bins in coverpoints. The option requires that you specified
-covg_dump_range at simulation time.
-group cross_num_print_missing
Specifies the number of missing (not covered) cross product bins that are saved to the
coverage database and printed in the coverage report. The default value of this option is 0.
Its syntax is as follows:
cross_num_print_missing=<number>
-merge_across_libs
Merges modules across different libraries.
Consider a scenario in which the kp_fsm module is present in two different directories, say
base.vdb and input.vdb, of the same library, say LIB. The number of assertions in the
module is different in both the directories, say N1 in base.vdb and N2 in input.vdb. By
default, VCS merges these modules (N1 union N2) and shows LIB.kp_fsm in the merged
report. If the kp_fsm module exists in two different libraries, say BASE and INPUT, VCS
does not merge these modules and their assertions. It shows two independent modules,

urg -metric assert -dir base.vdb -dir input.vdb -merge_across_libs

to remove library names from the exclusion file. To exclude objects with

urg -metric assert -dir simv.vdb -merge_across_libs -dbname

-grade [quick|index|cost|scores|greedy|list][goal R]
[columns][timelimit N] [maxtests N][minincr R][reqtests
file_name][testfile][listonly]
quick
Generates a grading report, displaying cumulative and incremental values of each metric
for each test in the order they are found in the vdbs or in which they are given in a -tests
file (if specified). The quick grading algorithm is linear in the number of tests.
Cumulative value is the coverage score after that test is merged with all previous tests in
the graded list. For each metric, incremental value is the score improvement contributed to
the cumulative value by that test after merging.
index
Produces a report where the tests have been put in best-first order based on usefulness of
the tests. The tests report shows the cumulative, stand-alone, and incremental scores for
each test in the graded list.
Cumulative value is the coverage score after that test is merged with all previous tests in
the graded list. Stand-alone value represents the individual score of that test by itself. For

each test in the graded list.
Cumulative value is the coverage score after that test is merged with all previous tests in
the graded list. Stand-alone value represents the individual score of that test by itself. For
each metric, incremental value is the score improvement contributed to the cumulative
value by that test after merging. The index argument is the default for the -grade option,
except that if index is given explicitly, covergroups are graded in the ratio mode (see the
-group ratio option). If only -grade is given with no suboption, covergroups are graded
using the LRM algorithm.
cost [cputime|simtime|clocktime]

Places tests in best-first order with the goal of minimizing the total cost (cpu time,
simulation cycles, or clock time) instead of minimizing the total number of tests.
scores [total|test|incr]
Shows the tests in default order and gives their stand-alone scores only. The score
grading algorithm is linear in the number of tests.
The simulation time/random seed for testbench coverage in URG is shown with the
-grade scores option only. The -grade scores option gives information for seed/
time and score for each test, and also lists the tests in the best first order, which is not
expensive.
At least one sub-argument must be given with scores, however one or more sub-
arguments can be given if separated by a + character. For example:
-grade scores total+test+incr
where,
total: Reports total accumulated score for the test.
test: Reports the standalone score of a test for each metric.
incr: Reports the incremental contribution of that test to the total.
greedy
Places tests in best-first order with the goal of minimizing the total number of tests, using
an older, slower algorithm. This option will be deprecated in a future release.
goal R
Stops grading when the selected tests' total cumulative coverage score equals or exceeds
R. If not specified, the program grades all specified tests. Applies to index, cost and
greedy algorithms only.
columns [col1+col2+]
Instead of using the default information columns in the grading report, shows the specified
columns along with the score for each test. The supported columns are:
- simtime : Simulation time
- cputime : CPU time
- clocktime : Clock time
- seed : random seed value
indexlimit N

Tracks at most N covering tests for each coverable object when using index or cost
grading. Higher values will produce more accurate results, but utilize more memory.
timelimit N
Specifies the time limit for the report generator to run before exiting. Only those tests that
are graded before the time limit is hit are included in the graded list.
maxtests N
Specifies the maximum number of tests to be selected in the report. Applies to index, cost
and greedy grading only.
minincr
Stops selecting tests when no additional tests can increase the overall score by at least
minincr. Applies to index, cost and greedy grading only. This value is specified as a real
number between 0.00 and 100.00.
reqtests file_name
Use this option with index, cost, or greedy to specify reading a list of test names from
file_name for inclusion in the grading report. Those tests are included at the top of the
graded list, regardless of their scores or effectiveness for coverage.

-mapfile <file_name>
Allows you to specify how coverage data from instance hierarchies in different designs
should be combined when merged.
urg -dir base.vdb -dir input.vdb -mapfile file_name
where, file_name is the mapping configuration file. For more information, see the section
"Mapping Coverage" in the Coverage Technology User Guide.
-map <module_name>
Maps subhierarchy code coverage from one design to another. This option is not available
for assert or group coverage. The full hierarchy is generated in the hierarchy.html file.

-map_merge_union
Enables map-merge for assertion coverage when used in conjunction with either -map or
-mapfile option. Under the -map_merge_union option, the merging semantics used while
map-merging is same as the default mode merge, that is, it accumulates all the assertions
of the module/instance being mapped from all the vdbs. Without this option, the assertions
that are present in the input vdbs, but not present in the base vdb, are ignored.
-flex_merge code_union_strict
This option is similar to code_union, but applies stricter rules regarding source code
consistency. The -flex_merge code_union_strict switch in URG enables a flow where
code coverage from both the base and input VDBs are combined for a module, provided
the source code itself has not changed.
The usage model for code_union_strict is the same as for code_union. To perform a
strict union merge, use the following command:
urg -dir merged1.vdb merged2.vdb -format both -flex_merge
code_union_strict
Merge Rules
• Modules whose source code has not changed can be union merged, where any
differences are due to ifdefs and generates, not due to source edits.
• If the coverage shape for a module has no differences, it is merged using the default
merging rules. But if the shape is different and the source file has changed, it is not
merged.
• Any instance that exists only in the input VDB is not added to the union design if the
module’s source information does not match with the base VDB.

code_union_strict option, URG issues the following warning:

Attempting strict union-merge data from 'input.vdb', but the
vdb was not created by simv binaries compiled using the same
version of the source code with other vdbs, as is required for
code_union_strict merging.

-assert minimal
Reports assertion coverage without loading the design information. This is to improve
performance and memory cost, for example, for sparsely used assertions inside a big
design, you needn’t load the whole design information. When this option is given, urg only
reports modules and instances that have assertions coverage data. This option is not
compatible with vdb directories that contain code coverage data.
With this option, the difference in the hierarchy page is as follows:
• If all instances have assertions, the hierarchy page is the same as usual.
• If some of the instances have assertions, the hierarchy page does not show the nodes
for the instances with no assertions. An instance is taken as a top-level instance if its
parent has no assertion.
For example A.B.C.D.E.F, the ‘A’, ‘B’, ‘C’, and ‘F’ instances have assertion. Their
hierarchy page would look like as follows:
A
|----->B
| |----->C
