VHDL wrapper combined with slave mode
The design contains a VHDL/SystemC interface model created with option -vhdl. This
kind of interface models should not be used in combination with VCS -slave elaboration
Remove the csrc directory and re-create the interface model with option -sysc=opt_if
instead of option -vhdl, then elaborate again.
TBLOG-SYSC-FAILED
Failed to write tblog record
SystemC failed to write a tblog record, because %s.

This warning is printed only once.
TBLOG-SYSC-RELOCATED
Relocated tblog record
SystemC cannot determine the active scope of a tblog object. This might occurred
because the object might be called outside of any SystemC scope and became orphaned
because the parent thread or method has ended. The tblog object is moved into the scope
'%s' to prevent data loss. This warning appears only once.
To debug the cause, use CBug to set a breakpoint in the
sc_snps::cbug_tblog_stop_here function. Set the breakpoint using the UCLI
commands cbug followed by stop -in sc_snps::cbug_tblog_stop_here. The
simulation stops each time the scope cannot be determined.
TLI-12
SV longint and C 'long' size mismatch
At least one argument of method '%s' of class '%s' is of type long.
The created type of the corresponding SV task argument is longint.
TLI-DA-4
Number of imported members exceeds 2000

The call syscan -tli_DA has imported '%s' members, and this increases the compile
time.
Use a tli file with the statement create directaccess and module name and call
syscan with '-tli <tli file name>.
TLI-GEN-MDA
Multi-dimensional arrays not supported
The member variable in line '%s' cannot be converted into a corresponding C member
variable because it is a multi-dimensional array, which is not supported. The member
appears in the generated C struct as a comment.
If you want this member to be packed/unpacked on the C side, manually modify the
generated pack/unpack C++ functions. See the user guide for how to deal with multi-
dimensional arrays.
TLI-INT-WARN
Internal Error in TLI

An internal TLI error occurred: %s.
The simulation continues.
TLI-MULT-USE-TARGETS
Multiple use targets
The targets '%s' have been specified with use clauses in the tli input file '%s'.
Only one use directive in a tli file is supported for verilog adapter code generation.
UCLI-CBUG-DETACH-1
Detach of CBug in pure SystemC mode
CBug is preparing to detach while running in pure SystemC mode. This action is not
recommended. The control is provided back to UCLI by setting a time-based breakpoint
at the next available simulation time. If the current SystemC process does not end or the
simulation does not move forward in time, control may not return to UCLI. Note that using
Control-C or SIGINT to interrupt the simulation may not work in this situation.
Recommendation: Do not detach CBug in pure SystemC mode.

%s is not supported for VHDL-only designs.
%s is not enabled.

One or more persistent C value-change breakpoints are frequently triggering a cycle of

If these cycles are not intentional, then type 'stop', look for 'controlling VCBPs' and disable
the relevant breakpoints. Change the limit to report this message to, for example, 100 with
command set watch::vcbp_silent_oos_limit 100.

top classes (for example. import *) but not from subclasses (for example, import *.*).
This method pattern will be skipped for TLI-adaptor generation.
SC-VCS-DLP-PART
No SystemC instances in partitions

partition for Design Level Parallelism (DLP). This can lead to incorrect simulation results.
Move the SystemC instances outside the partitions into the main partition.
SC-VCS-FILE-SC_MAIN
Turning on show_sc_main by using the -file option

vcs -file contains sc_main.
SC-VCS-FORCEGCC
SystemC library forced for a given SystemC version
Option %s has been used. Simulation will be linked with the SystemC library compiled for
GCC %s, but %s %s will be used to compile the SystemC and C++ code.

SC-VCS-MDIR-CLASH
Mdir library names lead to clash
The Mdir libraries %s and %s lead to the same library name %s. To avoid ambiguities, the
library names are passed with an absolute path name instead of a relative name to the
linker. Consequently, these libraries cannot be moved to another location.
SC-VCS-NO-SYSC
No SystemC models found
No SystemC models found, ignoring the -sysc option.
Check whether there are SystemC models analyzed with syscan and/or interface models
are generate with vlogan -sc_model and/or with vhdlan -sc_model.
SC-VCS-QTHREAD-OVERRUN
Stack of quickthread is maybe too small
The simulation received a fatal segmentation violation signal SEGV and will end because
it accessed protected stack guard memory.
SC-VCS-SVERILOG
Adding SystemVerilog elaboration option

The interface code between SystemC and Verilog is based on DPI. Therefore, the
SystemVerilog option is added to the VCS elaborator.
SC-VDEF-NO-PM
Default portmap file not found
The default portmap file %s cannot be found.
SC-WPROT-CSRC
The csrc directory is write protected

Update the directory by calling command syscan -shared
SC-WPROT-CSRC-O
The csrc directory is write protected
The %s directory is write protected: object files cannot be compiled when needed. This
can lead to link issues.

Update the directory by calling command syscan -shared
SC_TIMERES_SET_DEF
SystemC time resolution set automatically
The SystemC time resolution is set to %s because the time resolution has already been
set on the HDL side.
SYSC-E115-ENV-IGNORE
Ignoring environment variable SYSC_STRICT1666_DKI
Ignoring the environment variable $SYSC_STRICT1666_DKI because the environment
variable $SYSC_STRICT1666 is set.
For observing DKI driver issues, do unsetenv SYSC_STRICT1666 and run again.
SYSC-E115-IGNORE
Ignoring multiple DKI drivers option
The options -sysc=disable_multiple_dki_driver_check and
-sysc=enable_multiple_dki_driver_check are ignored because the environment
variable SYSC_STRICT1666 is set with a value other than 0.

Do unsetenv SYSC_STRICT1666 and rerun again.

Summary for multiple DKI drivers %s.
SYSC-UCLI-MULTI-TOP
Issue with Tracing of individual signals
The tracing of individual signals might be broken for a SystemC-Multi-Top design: the
signal might be invisible or streamed with the wrong contents.
Use tracing of the complete design to overcome this issue.

SETXPIGR
$set_x_xprop() system task used without enabling X-propagation (-xprop) during
The warning SETXPIGR is reported when the design contains a call to the SystemVerilog
system task $set_x_xprop(), but X-propagation support has not been enabled through
the -xprop option during VCS compilation.
In this configuration, the $set_x_xprop() call is ignored because X-propagation
functionality is unavailable. VCS issues the following warning:
Warning-[SETXPIGR] Set_x_xprop call will be ignored
Set_x_xprop call not allowed in this context. Enable xprop as per the
user guide during compilation to enable the set_x_xprop usage
• If the design intentionally uses $set_x_xprop(), compile the design with the -xprop
option enabled.
• If X-propagation is not required, remove or conditionally compile the $set_x_xprop()
call.

Preface
VCS Intelligent Coverage Optimization (VCS ICO) add-on for VCS fits seamlessly in your
regression environment and enables you to improve verification productivity (hitting more
goals per iteration) and efficiency (achieving at lower cost) by generating better stimulus
using Reinforcement Learning.
The preface discusses the following:
• Customer Support
• Synopsys Statement on Inclusivity and Diversity
Customer Support
Customer support is available through SolvNetPlus.
Accessing SolvNetPlus
The SolvNetPlus site includes a knowledge base of technical articles and answers to
frequently asked questions about Synopsys tools. The SolvNetPlus site also gives you
access to a wide range of Synopsys online services including software downloads,
documentation, and technical support.

Getting Started
Constraint Solver (CS) generates input stimuli for a Design Under Test (DUT) at each
stage during simulation by solving a set of user-defined testbench (TB) constraints at the
current state, as shown in the following figure:
Figure 1 Constraint Random Stimuli Quality
The quality of distribution of the generated stimuli is important as it can affect the number
of verification cycles needed to meet coverage goals. The distribution of the stimuli is
skewed by some preferred ordering of variables, which are induced by the constraints
such as solve before , dist, relational and solver’s affinity to certain variable ordering
due to tight time budget. By default, there is no active feedback mechanism to rectify the
skewed distribution.
Intelligent Coverage Optimization (ICO) using Adaptive Input Generator addresses the
limitation of achieving the user intended stimuli distribution by using Reinforcement

Chapter 1: Getting Started

Learning (RL) to maximize diversity, and thereby achieving improved stimuli quality.
Consider the following figure:
Figure 2 Stimuli Generation in ICO
ICO computes the compensated distribution on-the-fly and biases the solver with the
compensated distribution to nullify the skewness in the distribution and to maximize the
diversity in the stimuli distribution, in both intra- and inter-simulation runs. This helps to
reduce the repeated generation of the same stimuli in the regression, and thereby helps in
improved and faster coverage closure. It also helps to expose volume/rare bugs and hard-
to-hit scenarios.
In addition, ICO provides testbench (TB) stimuli visibility, diagnostics, and root cause
analysis capabilities to help you debug TB for potential over-constraints and under-
constraints causing low coverage, skewed distribution, and TB failures.
ICO can be used in all the stages (early, mid, and late stages) of a project. It can also be
used as early as when the coverage model is not defined. It fits seamlessly in the VCS
regression environment. There is no need to change the functional coverage model. It
does not require an additional merge server.

What’s New In This Release
This section describes the new features and improvements in VCS Intelligent Coverage
Optimization (ICO). The following points introduce the new and enhanced features of ICO
and provide pointers to additional information:
• ICO improves error detection by analyzing failure history-including unique signatures,
total failures, and failure rates to accelerate error detection through the following two
mechanisms:
◦ Predictive Bug Hunting: Learns from the past regression runs and applies that
knowledge to stress the observed failure spaces for adjacent failures and to explore
new failure spaces.
◦ Adaptive Bug Hunting: Uses the new bugs mode to automatically adjust bug
modes (such as bug, bug2, and so on) based on a prescribed methodology as
testing progresses and failure rates stabilize.
For more information, refer to Predictive and Adaptive Bug Hunting.
• Starting with this release, ICO can record Important Signal Predictor (ISP) data during
simulation as a compressed binary file named record.isp under the store record
directory. You can then use the crg command to translate this file into a readable form
(for example, CSV) and to generate an ID map that links each recorded value back to
its source location and variable name. The recorded data can be used for downstream
analysis, debug, and machine-learning flows.
For more information, refer to Identifying and Recording Important Signal Predictors
(ISP).
• Starting with this release, ICO can dump failure signatures during simulation when
you run it in bug-finding mode. A failure signature is a normalized form of an error
message in which dynamic content , such as simulation time and data values, has
been removed. As a result, multiple error messages that report the same underlying
problem collapse to a single signature.
For more information, refer to Dumping Failure Signatures.
• Starting with this release, ICO supports functional context aware class naming for
learning. Use +ntb_solver_bias_class_fcxt to enable function or task context in
class instance names and +ntb_solver_bias_class_fcxt_depth to control context

depth. This helps ICO distinguish randomization calls that occur through different call
paths and improves learning precision.
For more information, refer to Functional Context for Class Naming.
• Starting with this release, you can run the bugs strategy without the -l <log_file>
option when you enable an internal log by setting a positive log chunk size. This feature
is enabled using the +ntb_solver_bias_log_chunk_size runtime option.
For more information, refer to Manage Log Files for Bug and Failure Prediction.

Invoking ICO
You can use ICO in regression mode to allow inter-simv learning among the tests for
effective coverage optimization. There is no change in compilation. ICO is enabled with
runtime options only. There are two regression use modes: Non-Shared and Shared
modes. Shared mode is explained in the following section. For Non-Shared mode, refer to
Non-Shared Regression Mode: Manual Merging and Chaining.
Shared Regression Mode: Auto Merging and Chaining
ICO allows race-free shared update of cdb record among concurrently running simulations
(simvs). That is, two or more simv running concurrently can load and update the same
record.
This feature allows learning among concurrently running simvs by loading the latest cdb
generated by a simv run that just finished. Learning helps to reduce the generation of
the same stimuli and hence improve the verification efficiency. Local load/store backups
(shown in Figure 3) help to reproduce the simulation run for debugging. You can generate
the report anytime even while regression is in progress.

Invoking ICO
Figure 3 Shared Update of Coverage by Concurrent Simulation Runs
The following steps describe the usage of this feature:
1. Initialize the shared directory (record) before regression using the following command:
% crg -dir shared_record -shared init
2. Launch the concurrent simv (simulations running concurrently in the background,
updating the shared record) using the following commands:
//for i in 1..100; do #run simv in parallel
$ simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto_config=2 \
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=<shared_record> \
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name=<test_name> \
+ntb_solver_bias_store_record=<store_record> \
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record=<load_record> \
+<run_opts> &
//done
Enables auto configuration. For more information, refer to ICO Auto Configuration.
+ntb_solver_bias_store_record=<>
Specifies local store cdb directory.

Invoking ICO Prognosis
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record=<>
Specifies local backup cdb directory.
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=<>
Specifies global shared cdb directory.
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name=<…>
Specifies test name.
For more details on ICO auto configuration, refer to ICO Auto Configuration and
Reporting Enabled Features of ICO.
3. Take a snapshot of the shared record and generate the report from the shared directory
using the following command:
% crg -dir shared_record -report shared_rpt
When the shared CDB is initialized (in step 1), a readme.txt file is
automatically created. This text file includes details such as the current CDB
version, creation date, and user. It also provides guidance on key operations,
including:
• How to initialize the shared CDB for normal/slow fileserver
• Best practices for reuse
• Procedures for automatically purging stale data
• Steps to generate reports
• Instructions for cloning

Reading the Diagnostic Report
Testbench diagnostic information is stored in a text file
<ntb_solver_bias_store_record>/record.cdb.diag when you specify the
+ntb_solver_bias_diag=<1|2|3> option. The report is generated per test. Figure 10
shows the sample diagnostics report with the +ntb_solver_bias_diag=3 option.

Performing Root Cause Analysis (RCA)
Figure 10 Diagnostic Report
Performing Root Cause Analysis (RCA)
The potential uncoverable bins are marked as ILLEGAL yet to be covered bins are marked
as UNCOVERED in the Detail report as shown in Figure 11. The bins can be uncoverable
due to over constraints. Over constraints prevents the generation of certain scenarios and
hides potential design bugs.

Performing Root Cause Analysis (RCA)
Figure 11 Detail Report
ICO supports Root Cause Analysis (RCA) of the uncoverable/illegal bins generated during
runtime. This feature reports the constraints responsible for the uncoverable bins, which
can be useful to improve the TB. Also, this feature allows you to go deep into the bin-level
information of particular variable and explore why the bin is illegal.
You can add the runtime option +ntb_solver_bias_rca_config=1 during simv to enable
the root cause analysis feature. Following is the syntax:
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record=<record>
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_config=<0|1>
Where, 0 indicates disable, and 1+ indicates enable. For example,
+ntb_solver_bias_store_record=store_record +ntb_solver_bias_rca_config=1
After the run, use the crg utility on the <record> directory as follows to generate the
reports:
% crg -dir simv.cst/stimuliDB/store_record -report crgReport

from a variable to the Coverage Category window. You can click ILLEGAL hyperlink to
identify the root cause constraints shown in the pop-up window. This window shows the
potential over constraint possibilities. It takes you to one of the constraints that could be a
potential reason why the bin is illegal.

Mode Description

Option to Load Records
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record=<path>
If used in shared mode, path specifies the cdb database to be stored as a backup load
from the shared record. If this option is not specified, the database is stored in simv.cst/
stimuliDb/load_record.
Backup load is required to debug simv failures.
If used for replaying simulation failures of the runs in shared mode, the
path should be pointing to the same cdb database that is specified with the
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record option during the shared mode.
If not used in shared mode, then the path specifies the cdb database to be loaded from
a previous run for chaining. If this option is not specified, then there is no chaining.
If used for replaying simulation failures of the runs in non-shared mode,
the path should be pointing to the same cdb database that is specified with the
+ntb_solver_bias_load_record option during non-shared mode.

+ntb_solver_bias_rca_internal=<0|1>

0: No internal constraints (default).

For more information on these options, refer to RCA Due to Internal Constraints.

+ntb_solver_bias_rca_internal=1
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_cpu_limit=300
This option improves RCA usability. You can use this option to override any specific RCA
option if required.
For more information on these options, refer to Shortcut to RCA Configuration.

+ntb_solver_bias_rca_focus=nt+to

+ntb_solver_bias_enable_opt
+ntb_solver_bias_enable_opt=103
Enables prognosis-aware autobias mode selection.
+ntb_solver_bias_enable_opt=20
Enables a new constraint density metric for prognosis analysis.
For more information, refer to Generating Prognosis Report for Prognosis-Aware Autobias.
Options for Smart Error Detection
+ntb_solver_bias_enable_opt=105
Enables conditional bug finding, that is, automatically switches to bug finding mode when
all coverage monitors are disabled.

Options for Predictive and Adaptive Bug Hunting
+ntb_solver_bias_enable_opt=106
Enables bug finding, that is, force bug finding mode irrespective of whether coverage
monitors are disabled or not.
For more information, refer to Smart Error Detection.
Options for Predictive and Adaptive Bug Hunting
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_strategy=bugs
The strategy bugs can be both adaptive and predictive. This option adapts the bug modes
(such as bug, bug2, and so on) automatically based on the learning from the past history
of failure occurrences. It also applies the learning to predict new failures.
+ntb_solver_bias_fail_regex=<regex>
Specifies the regular expressions (regex) for identifying failure messages. By default, it
looks for various failure patterns, including common ones such as UVM_ERROR, offending,
and ASSERT FAILED .
+ntb_solver_bias_fail_regex_file=<regex_file>
Specifies a list of regexes, with one entry per line in an external file. If you specify
this option along with +ntb_solver_bias_fail_regex, the regex scope of
+ntb_solver_bias_fail_regex is expanded to include the expressions specified within
the file.
0: Disables predictive search (default).
1-100: Percentage of intensity of predictive search. This is applicable only when predictive
search is enabled.
101: Auto (any number > 100 is auto).
For more information, refer to Predictive and Adaptive Bug Hunting.
+ntb_solver_bias_log_chunk_size=<size>
Run the simulation without the -l and -a options. For more information, refer to Manage
Log Files for Bug and Failure Prediction.
Option to Enable New Autobias Setting
+ntb_solver_bias_enable_opt=201

Option to Enable Auto Clean at Runtime
Enables the corresponding optVal=201. This option enables new autobias setting when
used with the +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto_config=<1|2> option.
For more information, refer to Improving Coverage and Diversity in Autobias.
Option to Enable Auto Clean at Runtime
+ntb_solver_bias_clean=<cleanupLevel>
Reduces the disk footprint by removing the local records from the run directory.
Cleanup level cleanupLevel: 0 to 3 (default: 0).
0: No cleanup.
1: Remove local store coverage database.
2: Remove local store and local load coverage databases.
3: Enables 2 and removes local store cdb failed to be merged.
For more information, refer to Auto Clean at Runtime.
Option to Improve Coverage Tracking and Diversity With
Additional Singleton Bins
+ntb_solver_bias_enable_opt=16,17,18
16: Enables coverage tracking of additional singleton bins from 32 to 1023 (for unsigned)
and -512 to 511 (for signed).
17: Enables diversification of the bins using greedy approach.
18: Enables diversification of the bins using Reinforcement Learning (RL) approach.
For more information, refer to Improving Coverage Tracking and Diversity With Additional
Singleton Bins.

+ntb_solver_bias_enable_opt=19
Enables coverage tracking of additional singleton bins for values in the range [-231,
231-1] which appear in the interval ranges specified in the constraints.
+ntb_solver_bias_interval_size_limit
+ntb_solver_bias_interval_size_limit=<interval_size_limit>

Options for Improved Debugging of ICO Exposed Failures
Allows you to limit the size of intervals for +ntb_solver_bias_enable_opt=19. Any
interval specified with a size greater than the limit is not considered for singletons. The
maximum value of <interval_size_limit> is 65000 and the default value is 1024.
For more information, refer to Tracking and Diversifying Higher Values as Singleton Bins.

+ntb_solver_bias_debug_info
+ntb_solver_bias_debug_info=<0|1|2>
0: No debug information is reported
1: Prints the following trace information in the simulation log file:
Randomize serial, location, and vcs time.
2: Prints the following trace information in the simulation log file:
Randomize serial, location, vcs time, stimulus Variable name and values.+ntb_solver_bias_debug_filer

Prints the trace information bounded between randomize serial numbers L (low) and H
(high) values. Logging occurs between randomize serials L and H.
For more information, refer to Improved Debugging of ICO Exposed Failures.

+ntb_solver_bias_focus_file=<focusFile>
Restricts biasing of variables to those specified in the focusFile.
+ntb_solver_bias_focusX_file=<focusXFile>
Excludes variables from biasing to those specified in the focusXFile.
+ntb_solver_bias_focus_filter=L:H,L1:H1,L2:H2
Restricts biasing for the randomization with serial in the intervals L:H,L1:H1,L2:H2.
For more information, refer to Focused Biasing Control Support.
Option for Controlling the Shared CDB Update
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_update=<0|1>
Allows you to update the shared CDB conditionally based on the simulation result.

Option for Controlling Merging of Class Instances in Repeat Randomization
0: Shared CDB is not updated at the end of the simulation.
1: Shared CDB is updated at the end of the simulation (default behavior).
For more information, refer to Controlling the Shared CDB Update.
Option for Controlling Merging of Class Instances in Repeat
Randomization
+ntb_solver_bias_inst_merge=<0|1>
Allows you to enable or disable the merging of class instances in repeat randomization.
0: Disables the merging of class instances in repeat randomization.
1: Enables the merging of class instances in repeat randomization (default behavior).
For more information, refer to Controlling Merging of Class Instances in Repeat
Randomization.
Options to Include Functional Context in Class Naming
+ntb_solver_bias_class_fcxt=<fcxt_enable>
Controls which types of randomization calls include functional context in the class instance
name. Specify one of the following values:
• 0 — Disables functional context. This is the default.
• 1 — Enables functional context for std::randomize only.
• 2 — Enables functional context for non-std::randomize only.
• 3 — Enables functional context for both std::randomize and non-std::randomize.
+ntb_solver_bias_class_fcxt_depth=<0:31>
Controls how many levels of the call path ICO captures. Specify a value between 0 and
31:
• 0 — Disables context collection. This is the default when functional context is not
enabled.
• 1 — Captures one level of context. This is the default when functional context is
enabled.
• 2 to 31 — Captures deeper call paths up to the specified level.
For more information, refer to Functional Context for Class Naming.

chapter: 3 Records variables that are randomized only once across all time.
title: 3 Records variables that are randomized only once across all time.
text:
+ntb_solver_bias_isp_file=<include_file>
Specifies a file that lists the variables to include in ISP recording.
+ntb_solver_bias_ispX_file=<exclude_file>
Specifies a file that lists the variables to exclude from ISP recording.
+ntb_solver_bias_class_info=<0-3>
Controls how much class and module or package information ICO records along with the
ISP data. The following table describes the supported values:
Table 2 Class Info Values
Value Description

chapter: 3 Collects both class and module or package information.
title: 3 Collects both class and module or package information.
text:
For more information, refer to Identifying and Recording Important Signal Predictors (ISP).
Options for Dumping Failure Signatures
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_strategy=<bugs>

Options for Dumping Failure Signatures
Selects the ICO biasing strategy for the run. Use the bugs value to enable the bug-finding
strategy that triggers failure signature dumping.
Enables failure prediction. Specify a non-zero value to trigger failure signature dumping
independently of the strategy mode.
For more information, refer to Dumping Failure Signatures.

CRG Options
ICO produces stimuli distribution in a coverage database (cdb)of the TB during the
simulation run using the following command:
+ntb_solver_bias_store_record=<record>
A post simulation utility, crg is used to generate the reports from a cdb generated from
simv run. The crg utility can also be used to manage both shared and non-shared cdb
databases.
% crg -dir <dir> [-f <filelist>][-report report_dir][-format <text|
html|both>][-text <flat|hier|summary|brief>][-merge merge_dir]
[-elfile <elFile>][-purge <pFile>][-purgeX <xFile>][-purge_key <uvm
+rca+sbin>][-purgeX_key <uvm+rca+sbin>][-sbin_merge <add+reuse+modify>]
[-part_select][-work <wdir>][-wdiv][-shared <init|init_sfs|check|
snap|update|save|restore>][-reset_tag <biased|scope>][-purge_untag
<biased|scope>][-auto_purge][-exclude <uncovered|illegal>][-isp_in
<path_to_record.isp>][-isp_out <output_file>] [-isp_format <bin|csv>]
[-diff][-show <tests|records>][-zip <level>][-base_merge <level>][-incr]
[-prognosis][-stat][-illegal_attr][-illegal_group][-rca_effort_attr]
[-check_db][-q, -quiet][-l, -log <logfile>][-v, -version][-sdb <dir>]
[-shared_save_period <sec>]
-auto_purge
Purges the stale information from the given CDBs, saves it in <shared_cdb_new> (when
specified with the -merge option), and initializes it for sharing.
For more information, refer to Reusing Shared CDB Across Changing Models.
-base_merge <level>
Specifies the base class merge <level>. It should be 1 or more. For more information,
refer to Base Class Merging Based on User-Defined Level.
-check_db

Checks each input cdb and output cdb (if specified). Prints check db output in <wdir>/
check_db.txt. For more information, refer to Integrity Check of CDB.
-dir <record_dir>
Specifies the directory to record data. You can specify this option multiple times.
-diff
Displays and highlights the delta difference between two coverage databases in the
coverage report. For more information, refer to Delta Difference Between Two CDBs.
-elfile <elFile>
Exclude all the bins specified in the file. For example, you can use the text report file
bininst_status.csv to keep the lines you want to exclude. For more information, refer to
Excluding Uncoverable Bins From Reports.
-exclude <uncovered|illegal>
Specifies bin coverage type to exclude. Default is uncovered. You can specify multiple
-exclude options. This option is applicable only on bins specified with -elfile. The
-exclude illegal option excludes illegal bins only.
-format <text|html|both>
Specifies the report format. If html is specified (default), this option generates the report
files including index.html, dashboard.html, tests.html, and detail.html.
If text is specified, this option generates the following files:
bininst_status.csv, binclass_status.csv, varinst_status.csv,
varclass_status.csv, inst_status.csv, class_status.csv, total_status.csv
If both is specified, both html and text are generated in the same report directory. For
more information, refer to CSV Text Reports.
-f <filelist>
Specifies the file with source directory (one per line).
For more information, refer to Using File List for Coverage Merging and Report
Generation.
-isp_in <file>
Specifies the path to the ISP file to translate.
-isp_out <file>
Specifies the output file path. If you omit this option, crg writes the output to standard
output.

-isp_format <bin|csv>
Specifies the output format. The default format is bin.
For more information, refer to Identifying and Recording Important Signal Predictors (ISP).
-illegal_attr
Annotates crg HTML and text report with illegal bin attributes. For more information, refer
to Categorizing and Grouping Illegal Bins.
-illegal_group
Annotates crg HTML and text report with illegal bin group tags. For more information, refer
to Categorizing and Grouping Illegal Bins.
-incr
Specifies to use incremental information for merging, report generation, and get the
difference between two coverage databases. For more information, refer to Incremental
Recording and Merging.
-l,-log <logfile>
Logs the messages in <logfile>.
If there is any issue with writing <logfile> or if the -l or -log option is not specified, then
the -q and -quiet options are ignored and the messages are printed on stderr instead.
Also, further processing stops after printing single error message.
-merge <merge_dir>: [output]
If one or more database directories are specified, this option creates a merged database
in the output directory merge_dir after optional operations such as -purge, -reset_tag,
-purge_untag, and -zip.
-part_select
Includes part-selects of variables in the crg report. For more information, refer to Reporting
Part-Select Variables for Coverage and Diversity Distribution.
-prognosis
Generates the prognosis.csv file in the <reportDir> directory for the records that are
created during the runtime with prognosis feature. For more information, refer to ICO
Prognosis.
-purge <pFile>
All the variables in the file are purged. For example, you can use the text report files
varinst_scope.txt/varclass_scope.txt and keep the lines you want to purge.

For more information, refer to Purging Variables From CDB.
-purgeX <xFile>
Purge variables excluding those specified in the xFile. For more information, refer to
Support for Exclusions in ICO Biasing Scope File and CRG Purge File.
-purge_key uvm+rca+sbin
Purges variables depending on the keys uvm, rca, and sbin. The ‘+’ sign denotes the
disjunction of the keys. For more information, refer to RCA Noise Reduction.
-purgeX_key uvm+rca+sbin
Purges variables excluding those captured with the key uvm, rca, or sbin. The ‘+’ sign
denotes the disjunction of the keys. For more information, refer to RCA Noise Reduction.
-purge_untag <biased|scope>: [Input]
Specifies the tag to purge all the information of untagged biased or scope variables from a
coverage database. For more information refer to Reusing Shared CDB Across Changing
Models.
If both the tags are specified as follows, then the variable information is purged if it is not
tagged by either biased or scope. -purge_untag biased -purge_untag scope
-q,-quiet
Suppress all messages.
-rca_effort_attr
Annotates RCA effort attributes for bins with no RCA information. For more information,
refer to Incremental RCA Support for Auto Bins.
-reset_tag <biased|scope>: [Flag]
Specifies the tag to reset (default: none). If scope, then scope tag of all the variables are
reset. If biased, then biased tag of all the variables are reset. For more information refer to
Reusing Shared CDB Across Changing Models.
During simv runs, if a variable is biased, it is tagged as biased, and is not untagged
until reset_tag is invoked. Similarly, if a variable is tagged as scope, it is not untagged
until reset_tag is invoked. You can use both the tags as follows: -reset_tag biased
-reset_tag scope
-report <report_dir>: [output]

Generates the coverage report in the report_dir directory in either HTML or text format.
The reports are generated with tagged biased and scope variables. The following files are
generated, which contain list of variables that are scope or biased:
varinst_scope.txt, varclass_biased.txt
The varinst_scope.txt file contains a line denoting a variable var for the randomization
object identified by the randomize site file:line and class name as follows:
file:line:class:var
Example: test.sv:10:foo:x
The varclass_biased.txt file contains a line denoting a variable var for the
randomization object identified by a class name as follows:
*:*:class:var
Example: *:*:foo:x
Both varinst_scope.txt and varclass_biased.txt files can be used as scope file
(+ntb_solver_bias_scope_file=scope.txt) in simv run or as pFile in crg -purge
<pFile>.
-show <tests|records>
Shows the names of the tests in the coverage reports. For more information, refer to
Coverage Option.
-stat
Prints cdb statistics in <work_dir>/stat.txt. For more information, refer to Reporting
Recommendation to Purge the Shared CDB or Use New DB.
-sbin_merge add+reuse+modify
Enables merging of the user-defined sample bins (sbins). For more information, refer to
Custom Diversification.
-shared init
Initialize <dir> for shared recording. For more information, refer to Shared Regression
Mode: Auto Merging and Chaining.
-sdb <dir>
Generate compressed csv database in the '<dir>' directory for Verdi. For more
information, refer to the Verdi ICO chapter in the Verdi and Siloti LCA Features Guide.
-shared init_sfs

Initializes shared record <dir> for slow file server (fs). For more information, refer to
Configuring Shared CDB for Congested Network.
-shared check
Checks the health of the shared record <dir>. The report is logged in <wdir>/check.log.
-shared snap
Default option. Takes a snapshot of the shared record (even while concurrent runs are
recording). The snapshot record is stored in <wdir>/snap_XXXXXX and a log file is created
<wdir>/snap_XXXXXX.log.
-shared update
Updates the Shared CDB with a merge of <db1>, <db2>, … . specified with the -dir or -f
options. For more information, refer to Controlling the Shared CDB Update.
-shared save
Enables backup of shared cdb.
-shared restore
Restores from the backup (must exist).
-shared_save_period <sec>
Takes periodic backup every <sec> seconds (default 0) of the shared cdb. If the value is

ICO Auto Configuration
ICO supports shortcut options for auto bias that combines most of the runtime options with
their default values. These options allow you to selectively overwrite the default values,
thereby, enabling you to harness the full value. Also, you to quickly make the changes in
the legacy scripts and easily track optimal configuration.

ICO Auto Biasing
There are multiple bias modes (+ntb_solver_bias_mode) to configure ICO depending
on the choice of constraint solver (+ntb_solver_mode), part selects, bin biasing, inter and
intra learning.
ICO is enhanced to learn and automate bias mode using the Auto Bias feature for
improved usability and ease of usage. You must use the +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto
runtime option to enable this feature.
The +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto option takes a value from 1 to 10 corresponding
to the most conservative biasing to aggressive biasing, respectively. For example,
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto=5 is the most balanced biasing mode allowing equal
proportion of simv runs with various biasing modes such as 16649, 24841, 20745, and
28937. For each bias mode, the solver mode is automatically selected under the hood.
You can also track the test name for each bias using the +ntb_solver_bias_test_name
runtime option. Auto biasing can exploit the test names such that proportion is
applied to the reseeded run set of each unique test separately. To enable this,
you can use the +ntb_solver_bias_test_name=<uniqTestName>_<Id> or
-cm_test <uniqTestName>_<Id> option. Id can be a random seed (specified using
+ntb_random_seed). If Id is a random seed, then ‘_’ separator is not needed. Preference
is given to +ntb_solver_bias_test_name over the -cm_test option.

Following is the Auto Bias use model:
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto=<auto_bias_mode>
+ntb_enble_fast_solver=0 +ntb_solver_bias_test_name=<uniqTestName>_<Id>
-cm_test <uniqTest><Id>
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto=<auto_bias_mode>
auto_bias_mode: 0 to 10 (default: 0).
0: Disable auto bias

CRG Options
ICO produces stimuli distribution in a coverage database (cdb)of the TB during the
simulation run using the following command:
+ntb_solver_bias_store_record=<record>
A post simulation utility, crg is used to generate the reports from a cdb generated from
simv run. The crg utility can also be used to manage both shared and non-shared cdb
databases.
% crg -dir <dir> [-f <filelist>][-report report_dir][-format <text|
html|both>][-text <flat|hier|summary|brief>][-merge merge_dir]
[-elfile <elFile>][-purge <pFile>][-purgeX <xFile>][-purge_key <uvm
+rca+sbin>][-purgeX_key <uvm+rca+sbin>][-sbin_merge <add+reuse+modify>]
[-part_select][-work <wdir>][-wdiv][-shared <init|init_sfs|check|
snap|update|save|restore>][-reset_tag <biased|scope>][-purge_untag
<biased|scope>][-auto_purge][-exclude <uncovered|illegal>][-isp_in
<path_to_record.isp>][-isp_out <output_file>] [-isp_format <bin|csv>]
[-diff][-show <tests|records>][-zip <level>][-base_merge <level>][-incr]
[-prognosis][-stat][-illegal_attr][-illegal_group][-rca_effort_attr]
[-check_db][-q, -quiet][-l, -log <logfile>][-v, -version][-sdb <dir>]
[-shared_save_period <sec>]
-auto_purge
Purges the stale information from the given CDBs, saves it in <shared_cdb_new> (when
specified with the -merge option), and initializes it for sharing.
For more information, refer to Reusing Shared CDB Across Changing Models.
-base_merge <level>
Specifies the base class merge <level>. It should be 1 or more. For more information,
refer to Base Class Merging Based on User-Defined Level.
-check_db

Checks each input cdb and output cdb (if specified). Prints check db output in <wdir>/
check_db.txt. For more information, refer to Integrity Check of CDB.
-dir <record_dir>
Specifies the directory to record data. You can specify this option multiple times.
-diff
Displays and highlights the delta difference between two coverage databases in the
coverage report. For more information, refer to Delta Difference Between Two CDBs.
-elfile <elFile>
Exclude all the bins specified in the file. For example, you can use the text report file
bininst_status.csv to keep the lines you want to exclude. For more information, refer to
Excluding Uncoverable Bins From Reports.
-exclude <uncovered|illegal>
Specifies bin coverage type to exclude. Default is uncovered. You can specify multiple
-exclude options. This option is applicable only on bins specified with -elfile. The
-exclude illegal option excludes illegal bins only.
-format <text|html|both>
Specifies the report format. If html is specified (default), this option generates the report
files including index.html, dashboard.html, tests.html, and detail.html.
If text is specified, this option generates the following files:
bininst_status.csv, binclass_status.csv, varinst_status.csv,
varclass_status.csv, inst_status.csv, class_status.csv, total_status.csv
If both is specified, both html and text are generated in the same report directory. For
more information, refer to CSV Text Reports.
-f <filelist>
Specifies the file with source directory (one per line).
For more information, refer to Using File List for Coverage Merging and Report
Generation.
-isp_in <file>
Specifies the path to the ISP file to translate.
-isp_out <file>
Specifies the output file path. If you omit this option, crg writes the output to standard
output.

-isp_format <bin|csv>
Specifies the output format. The default format is bin.
For more information, refer to Identifying and Recording Important Signal Predictors (ISP).
-illegal_attr
Annotates crg HTML and text report with illegal bin attributes. For more information, refer
to Categorizing and Grouping Illegal Bins.
-illegal_group
Annotates crg HTML and text report with illegal bin group tags. For more information, refer
to Categorizing and Grouping Illegal Bins.
-incr
Specifies to use incremental information for merging, report generation, and get the
difference between two coverage databases. For more information, refer to Incremental
Recording and Merging.
-l,-log <logfile>
Logs the messages in <logfile>.
If there is any issue with writing <logfile> or if the -l or -log option is not specified, then
the -q and -quiet options are ignored and the messages are printed on stderr instead.
Also, further processing stops after printing single error message.
-merge <merge_dir>: [output]
If one or more database directories are specified, this option creates a merged database
in the output directory merge_dir after optional operations such as -purge, -reset_tag,
-purge_untag, and -zip.
-part_select
Includes part-selects of variables in the crg report. For more information, refer to Reporting
Part-Select Variables for Coverage and Diversity Distribution.
-prognosis
Generates the prognosis.csv file in the <reportDir> directory for the records that are
created during the runtime with prognosis feature. For more information, refer to ICO
Prognosis.
-purge <pFile>
All the variables in the file are purged. For example, you can use the text report files
varinst_scope.txt/varclass_scope.txt and keep the lines you want to purge.

For more information, refer to Purging Variables From CDB.
-purgeX <xFile>
Purge variables excluding those specified in the xFile. For more information, refer to
Support for Exclusions in ICO Biasing Scope File and CRG Purge File.
-purge_key uvm+rca+sbin
Purges variables depending on the keys uvm, rca, and sbin. The ‘+’ sign denotes the
disjunction of the keys.

Figure 13 Viewing Names of the Tests in the Coverage Reports
ICO Auto Biasing
There are multiple bias modes (+ntb_solver_bias_mode) to configure ICO depending
on the choice of constraint solver (+ntb_solver_mode), part selects, bin biasing, inter and
intra learning.
ICO is enhanced to learn and automate bias mode using the Auto Bias feature for
improved usability and ease of usage. You must use the +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto
runtime option to enable this feature.
The +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto option takes a value from 1 to 10 corresponding
to the most conservative biasing to aggressive biasing, respectively. For example,
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto=5 is the most balanced biasing mode allowing equal
proportion of simv runs with various biasing modes such as 16649, 24841, 20745, and
28937. For each bias mode, the solver mode is automatically selected under the hood.
You can also track the test name for each bias using the +ntb_solver_bias_test_name
runtime option. Auto biasing can exploit the test names such that proportion is
applied to the reseeded run set of each unique test separately. To enable this,
you can use the +ntb_solver_bias_test_name=<uniqTestName>_<Id> or
-cm_test <uniqTestName>_<Id> option. Id can be a random seed (specified using
+ntb_random_seed). If Id is a random seed, then ‘_’ separator is not needed. Preference
is given to +ntb_solver_bias_test_name over the -cm_test option.

Following is the Auto Bias use model:
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto=<auto_bias_mode>
+ntb_enble_fast_solver=0 +ntb_solver_bias_test_name=<uniqTestName>_<Id>
-cm_test <uniqTest><Id>
+ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto=<auto_bias_mode>
auto_bias_mode: 0 to 10 (default: 0).
0: Disable auto bias

title: 5 to 9: Balanced auto biasing
text:
10: Aggressive auto biasing
Key Points to Note
• If auto bias is enabled, the +ntb_solver_bias_mode option is ignored if specified.
• The following options are not needed and are internally set by the auto bias feature:
+ntb_solver_mode
However, if they are specified, then the values of these options are honored overriding
the internal value set by the auto bias feature.
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name=<uniqTestName>_<Id>
Tracks the test name in the coverage reports. Id can be a random seed (specified
using +ntb_random_seed). If Id is a random seed, then ‘_’ separator is not needed.
Preference is given to +ntb_solver_bias_test_name over -cm_test.
Support for Changing Bias Mode During Simulation
ICO allows you to change the bias modes intra-simv, that is, across
randomization within a single simv run. This feature is enabled using the
+ntb_solver_bias_auto_intra_enable=1 simulation option. This feature improves the
diversity of the bias modes and stimuli coverage.
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto=<autoBias>
+ntb_solver_bias_auto_intra_enable=<0|1>

+ntb_solver_bias_auto_intra_enable=<0|1>
0: Default value. Disables auto bias for intra simv
1: Enables auto bias for intra simv
Example 1 test.sv
class myClass;
rand bit[4:0] x,y,z,w;
constraint c {
x<y && y<z && z<w;
w dist {[0:9] := 10,
[10:19] := 4,
[20:31] := 1};
}

myClass t=new;
repeat (1000) begin
t.randomize();
end
end
Run with Auto Bias Mode:
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto=5 +ntb_enable_fast_solver=0
Following is the output:
Figure 14 Run with Auto Bias Mode

Run with Auto Bias Mode with Intra-Simv:
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto=5 +ntb_enable_fast_solver=0
+ntb_solver_bias_auto_intra_enable=1
Following is the output:
Figure 15 Run with Auto Bias Mode with Intra-Simv
Extracting Test Names Using Filters Based on Regular
Expressions
ICO uses test names to identify tests that belong to the same template test. The biasing
engine uses this inference to determine the optimal auto-biasing parameters. If the
correct template test is not inferred, the setting is sub-optimal, and desired outcome is not
observed.
You can use the runtime options +ntb_solver_bias_test_name and
+ntb_solver_bias_test_type to specify test names. However, ICO does not infer the
UVM template test name in the following cases:
• The suffix of the template test name does not match the random seed.
Example: +ntb_solver_bias_test_type=uvm +UVM_TESTNAME=mytest_ 1234
+ntb_random_seed=300
• Only suffix check is supported even when the prefix of the template test name matches
the random seed.
Example: +ntb_solver_bias_test_type=uvm +UVM_TESTNAME=300_mytest
+ntb_random_seed=300
• Using the hash value of random seed as a suffix.

Example: +ntb_solver_bias_test_type=cm_name -cm_name mytest-<hashValue
of random seed> +ntb_random_seed=300
• Updating the test name of the +ntb_solver_bias_test_name runtime option in the
script due to legacy reasons.
To overcome the above mentioned limitations, ICO allows you to specify filters
based on regular expressions to include/exclude part of test names using the
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name_filter=<regex> runtime option.
+ntb_solver_bias_test_type=<uvm|ovm|cm_test|cm_name>
+UVM_TESTNAME=<uvm>
+OVM_TESTNAME=<ovm>
-cm_test <cm_test>
-cm_name <cm_name>
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name_filter=<regex>
You can specify the test type to override the default order by using
+ntb_solver_bias_test_type with one of the cm_name|cm_test|ovm|uvm strings.
• Only POSIX regular expressions are supported.
• The test name filter is applicable for both auto and prognosis runs.
Examples
Example-1:
+ntb_solver_bias_test_type=cm_name -cm_name test-a1234
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name_filter="[[:alpha:]]+" +ntb_random_seed=12
+ntb_solver_bias_store_record=./record
% crg -dir record -json -WORK; grep tnames WORK/record.cdb.json

"tnames":["test_12"]
"utnames":["test_"]
Example-2:
+ntb_solver_bias_test_type=cm_name -cm_name testB1234
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name_filter="([[:alpha:]]+)B" +ntb_random_seed=13
+ntb_solver_bias_store_record=./record

% crg -dir record -json -WORK; grep tnames WORK/record.cdb.json

"tnames":["test_13"]
"utnames":["test_"]
Example-3:
+ntb_solver_bias_test_type=uvm +UVM_TESTNAME="test_1234_xyz_1245"
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name_filter="([[:alpha:]]+)_[0-9]+_([[:alpha:]]+
)_" +ntb_random_seed=14 +ntb_solver_bias_store_record=./record

% crg -dir record -json -WORK; grep tnames WORK/record.cdb.json

"tnames":["test_xyz_13"]
"utnames":["test_xyz_"]
When there are two captures with ‘(..)’, they are combined with ‘_’ .
Example-4:
+ntb_solver_bias_test_type=uvm +UVM_TESTNAME="test_1234_xyz_1245"
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name_filter="(([[:alpha:]]+))_[0-9]+_([[:alpha:]]+
)_" +ntb_random_seed=14 +ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=./record

% crg -dir record -json -WORK; grep tnames WORK/record.cdb.json

"tnames":["test_test_xyz_13"]
"utnames":["test_test_xyz_"]
When there is nested capture ‘(..)’ each capture is combined with ‘_’.
Example-5:
+ntb_solver_bias_test_type=uvm +UVM_TESTNAME="test_1234_xyz_1245"
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name_filter="(([[:alpha:]]+))_[0:9]+_([[:alpha:]]+
)_" +ntb_random_seed=14 +ntb_solver_bias_store_record=./record
The following warning message is issued:
Warning-[CNST-TNFNM] Testname filter match not found
Testname filter '(([[:alpha:]]+))_[0:9]+_([[:alpha:]]+)_' has no match in
'test_1234_xyz_1245'.
Continuing without it.

Example-6:
+ntb_solver_bias_test_type=uvm +UVM_TESTNAME="test_1234_xyz_1245"
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name_filter=".*[_" +ntb_random_seed=14
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=./record
The following warning message is issued:
Warning-[CNST-TNFNR] Testname filter not well-formed
Testname filter '.*[_' is not a well-formed regular expression.
Continuing without it.
Biasing of the Part-Select Variables
Constraints on part-select of variables is not supported by default. Consider the following
example with the constraints on part-selects on variable x (highlighted in the following
example):
Example 2 Testcase
rand bit signed [10:0] x;

covergroup cg;
cp1: coverpoint x[2:0] {
bins low = {[5:7]};
}
cp2: coverpoint x[10:1] {
bins low = {[10:32]};
bins med = {[33:64]};
bins high = {[65:$]};
}
constraint cons {
x[2:0] >= 4;
x[10:3] >= 10;
}
function new;
cg = new;
endfunction
endclass initial begin
obj.cg.sample;
end
end

The diagnostic file record.cdb.diag shows that the variable x is not biased (highlighted)
as follows:
@SECTION 1: Per variable info

File:Line:Class:VarName, #expected, #covered, #uncovered, #illegal,
#randomized, #biased
test4.sv:25:cls:x, 44, 5, 39, 0, 10, 0
ICO supports biasing of the part-select variables. This feature helps to improve the overall
URG score.
To enable the part-select biasing, you must add +16384 to the

Extracting Test Names Using Filters Based on Regular
Expressions
ICO uses test names to identify tests that belong to the same template test. The biasing
engine uses this inference to determine the optimal auto-biasing parameters. If the
correct template test is not inferred, the setting is sub-optimal, and desired outcome is not
observed.
You can use the runtime options +ntb_solver_bias_test_name and
+ntb_solver_bias_test_type to specify test names. However, ICO does not infer the
UVM template test name in the following cases:
• The suffix of the template test name does not match the random seed.
Example: +ntb_solver_bias_test_type=uvm +UVM_TESTNAME=mytest_ 1234
+ntb_random_seed=300
• Only suffix check is supported even when the prefix of the template test name matches
the random seed.
Example: +ntb_solver_bias_test_type=uvm +UVM_TESTNAME=300_mytest
+ntb_random_seed=300
• Using the hash value of random seed as a suffix.

title: 5 to 9: Balanced auto biasing
text:
Example: +ntb_solver_bias_test_type=cm_name -cm_name mytest-<hashValue
of random seed> +ntb_random_seed=300
• Updating the test name of the +ntb_solver_bias_test_name runtime option in the
script due to legacy reasons.
To overcome the above mentioned limitations, ICO allows you to specify filters
based on regular expressions to include/exclude part of test names using the
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name_filter=<regex> runtime option.
+ntb_solver_bias_test_type=<uvm|ovm|cm_test|cm_name>
+UVM_TESTNAME=<uvm>
+OVM_TESTNAME=<ovm>
-cm_test <cm_test>
-cm_name <cm_name>
+ntb_solver_bias_test_name_filter=<regex>
You can specify the test type to override the default order by using
+ntb_solver_bias_test_type with one of the cm_name|cm_test|ovm|uvm strings.
• Only POSIX regular expressions are supported.
• The test name filter is applicable for both auto and prognosis runs.

Scoping Random Variables and Constraint Blocks for Biasing
Use the scoping feature to control which random variables and constraint classes ICO
(Intelligent Coverage Optimization) targets for biasing during simulation. Specify your
selection in a scope file using the +ntb_solver_bias_scope_file=<scopeFile> option,
allowing you to focus biasing on specific variables or classes and improve simulation
efficiency and coverage quality. Use wildcards and escaped names in the scope file to
match multiple variables or parameterized classes as needed.
By default, all random variables are targeted by ICO during runtime. You can selectively
choose certain random variables, constraint classes, and class instances to target for
biasing using a scope file. This file is specified as a runtime option during simulation using
the +ntb_solver_bias_scope_file=<scopeFile> option.
The scope file is a text file with one or more lines. You should follow the following format,
that is, four fields separated by ‘:’, representing one or more instances of random variables
to be included, as follows:
<filePath>:<lineNum>:<className>:<varName>
Where, <varName> corresponds to a random variable of the constraint class <className>
whose instance is randomized at source file <filePath> and line <lineNum>, respectively.
Example: test.sv:10:foo:x
This corresponds to the variable instance with name x of the constraint class foo which is
randomized at line 10 of the file test.sv.
Support for Wildcard '*'
There is a limited support with wildcard to include more variables per line. A field can have
a wildcard '*'. It represents all possible names with prefix match to the field upto '*'.

Following are some examples:
• test.sv:*:foo:xyz — Match all variables with name xyz of the randomized class foo
instantiated anywhere in file test.sv.
• *:*:foo:xy* — Match all variables with prefix xy of the randomized class foo
instantiated anywhere.
• *:*:foo:* — Match all variables of the randomized class foo instantiated anywhere.
• *:*:f*:xyz — Match all variables with name xyz of the randomized classes with
prefix f instantiated anywhere.
• test.*:*:f*:x* — Match all variables with prefix ‘x’ of the randomized classes with
prefix f instantiated anywhere in files test.*.
• *:*:f*:* — Match all variables of the randomized classes with prefix ‘f’ instantiated
anywhere.
• *:*:f*:<SP>xy — Match all variables with prefix <SP>xy (<SP> denotes a space) of
the randomized classes with prefix f instantiated anywhere.
If there is more than one ‘*’ in a field, matching is done up to the first ‘*’. Following is an
example:
• *:*:foo*bar*:xyz — Match all variables with name xyz of the randomized classes
with prefix foo instantiated anywhere.
Support for Parameterized Class and Escaped Names
You need special consideration for Parameterized Class and Escaped Names when using
them with or without wildcard ‘*’.
An Escaped Name starts with \ and end with a space (denoted as <SP>).
In general, you need escape names in the scope file for the following cases:
• Parameterized class name with or without ‘*’ [must]
• Escaped class with or without ‘*’ [must]
• Escaped variable with ‘*’ [must]
• Escaped variable with no ‘*’ [optional]

Following are some examples to illustrate various use cases:
• *:*:\my_rand#(1,bit[6:0],10)<SP>:\a#<SP> — match all escaped variables a# in
the parameterized class my_rand#(1,bit[6:0],10) instantiated anywhere.
• *:*:\myrand*<SP>*:\a#<SP>*— match all escaped variables with prefix a# in all the
randomized escaped classes with prefix my_rand* instantiated anywhere.
You can generate a scope file using the crg command:
% crg -dir record0 -report crgReport -format text
The files in crgReport/{varinst_scope.txt, varclass_scope.txt} can be used as
scope files by removing some lines corresponding to the excluded variables.
Functional Context for Class Naming
By default, ICO identifies each class instance by file, line, and class name. This works well
for direct randomization calls. If multiple call sites invoke the same helper function or task,
ICO can merge those calls into a single learning instance. This reduces learning precision.
Functional context for class naming solves this problem by appending the function or task
call path to the class instance name. This lets ICO treat randomization calls from different
call paths as separate learning instances. As a result, ICO can learn more accurately and
improve stimulus diversity.
You enable this feature through two simv runtime options. No compilation change or flow
change is required.
• Use Model
• Guidelines
• Example
• Notes and Limitations
Use this feature when your testbench wraps randomize() or std::randomize() inside
helper functions or tasks and different call paths represent different functional scenarios.
Leave the feature disabled if you want ICO to merge those call paths into the same
learning instance.

Simv Runtime Options

helper functions or tasks and different call paths represent different functional scenarios.
Leave the feature disabled if you want ICO to merge those call paths into the same

Simv Runtime Options
To enable functional context for class naming, add the following runtime options to your
existing ICO simv command:
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_strategy=<ico_strategy> \
+ntb_solver_bias_class_fcxt=<fcxt_enable> \
+ntb_solver_bias_class_fcxt_depth=<0:31>
Where:
+ntb_solver_bias_class_fcxt=<fcxt_enable>
Controls which types of randomization calls include functional context in the class instance
name. Specify one of the following values:
• 0 — Disables functional context. This is the default.
• 1 — Enables functional context for std::randomize only.
• 2 — Enables functional context for non-std::randomize only.
• 3 — Enables functional context for both std::randomize and non-std::randomize.
+ntb_solver_bias_class_fcxt_depth=<0:31>
Controls how many levels of the call path ICO captures. Specify a value between 0 and
31:
• 0 — Disables context collection. This is the default when functional context is not
enabled.
• 1 — Captures one level of context. This is the default when functional context is
enabled.
• 2 to 31 — Captures deeper call paths up to the specified level.
Guidelines
Follow these guidelines when you enable functional context:
• Start with +ntb_solver_bias_class_fcxt=3 and
+ntb_solver_bias_class_fcxt_depth=1 if your testbench uses helper functions or
tasks around randomization calls. This gives you the new behavior with minimal path
depth.
• Increase the depth only when nested helper calls represent distinct learning scenarios
that you want ICO to track separately.
• Keep the depth value small unless you need deeper call-path separation. Smaller
values keep instance names shorter and easier to interpret.

Consider a testbench where a packet object gets randomized through multiple tasks and
functions:
class pkt;
rand bit [7:0] addr;
constraint c_addr { addr < 200; }

task automatic gen_pkt_task(ref pkt p, int max_addr);
p.randomize() with { addr < max_addr;};
endtask

task automatic gen_pkt_task2(ref pkt p, int max_addr);
gen_pkt_task(p, max_addr);
endtask

function automatic gen_pkt_fn (ref pkt p, int min_addr);
p.randomize() with { addr > min_addr;};
gen_pkt_task(p, min_addr);
endfunction

pkt p = new();
int i=80;

gen_pkt_task(p, i);
gen_pkt_task2(p, i);
gen_pkt_fn(p, i);
end
Without functional context, ICO records only two learning instances because it identifies
them by randomization location and class name alone:
test6a.sv:9:pkt
test6a.sv:17:pkt
With functional context enabled, ICO records four distinct instances because it includes
the call path:
test6a.sv:25:gen_pkt_task.pkt:addr
test6a.sv:26:gen_pkt_task2.gen_pkt_task.pkt:addr
test6a.sv:27:gen_pkt_fn.pkt:addr
test6a.sv:27:gen_pkt_fn.gen_pkt_task.pkt:addr
This separation gives ICO more precise learning information and helps it distinguish
scenarios that the default naming scheme would merge.

Notes and Limitations
• If you specify a depth greater than 31, depth is capped at 31.
• If a function name is escaped, full class instance name is escaped.
• In nested function or task hierarchies, an optimized simv can remove inner nesting
levels. Use -debug_access+all to preserve those levels. Runtime behavior can differ
between optimized and debug builds when this feature is enabled.
• This feature changes class-instance naming for learning only. It does not introduce any
other flow change.
Focused Biasing Control Support
This section describes focused biasing control support in VCS ICO, which enables
selective biasing of random variables during constrained randomization. Instead of biasing
all constrained random variables by default, users can specify inclusive or exclusive
variable lists using focus files and restrict biasing to specific randomization intervals using
filter options. This capability provides fine-grained control over the biasing process, useful
for selective randomization testing and delta debugging workflows. The section details the
runtime option syntax, filter specification formats, file combination behaviors, and provides
practical examples.
By default, all random variables with constraints are recorded and biased when the bias
mode is enabled. You can use the following runtime options to bias selective variables for
specific randomizations while recording the rest:+ntb_solver_bias_focus_file
+ntb_solver_bias_focus_file=<focusFile>+ntb_solver_bias_focusX_file
+ntb_solver_bias_focusX_file=<focusXFile>+ntb_solver_bias_focus_filter
+ntb_solver_bias_focus_filter=L:H[,L1:H1,L2:H2]
These options allow you to specify a list of inclusive/exclusive variables for recording and
biasing while ignoring the rest. This feature expands biasing control to focus on selective
randomization and selective variables while still recording as per the scope rules. Also,
this feature can be used for delta debugging.
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_scope_file=<scopeFile>
+ntb_solver_bias_scopeX_file=<scopeXFile>
+ntb_solver_bias_focus_file=<focusFile>

+ntb_solver_bias_focusX_file=<focusXFile>
+ntb_solver_bias_focus_filter=L:H[,L1:H1,L2:H2]
+ntb_solver_bias_focus_file=<focusFile>
Restricts biasing of variables to those specified in the focusFile.
+ntb_solver_bias_focusX_file=<focusXFile>
Excludes variables from biasing to those specified in the focusXFile.
+ntb_solver_bias_focus_filter=L:H,L1:H1,L2:H2
Restricts biasing for the randomization with serial in the intervals L:H,L1:H1,L2:H2.
If both ntb_solver_bias_focus_file and ntb_solver_bias_focusX_file
options are specified, then biasing of variables is the intersection of the
variables specified in the focusFile and those NOT specified in the
focusXFile.

Variables recorded = S ∩ ¬ SX

Root Cause Analysis (RCA) of the Uncovered Bins
Enable Root Cause Analysis (RCA) to identify and mark bins as illegal when constraints
block them, using the +ntb_solver_bias_rca=2 runtime option. This feature helps you
improve coverage and diversity scores by automatically detecting which bins cannot be
covered due to constraints. Review RCA results in the coverage report to understand and
address coverage gaps efficiently.
ICO is enhanced to search the blocking constraints for the uncovered bins and mark them
as illegal. You must use the +ntb_solver_bias_rca=2 runtime option to enable this
feature. This feature helps to improve the overall O-SCOREs of coverage and diversity.
This feature requires additional computation. You can use the
+ntb_solver_rca_cpu_time_limit=<nsec> runtime option to increase the
CPU time allocated for RCA. Where, <nsec> is the time limit of RCA.
Use the +ntb_solver_bias_rca=2 and +ntb_solver_bias_rca_cpu_limit=<nsec>
options as follows to enable RCA of the uncovered bins:
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto=<mode>
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=<shared_record> +ntb_solver_bias_rca=2
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_cpu_limit=100
To generate reports, use the crg utility on the <record> directory after the run as follows:
% crg -dir <record> -report crgReport
% firefox crgReport/index.html
Viewing RCA of Uncovered Bins
Example 6 test.sv
rand bit [7:0] r1;
constraint cons {

(r1 % 2) == 1;
}

repeat(10)
end
This feature marks uncovered bins containing no odd values such as [2:2] and [4:4] as
illegal as these values are also blocked.
As shown in Figure 16, uncovered bins are marked as illegal along with the blocking
constraint. You can also see an increase in O-SCOREs for both coverage and diversity:
Figure 16 Viewing RCA of Uncovered Bins
RCA for User-Defined Bins
You can use the +ntb_solver_bias_rca=4 runtime option to enable RCA support for
the custom or user-defined bins. This option also enables RCA effort attributes and RCA
information features for the custom bins.

simv +ntb_solver_bias_sbin_file=<sbin_file>
+ntb_solver_bias_sbin_store_merge=add+reuse+modify
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_incr=<0|1>
+ntb_solver_bias_rca=<0|1|2|3|4>
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_incr=<0|1>
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_focus=<nt|to|nt+to>
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_cpu_limit=total:min:max
+ntb_solver_bias_rca=<0|1|2|3|4>
0: Disable
1: Enable for illegal
2: Enable for uncovered
3: Enable for uncovered due to soft constraints, a superset of 2.
4: Enable 1, 2, and 3 for user-defined bins also (superset of 3).
Example 7 test.sv
class my_rand;
typedef enum bit [9:0] {lcolor[20]} ltype;
rand ltype a1,a2;
rand bit [9:0] b1,b2;
rand int c1,c2;
int p=1100;
constraint my_constraint {
a1 inside {lcolor1, lcolor3, lcolor5, lcolor7};
a1 != a2;
b1 != b2;
c1 != c2;
c1 > 0;
soft b1 < 100;
b2 < p;
}

program test;
my_rand my_rand1 = new();
repeat(2)
my_rand1.randomize();

end

Root Cause Analysis (RCA) Due to Soft Constraints
ICO is enhanced to search the soft blocking constraints for the uncovered bins and mark
them as illegal. You must use the +ntb_solver_bias_rca=3 runtime option to enable
this feature. This feature helps to improve the overall O-SCOREs for both coverage and
diversity.

This feature requires additional computation. You can use the
+ntb_solver_rca_cpu_time_limit=<nsec> runtime option to increase the
CPU time allocated for RCA. Where, <nsec> is the time limit of RCA.
To enable RCA of the uncovered bins due to soft constraints, use the
+ntb_solver_bias_rca=3 and +ntb_solver_bias_rca_cpu_limit=<nsec> options as
follows:
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto=<mode>
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=<shared_record> +ntb_solver_bias_rca=3
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_cpu_limit=100
After the run, use the crg utility on the <record> directory, as follows, to generate reports:
% crg -dir <record> -report crgReport
% firefox crgReport/index.html
Viewing RCA of Soft Blocking Constraints for the Uncovered Bins
Example 9 test.sv
rand bit [9:0] a,b;
constraint cons {
soft {a > 5};
a < b;
}

repeat(10)
end
This feature marks uncovered bins of b with singleton values less than 7 (such as [1:1],
[2:2], and so on) and uncovered bins of a with singleton values less than 6 (such as
[0:0],[1:1], and so on) as illegal as these values are blocked due to soft constraints.
As shown in Figure 20, bins such as [1:1] for b and [3:3] for a (with red arrow), along
with illegal bin [0:0] for variable b (with blue arrow), are marked as illegal.

Figure 20 Viewing RCA of Uncovered Bins Due to Soft Constraints
Support for Ignoring Soft Constraints
Soft constraints allow you to specify default values for random variables. These
constraints must be honored if possible; otherwise, they are disregarded or dropped if no
solution is possible. Soft constraints are applied only to individual constraint expressions
and provide control for each constraint expression.
Example: soft x < 10;
If there are no other constraints on x, then x must take a value less than 10 as per the
SystemVerilog LRM. You may want to drop x, so that it is free to take any value. When
a design is close to tape out, you may want to drop the soft constraints and check if the
blocked scenarios can expose some real bugs.
ICO provides a set of +ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignore* runtime options to ignore (that
is, drop) soft constraints. These options allow you to:
• Ignore all soft constraints or only for certain random variables of certain classes of
certain class instances.
• Ignore soft constraints for a specific randomization serial only.

• Simv Runtime Options
• Behavior of Various Combinations of the Soft Ignore File and Soft IgnoreX File Options
• Example
Simv Runtime Options
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignore=<0|1|2>
+ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignore_file=<ignoreFile>
+ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignoreX_file=<ignoreXFile>
+ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignore_dump=<0|1>
+ntb_solver_bias_focus_filter=l:h[,l1:h1,l2:h2]
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_config=<0|1>
+ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignore=<0|1|2>
0: Honors all soft constraints
1: Ignores all soft constraints irrespective of whether biasing is ON or OFF
2: Ignores all soft constraints only when biasing is ON
+ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignore_file=<ignoreFile>
Restricts ignoring soft constraints to the variables specified in the ignore file.
This option is enabled only when +ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignore is set to either 1 or
2. A soft constraint may be ignored if at least one variable of the constraint is in the scope
file. Format is same as scope file, that is, file:line:class:varname. Where, varname
can be indexed array such as a[1].
+ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignoreX_file=<ignoreXFile>
Exclude ignoring soft constraints of the variables specified in the ignoreX file.
• This option is enabled only when +ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignore is set to
either 1 or 2.
• A soft constraint may still be ignored if at least one constraint variable is not
in the scopeX file. That is, to exclude ignoring a soft constraint, all variables
of the constraint must be excluded.
• Format is same as the scope file, that is, file:line:class:varname.

+ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignore_dump=<0|1>
0:Do not dump the soft constraints (default)
1:Dump the soft constraints in a file (<store_record>/record.cdb.softdrop)
+ntb_solver_bias_focus_filter=l:h,l1:h1,l2:h2
• When +ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignore=1, there is no effect of the focus
filter on soft ignoring of constraints.
• When +ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignore=2, soft ignoring of constraints
may occur for serialization where biasing is enabled. It does not occur when
biasing is disabled.
Key Points to Note
• RCA of the blocked values of class instance variables where soft constraints are
ignored do not have soft constraints in the root causes.
• If both +ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignore_file and
+ntb_solver_bias_solver_ignoreX_file options are provided, then variables in
the intersection of the variables specified by ignoreFile and those NOT specified in
ignoreXFile determine whether the soft constraints can be ignored or not.
• The following message is issued when +ntb_solver_bias_soft_ignore is set to
either 1 or 2:
Prognosis + BugFind + DistMerge + SoftIgnore feature(s).

Incremental RCA Support for Auto Bins
When performing Root Cause Analysis (RCA), you can limit the CPU time allocated for
RCA run using the runtime option such as
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_cpu_limit=300
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_cpu_limit=300.
Due to this time limit, it is possible that some RCA information may not get generated. For
uncovered bins, it is not clear if they are potentially coverable or cannot be covered at all
(not tried or timed-out).
VCS ICO provides effort attributes for the uncovered/illegal categories. These attributes
provide information on whether the unresolved problem:
• is hard and requires more time, or
• does not have sufficient time allocated and no time left to try, or
• is coverable, that is, not blocked, and sufficient randomization is needed.

VCS ICO provides the following runtime options to specify the kind of problem to target or
not for RCA and specify the time effort for each problem:
• The
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_incr=1
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_incr=1 option to track the effort attributes of each RCA
problem.
• The
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_focus=nt+to
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_focus=nt+to option to focus on the not tried ‘nt’ and
timed out ‘to’ RCA problems.
• The
ntb_solver_bias_rca_cpu_limit=totalminmax
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_cpu_limit=total:min:max option is enhanced to
control the CPU time.
Simulation Runtime Options
simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto_config=2 ; //recommended
+ntb_solver_bias_clean=0 ; //recommended
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=<sharedDb>
+ntb_solver_bias_rca=<0|1|2|3>
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_incr=<0|1>
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_focus=<nt|to|nt+to>
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_cpu_limit=total:min:max
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_incr=<0|1>
0: No tracking of incremental RCA effort (default).
1: Enables tracking of incremental RCA effort.
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_focus=<nt|to|nt+to>
nt: Target not-tried RCA unsolved problems.
to: Target timed-out RCA unsolved problems.
nt+to, to+nt: Target both not-tried and timed-out RCA problems.
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_cpu_limit=total:min:max
total: Total CPU time (in sec) for solving the RCA problem.
min: Minimum CPU time (in sec) allocated for solving an RCA problem. When a problem is
attempted for the first time, this time is allocated. Default min time is 60 sec.
max: Maximum CPU time (in sec) allocated for solving an RCA problem. Default max time
is twice the min value.
When a problem is timed-out, then the time allocated to it the next time is doubled until it
reaches max or gets solved. Maximum time can be up to 2 hours.

Coverage Runtime Option
Starting with this release, you can use the
-rca_effort_attr
-rca_effort_attr crg runtime option to
annotate RCA effort attributes for bins with no RCA information. Following is the use
model:
% crg -dir <cdb> -illegal_attr -illegal_group -rca_effort_attr
The RCA effort attributes are annotated in the Class Instance report as follows:
UNCOVERED::<TO|CO|NT>::E<n>
ILLEGAL::<TO|NT>::E<n>
TO: Timed Out
NT: Not Tried
CO: Coverable, that is, not blocked, and needs more randomization.
E<n>: Effort measure where n is between 1 <= n <= 8 . It represents the effort of 2n-1
sec of CPU time spent before time out.
When you retry, the effort is doubled until E8 or max is reached, whichever is earlier.

Figure 21 shows a sample report with annotated RCA effort attributes:
Figure 21 Annotated RCA Effort Attributes
Table 7 Annotated RCA Effort Attributes
Effort Attribute Description Action
UNCOVERED::CO Coverable More randomization is needed.
UNCOVERED::NT Not Tried More total RCA CPU time is needed.
UNCOVERED:TO Timed Out More min:max RCA CPU time is needed.
ILLEGAL::NT Not Tried More total RCA CPU time is needed.
ILLEGAL::TO Timed Out More min:max RCA CPU time is needed.
RCA Due to Internal Constraints
You can use the +ntb_solver_bias_rca_internal=1 runtime option to view the values
blocked by the internal constraints in the RCA view. This feature allows you to identify why
certain values are blocked.

This enhancement is backward compatible and do not change the existing behavior.
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_internal=<0|1>
0: No internal constraints (default)
1: Allows internal constraints in RCA if there are no user constraints.
Shortcut to RCA Configuration
You can use the +ntb_solver_bias_rca_config=1 runtime option to automatically
enable all recommended RCA options. This option improves RCA usability. You can use
this option to override any specific RCA option if required. This enhancement is backward
compatible and do not change the existing behavior.
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto_config=2;//recommended
+ntb_solver_bias_shared_record=<sharedDb>
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_config=<0|1>
where,
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_config=<0|1>
0: No effect
1: The following RCA options are enabled automatically:
+ntb_solver_bias_rca=4
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_incr=1
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_internal=1
+ntb_solver_bias_rca_cpu_limit=300

Singleton Bins for Enum Types
You can use the +ntb_solver_bias_enum_bin=1 simulation option to create singleton
bins for each enum value. This option is supported only for the variables of enum type.
This feature does not change the behavior of auto-binning for non-enum type variables.
% simv +ntb_solver_bias_enum_bin=<0|1> +ntb_solver_bias_mode_auto=<mode>
+ …
+ntb_solver_bias_enum_bin=<0|1> (default: 0)
When set to 1, this option creates singleton bins for all enum values.

If any cdb_record is created with +ntb_solver_bias_enum_bin=1, then the coverage
report for enum bin changes.
If the number of enum values of any given enum type is greater than 65536, default
binning is used.
The bin values are shown in HEX format, that is, h_XXX. Non-enum values are not
displayed.

typedef enum signed [10:0] {sA=-63, sB, sC=64,sD,sE=260} stype1;

rand stype1 s1;
rand ltype2 l1, l2;
rand bit [10:0] d1, d2;
constraint my_constraint {
r1 != r2;
l1 != l2;
d1 != d2;
s1 inside {sA,sB,sC,sD};
}

program test;

The auto binning support creates singleton bins for each value in the range [0,31] (for
unsigned numbers) and [-16,15] (for signed numbers) respectively. That is, values >=32
