The compile-time configuration file lists the modules whose instances you might replace
along with their corresponding substitute modules.
In this test case, the compile-time configuration file is named as config.txt:
//config.txt

replace module {test} with module {test_sbst};
This configuration file specifies the possible replacement of an instance of module test
with an instance of module test_sbst.
The compile-time command-line is as follows:
% vcs basic.v +optconfigfile+config.txt

Support with VCS Native Low Power
VCS displays the following information message from dynamic reconfiguration:
DYNAMIC RECONFIG> Replacing test With test_sbst Enabled
You have enabled replacing instances of module test with instances of module
test_sbst at runtime.
So at runtime, you must first write another configuration file specifying, by hierarchical
name, the module instances you want to replace. In this test case, the configuration file is
named as runconfig.txt:
//runconfig.txt

top.test_inst
This configuration file specifies that you want the module instance with the hierarchical
name top.test_inst to be replaced. The other instance of module test, with the
hierarchical name top.test_inst1, is not replaced.
Figure 78 Diagram of the Dynamically Reconfigured Test Case
top
test test_inst1 test_sbst
The runtime command-line for this dynamic reconfiguration is as follows:
% simv -dynaconfig runconfig.txt
Before simulation, VCS replaces this instance with an instance of the substitute module
specified in the compile-time configuration file, an instance of module test_sbst.
Also, before the simulation, VCS displays the following information message:
DYNAMIC RECONFIG: Instance top.test_inst is replaced with module
(test_sbst)
Support with VCS Native Low Power
During the design compilation phase, you must provide both the original and substitute
alternate module source files along with the configuration file, and specify the UPF file
using the -upf option, as shown below:
% vcs +optconfigfile+ compile_config_file_name \
top_module_of_design.v \

Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
original_module.v substitute_module.v \
-upf original_module.upf
With respect to the VCS Native Low Power (NLP), the following simulation behavior
applies:
• Power-down semantics: Power-down corruption would be instrumented for both the
original and substitute modules. Though the power-down corruption instrumentation is
done for substitute modules, you must not see any corruption behavior at runtime.
• Isolation semantics: Isolation would not get instrumented for the substitute modules
except when you specify the isolation as parent or fanout. You must not observe any
isolation on the ports/pins of the substituted modules except when the isolation location
is parent or fanout.
• Retention semantics: No retention would be instrumented for the substitute modules.
You must not observe any registers being retained in the substituted module.
The following restrictions apply if you use dynamic reconfiguration flow with VCS NLP:
• Though the substituted modules are simulated without Low power semantics, still
runtime low power messages related to the power domain are generated.
• If power domain related control signals like switch, isolation control are present in the
original module and got replaced with the substitute module, then all those control
signals gets “Z” value, and related runtime low power messages are generated
accordingly.
Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
You can use dynamic reconfiguration in a mixed signal verification, but only if the analog
(SPICE or Verilog-A) part of the mixed signal design is entirely in the active, stimulated,
and unchanged part of the design.
Consider the hypothetical design in Figure 79 in which the analog part of the design is
entirely in the active, stimulated and unchanged part of the design.
Note that the sub-hierarchies whose top-level SystemVerilog module instances are eql1
and sem1 are not active or stimulated in a series of tests and are purely digital. As long as
you are not replacing the analog part of the design, you can use dynamic reconfiguration
at runtime to replace these sub-hierarchies with empty substitute modules.

Dynamic Reconfiguration in a Mixed Signal Flow
• Cross-module references (XMRs) from analog side of mixed signal boundary to the
replaced side of the dynamic reconfiguration boundary are not supported.
• Analog tunnel re-analysis cannot happen when a Verilog module is replaced at runtime
using dynamic reconfiguration. All the connectivity analysis happens at compile-time
and therefore runtime changes from dynamic reconfiguration is not reflected in this
analysis.
The use model for using the dynamic reconfiguration at runtime feature in a mixed signal
design is a combination of the use models for dynamic reconfiguration and mixed signal
verification. The following are the steps in the combined use model:
1. Write substitute empty module definitions to replace the top-level modules of the sub-
hierarchies that are inactive for a series of tests.
2. Write a compile-time configuration file for dynamic reconfiguration that specifies:
◦ the original module definitions of the top-level module instances in the inactive sub-
hierarchies
◦ the substitute empty module definitions that replace the originals at runtime
3. Write a setup file for the analog part of the mixed signal design.
4. Compile the digital part of the design, specifying three things:
◦ compiling for dynamic reconfiguration with the compile-time configuration
file specified with the following option: +optconfigfile+compile-
time_config_file_name
◦ compiling for mixed signal simulation and specifying the setup file with the following
option: -ad=setup_file
◦ the source files for the module definitions in the design and the source files for the
empty substitute modules
The vcs command line has the following syntax:
% vcs +optconfigfile+ compile-time_config_file_name \ -ad=setup_file
top_module_of_design.v original_module.v \ substitute_module.v
Example 110 Example vcs Command Line
% vcs +optconfigfile+com_config.txt -ad=my_spsetup prog.sv \
top.sv introctr.sv ptarbt.sv sem.sv eql.sv. sub_eql.sv \
sub_sem.sv.

5. Write a runtime configuration file for dynamic reconfiguration that specifies the
hierarchical names of the top-level module instances in the inactive sub-hierarchies.
6. Start the simulation with a simv command line specifying the runtime configuration file
with the following option and argument: -dynaconfig runtime_config_file_name

The feature has the following limitations:
• MDAs for interface type object across partial elaboration are not supported.
• Only top-down absolute XMRs in substitute modules are allowed to access object in
the fixed part of the design.
• Original module of partial elaboration hierarchy can have reference to the upward XMR
or the module XMR. These XMRs are valid if no replacement happens at simulation
time. If the substitute module has upward XMR, then VCS generates compile-time
error.
• XMRs with target inside partial elaboration hierarchy do not have value if the module is
replaced at simulation time. If original module is used at simulation time, then values of
XMR are updated.
• The substitute module that do not have any instance in fixed part of the design are
instantiated as a dummy top-level instance at simulation time.
• Only XMRs to scalars. vectors, and MDA across the dynamic reconfiguration boundary
are allowed. All other complex types result in compile-time XMR error conditions.
If replacement happens any XMR reading from the replaced hierarchy returns Z (high
impedance). Even if the replacement module instance matches with the XMR path, the
XMR does not get resolved in the new instance.
• The ports of the original and substitute modules must be the same in terms of:
◦ Direction
◦ Size (bit-width and number of dimensions)
◦ Data type
There is no requirement that the corresponding ports have the same name.

• Strength declarations, registered nets, and ref ports are not allowed on modules
on the dynamic reconfiguration boundary. This boundary has the following module
definitions:
◦ Original modules whose instances might be replaced at runtime
◦ Substitute modules
• In VCS mixed-HDL designs, module definitions on the boundary must be Verilog or
SystemVerilog and have none of the following hierarchically under them:
◦ VHDL code cannot be hierarchically under a replacement module.
◦ SystemC module
◦ An analog part of a mixed-signal design
◦ A DirectC call, but PLI and VPI calls across the boundary are allowed.
• Parameter values are evaluated at for compile-time. Parameter passing across the
boundary is allowed but VCS does not assign the parameter values in the replaced
instances.
• The module definitions for substitute modules must be part of the design’s source
code. VCS does not create empty modules for you.

Support for Latch-Type Isolation Cell with Set/Reset Pins
VCS NLP allows you to specify the connections for the set/reset pins in the
set_isolation command.
Figure 85 Latch Isolation Cell With Set/Reset Pins
An isolation cell with -clamp_value specified as latch can sometimes have an
asynchronous set or reset pin on the cell. When that cell is inserted by the UPF using the
set_isolation command, it also requires connection to the set/reset pins of the isolation
cell. The syntax of set_isolation command is extended to enable you to specify the
control signal which connects to the set/reset pins of the isolation cell.
This feature allows you to model latch type isolation cells with asynchronous set/reset
pins.

Support for Latch-Type Isolation Cell with Set/Reset Pins
VCS NLP supports the following set_isolation command options to enable this feature:
set_isolation
[-async_set_reset { net_name <high | low>}]
[-async_clamp_value <0 | 1>]
[other options]
• The -async_set_reset option specifies the control signal (net) which should be
connected to the set/reset pins of the isolation cell along with the sensitivity (high/low)
of the signal.
• The signal specified with the -async_set_reset option acts either as a set or reset
of the isolation cell based on the clamp value set by the -async_clamp_value option
(clamp value is 0 for reset and 1 for set)
• The net_name is the name of the control signal which acts as the set or reset.

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
reset option acts either as a set or reset
of the isolation cell based on the clamp value set by the -async_clamp_value option
(clamp value is 0 for reset and 1 for set)
• The net_name is the name of the control signal which acts as the set or reset. Its type
is similar to -isolation_signal and can be either port, pin, or net. The sensitivity is
specified using the high or low keyword.
• The -async_clamp_value option specifies whether the -async_set_reset option acts
as a set or reset.
• When -async_clamp_value is 0, net_name acts as a reset of the isolation cell.
• When -async_clamp_value is 1, net_name acts as a set of the isolation cell.
• Specifying -async_clamp_value is optional. The clamp value can also be set using a
port attribute.
• The -async_set_reset and -async_clamp_value options can be specified with
-update. They can occur in any order.
Using Port Attribute
If you do not want the control pin to act as a set or reset while specifying the strategy, you
can use the UPF_async_clamp_value port attribute. In this case, the same control pin
may get connected to some cells which have set and other cells which have reset pin.
set_port_attributes -ports {p1} -attribute {UPF_async_clamp_value 0/1 }
This attribute is applicable when -async_set_reset option is specified. For an isolation
strategy with -async_set_reset option and without a -async_clamp_value option, VCS
NLP uses the specified clamp value in the port attribute.
If there is a conflict between -async_clamp_value and the UPF_async_clamp_value
attribute, a warning message is issued and the UPF_async_clamp_value attribute is used
for behavior.

Support to Allow Internal Direction for Supply Port
Error and Warning Conditions
The following are the error and warning conditions:
• An error message is issued when -async_set_reset is specified and -clamp_value
is not a latch.
• An error message is issued when net_name is specified, but sensitivity <high|low> is
not specified.
• An error message is issued when net_name does not exist in the design.
• A warning message is issued when -async_set_reset is specified and there is
no -async_clamp_value specified in the set_isolation command or through the
set_port_attributes command (as specified in the UPF_async_clamp_value port
attribute). The -async_set_reset option is ignored.
• A warning message is issued when -async_clamp_value is specified, but there is no
-async_set_reset option. The -async_clamp_value option is ignored.
Also, when the UPF_async_clamp_value attribute is specified, but there is no
-async_set_reset option, the attribute is ignored.
Support to Allow Internal Direction for Supply Port
In some flows, at one point in the design process, it is useful to seamlessly swap between
a liberty model and a UPF based model. In this case, a key goal is that the top level UPF
should not be modified.
You can use a top level virtual net to connect ports of liberty models with direction :
internal. However, when the liberty model is represented with UPF, you can use a new
direction internal with the create_supply_port command, which gives the equivalent
of direction : internal in a liberty model.
The set of possible values for the -direction option of the create_supply_port
command is enhanced to include value internal. This feature allows seamless switching
between liberty models and UPF models during the design process.
create_supply_port port_name
[-domain domain_name]
[-direction <in | out | inout | internal>]

Handling Multiple Connections to Virtual Supplies
Handling Multiple Connections to Virtual Supplies
A PG pin of direction internal (irrespective of pg_type) is considered as a virtual driver
for a supply net. Any other kind of driver is a real driver.
If there are multiple real drivers, you must specify the resolution for the supply net. If
there are only virtual drivers or one real driver along with other virtual drivers, VCS NLP
considers the resolution as parallel.
For example, VCS NLP supports the following usage where VDD_int is a PG pin of a
macro (whose instances are macro_inst1 and macro_inst2) with direction internal.
Supply VDD that is unresolved has two drivers:
create_supply_net VDD
connect_supply_net VDD -ports {macro_inst1/VDD_int macro_inst2/VDD_int}
For the above UPF code, multiple drivers are created on the virtual supply net that is
connected to the internal PG pins.
Support for SPA -literal_supply Option
VCS NLP supports the -literal_supply option of the set_port_attributes command.
This option allows you to define the supply to be used to model a literal constant value
(1'b0/1'b1) associated to a pin/port marked with this option.
set_port_attributes
[-elements elements_list]
[-exclude_elements elements_exclude_list]
[-ports port_list]
[-exclude_ports port_exclude_list]
[-applies_to inputs | outputs]
-literal_supply supply_set_reference
This enhancement allows you to specify (change) the related supply of literal constants
(1'b0 and 1'b1). That is, you can use a different supply for literal value instead of parent
domain’s supply.
set_port_attributes -literal_supply SS_A0 -ports {OUT1 OUT2}
If a literal constant is associated to a pin/port attributed with literal supply, then the literal
constant is assumed to be powered by the supply referenced in the -literal_supply
option, and consequently affects isolation analysis and modeling of corruption semantics
for the literal.

Support for SPA -literal_supply Option
• The -model option cannot be used with -literal_supply
• At least one of -ports or -elements should be specified while using
-literal_supply.

The following semantic checks are added:
• The set of ports to be attributed must not be empty. They must be obtained from
processing the explicit references in -ports and -exclude_ports and the implicit
references in -elements and -exclude_elements.
• For each port to be attributed, precedence resolution is done based on the precedence

Figure 86 Modeling Literal Constant Driver on Input Port
PDTOP.primary PDBOT.primary VSS
ON ON GND
OFF ON GND
Without this enhancement, the constant driver domain’s primary supply TOP.primary is
used to assess source/sink isolation strategy applicability, so macro_in_ISO strategy is
applicable.
With this enhancement, Literal is assumed to be powered by BOT.primary and isolation
strategy macro_in_ISO does not apply.
Example-2: Constant Driving Primary Output Port

Support for SPA -literal_supply Option
Consider the following UPF:
Example 118 test.upf
create_power_domain PDTOP -elements {.}

set_port_attributes -ports {out1} \
-literal_supply SS_A0
Figure 87 Constant Driving Primary Output Port
PDTOP.primary (VDD) SS_AO.power (A0_VDD) VSS
ON ON GND
OFF ON GND
Without this enhancement:
• Literal constant driver is assumed to be powered by the primary ( VDD).
• Simulates the literal as a Tie-cell powered by PDTOP primary power (VDD), driving the
port out1.
With this enhancement:
• Literal constant driver is assumed to be powered by the primary ( SS_AO (AO_VDD) ).
• Simulates the literal as an AO Tie-cell powered by SS_AO, so there is no isolation
requirement on this path.

Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation Semantics
Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation Semantics
VCS NLP supports the set_retention -use_retention_as_primary option. When this
option is specified, the retention supply powers the output driver of the register. That is, the
primary supply of the output pin of the retention register is the retention supply.
set_retention retention_name
-domain domain_name
[ -use_retention_as_primary]
set_retention RET1 -domain PD1 -use_retention_as_primary
map_retention_cell -domain PD1 -lib_cells {SDFRET*} RET1
This enhancement allows you to model a retention cell with output related to backup
supply. Specifying the -use_retention_as_primary option instructs VCS NLP to use a
retention cell whose output pin is related to the retention supply (rather than the domain
primary).
Figure 88 Library Cell Used When -use_retention_as_primary is Specified

Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation Semantics
• When the -use_retention_as_primary option is not specified, for paths which
originate from the output of the retention, the primary supply of the domain is
considered as the driver_supply.
• When the -use_retention_as_primary option is specified, for paths which originate
from the output of the retention, the retention_supply of the retention strategy is
considered as the driver_supply of the path.
• The -use_retention_as_primary option changes the driver supply of ports that are
sinks of the inserted retention register. Such changes could affect the interpretation of
the -source filters of the set_isolation strategies that apply to those ports.
Corruption and Isolation Semantics
Following are the corruption semantics:
• When - use_retention_as_primary option is specified, the output of the retention
registers associated with this strategy are not corrupted when domain is in CORRUPT
state.
• When - use_retention_as_primary option is not specified, the retention registers are
corrupted when the domain is in CORRUPT state.
Following are the isolation semantics:
• Using the - use_retention_as_primary option with retention strategies impacts the
-source filter of the isolation strategies on the domain crossing driven by the retention
register.
Isolation strategies specified on ports that are driven by this retention register must be
evaluated with the source supply as the retention supply rather than domain primary.
Example: Impact on Source-Based Strategies
Consider the following UPF:
Example 119 test.upf
create_power_domain PD_MID -elements {Mid}
create_supply_set SS1

Figure 89 Impact on Source-Based Strategies
Isolation cells based on strategy ISO2 are inserted on the net driven by the retention
register O1_reg (associated with retention strategy RET1). Since RET1 strategy does not
specify -use_retention_as_primary, register output supply is PD_MID.primary.
Isolation cell based on strategy ISO1 is inserted on the net driven by the retention
register O2_reg (associated with retention strategy RET2). Since RET2 strategy specifies
-use_retention_as_primary, register output supply is SS1.
Following is the limitation of this feature:
• VHDL is not supported for the isolation semantics.
Support for Atomic Power Domains
VCS NLP supports atomic power domains as per 1801-2018 version of the UPF LRM.
As per the LRM, extent of an atomic power domain can be modified, that is, updating
the options -elements {} and -exclude_elements {} of an atomic power domain is
allowed.
You must use the -atomic option of the create_power_domain command to define an
atomic power domain. Following is the syntax for creating an atomic power domain:
create_power_domain <name> -atomic
[-elements element_list]
[-exclude_elements exclude_list]
[…]

Support for Atomic Power Domains
• To define an atomic power domain, you must specify the -atomic option during the first
definition of that power domain. Specifying the -atomic option later with -update is not
allowed, it results in an error and dropping of that constraint.
• For any cell in the extent of atomic power domain to be added to any other power
domain, the cell or its ancestor must be excluded from the atomic power domain.
• In the rest of this section, any mention of the phrase power domain implies non-atomic
power domain.
Supported Usage
The following points describe the supported usage of the -atomic option:
• An empty power domain can be defined as atomic.
• A power domain on macro, ETM, or black box can be defined as atomic.
• A power domain on leaf cells can be defined as atomic.
• You can update the extent of an atomic power domain, that is, updating -elements {}
and -exclude_elements {} is allowed.
• An element excluded from atomic power domain can be added to either atomic or non-
atomic power domain. There is no restriction that an element excluded from atomic
should be added only to atomic power domains.
• There is no restriction that root cells of atomic power domains should be part of same
voltage area. They can be part of different voltage areas too.
Error Checks
The following error checks are added:
Error Check-1
VCS NLP will not allow any instance in the descendant subtree of an atomic power
domain to be included in the extent of another power domain, unless that instance name
is, or is in the descendant subtree of an instance which is excluded from that atomic
domain. Violating this results in an error message (see Example 2).
Error Check-2
VCS NLP will not allow updating a non-atomic power domain as atomic (see Example 3).
That is, the -atomic option cannot be specified with -update, unless the power domain is
already defined as atomic. Violating this results in an error message.
In addition to the above checks, all existing checks that are performed while creating non-
atomic power domains applies to atomic power domains too.

Support for Atomic Power Domains
This section provides various examples with respect to the atomic power domains.
Example-1
Consider the following UPF code:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -elements {m2 m1/b1} -include_scope
create_power_domain PD_MID -atomic -elements {m1}
Figure 90 Atomic Power Domains
As per the processing rules of power domains, atomic power domains must be created
first, so PD_MID is created first. Root cell of atomic power domain PD_MID is m1. Therefore,
the entire descendant tree of m1 is in the extent of PD_MID.
Now, non-atomic power domains must be created, so VCS NLP tries to create PD_TOP.
However, m1/b1 listed as root cell of PD_TOP is already in the extent of atomic power
domain PD_MID. As per Error Check-1, this is incorrect and results in an error.
Later, you can fix the UPF in the following two ways:
Approach-1:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -elements {m2 m1/b1} -include_scope
create_power_domain PD_MID -atomic -elements {m1}
…
create_power_domain PD_MID -exclude_elements {m1/b1} -update
You can exclude m1/b1 from atomic power domain PD_MID.
Approach-2:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -elements {m2 m1/b1} -include_scope
create_power_domain PD_MID -atomic -elements {m1}
…
create_power_domain PD_TOP -exclude_elements {m1/b1} -update
You can exclude m1/b1 from non-atomic power domain PD_TOP and add it to atomic power
domain PD_MID.

Support for Modeling Isolation Cell Without Enable Pin in Liberty
Example-2
Consider the following UPF code:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -include_scope
create_power_domain PD_MID -elements {mid} -atomic
create_power_domain PD_BOT -elements {mid/bot}
Here, root cell of power domain PD_BOT mid/bot is in the extent of atomic power domain
PD_MID. As per Error Check-1, this is incorrect and results in an error.
Later you can fix the UPF by excluding mid/bot from atomic power domain PD_MID.
create_power_domain PD_TOP -include_scope
create_power_domain PD_MID -elements {mid} -atomic
create_power_domain PD_BOT -elements {mid/bot}
…
create_power_domain PD_MID -exclude_elements {mid/bot} -update
Example-3
Consider the following UPF code:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -include_scope
create_power_domain PD_MID -elements {mid1}
create_power_domain PD_BOT -elements {mid1/bot}
create_power_domain PD_MID -elements {mid2} -update -atomic
Here, non-atomic PD_MID is being updated as atomic by the last create_power_domain
command. As per Error Check-2, updating non-atomic power domain as atomic is not
allowed. The last create_power_domain command results in an error and PD_MID
continues to be a non-atomic power domain.

Marking a Cell or Module As Power Aware by Considering the Direction and Type of Its PG
Pins
Marking a Cell or Module As Power Aware by Considering the
Direction and Type of Its PG Pins
VCS NLP is enhanced to perform a strict DB PG pin matching for a cell or module
by considering the direction and type of its PG pins in Liberty and Verilog model, and
appropriately mark the
IsPowerAwareModuleCell
IsPowerAwareModuleCell attribute as true or false in the
mvsim_native_reports/library_mapping.rpt file. It performs the following checks to
mark a cell or module as power aware:
• If Liberty declares a PG pin with direction : in, it should be direction inout or input in
the Verilog model for the cell or module to be classified as power aware.
• If Liberty declares a PG pin with direction : out, it should be direction inout or output
in the Verilog model for the cell or module to be classified as power aware.
• If the direction of a PG pin in Liberty is unknown, VCS NLP checks for its pg_type.
If pg_type is internal power or ground, it cannot match to an input port, but can match
to either of the output, inout, reg, wire, supply0, supply1, and supply_net_type.
If pg_type is primary power or ground, it can match to any port (input, output, or
inout), reg, wire, supply0, supply1, or supply_net_type.
To enable this feature, use the
-power=strict_db_match
-power=strict_db_match compile-time option.
Simulation behavior depends on whether the Verilog model is power aware or non-power
aware. This feature allows you to correct the Verilog model or make any other required
changes to get accurate simulation behavior of a DB cell or model.

text:
Support for Golden UPF
Following are the limitations of this feature:
• This feature is supported only for SystemVerilog real variable type only. Wreal or any
other nettype nodes involving ‘real’ are not supported.
• This feature is supported only for pure Verilog designs. VHDL is not supported.
• The corruption is restricted to the ‘simstate’ based corruption only. Therefore, this
feature does not affect the corruption due to isolation power, SRSN/SPA power, or any
port-based corruption.
Support for Golden UPF
In the UPF flow, each stage of the flow uses a single UPF file that is modified during
synthesis and physical implementation in the following ways:
The original UPF file, written with the RTL description, is modified by the Design Compiler,
resulting in the UPF' (UPF prime) file. The UPF' file reflects the changes that occurred
during synthesis such as insertion of always-on buffers, isolation and retention cells, and
PG connections to the cells.
The UPF' file is modified by the IC Compiler, resulting in the UPF'' (UPF double prime) file.
The UPF'' file reflects the changes that occurred during physical implementation, such as
the insertion of power switch cells.
The Synopsys Galaxy Implementation Platform offers a method of maintaining the UPF
multi-voltage power intent of the design using the original “golden” UPF file throughout the
synthesis, physical implementation, and verification steps, along with supplemental UPF
files generated by the Design Compiler and IC Compiler tools. This method is called the
golden UPF flow.
% vcs <design_files> -sverilog -gupf_config power.config
% ./simv
The -gupf_config option allows you to specify the power configuration file
(power.config). Following are the contents of the power.config file:
db_search_path = "<dir1>,<dir2>,…"
db_link_library = "<file1.db>,<file2.db>,…"
set upf_name_map { {mod1 mod1.nmf} {mod2 mod2.nmf} {mod3 mod3.nmf} … }
read_upf <UPF_FILE_NAME> \
-strict_check false \
-supplemental <supplemental_UPF_file> \
-target <icc_netlist|dc_pg_netlist|dc_netlist> \
-scope <TARGET MODULE>

Support for Golden UPF
db_search_path
Global variable. Used to search for .db (liberty) files.
db_link_library
Global variable. Used to specify the list of .db files to be used in the design.
upf_name_map
Global variable. Used to specify the name of the map file for a design top module.
read_upf
This command is used to parse the Synopsys flow compatible UPF file.
The read_upf command must be specified for the top-level UPF file. The options of this
command have the following semantics:
-strict_check false
When false (as for golden UPF application to a netlist), default matching rules are used
for name lookups, if no rules are defined.
-supplemental <supplemental_UPF_file>
Specifies a supplemental UPF file to be loaded after the golden UPF file. The
supplemental UPF additionally supports create_power_domain -elements -update .
-target <icc_netlist|dc_pg_netlist|dc_netlist>
Specifies the target design.
icc_netlist — Specifies that the isolation and retention strategies, and power switches
are implemented in the incoming target netlist, and resulting cells are explicitly connected
to their supplies through the connect_supply_net commands in the incoming UPF.
VCS NLP supports ICC PG netlists where supplies are implemented and
explicitly connected in the netlist.
dc_pg_netlist — Specifies that the supplies are implemented and explicitly connected in
the incoming target DC netlist.
dc_netlist — Specifies that the isolation and retention strategies are implemented in the
incoming target netlist, and resulting cells are explicitly connected to their supplies through
the connect_supply_net commands in the incoming UPF.

• The correlated_supply_group attribute

Successive Refinement of a Supply Set State
VCS NLP allows you to define a supply set state partially and then incrementally refine it
to a fully-defined states using the -update option of the add_power_state command. To
begin with, you can initially specify the name of the state, and then incrementally add more
intent to the state using the -update option.

Successive Refinement of a Supply Set State
This feature is supported for all types of objects (supply set, domain, and group) that are
currently supported with the add_power_state command. Following are the general rules
to achieve a successive refinement flow using the -update option:
1. To begin with, the initial definition of the state can have just the name of the state (It
may or may not have additional information).
2. Additional information for the state (-supply_expr, -logic_expr, and so on) can be
added incrementally using the -update option.
3. If a state defined with the supply network expression (-supply_expr) is updated with
another -supply_expr, the new definition is interpreted as the conjunction of the two.
That is, -supply_expr can be updated in the following ways:
◦ The initial definition can have just the net state ( FULL_ON/OFF) for a functional net
without voltage, and the updated definition can specify the voltage for the functional
net.
◦ The initial definition can have one or more functional nets, and the updated
definition can specify more functional nets.
4. If a state defined with the logic expression (-logic_expr) is updated with another
-logic_expr, the new definition is interpreted as the conjunction of the two.
5. If the -simstate option is specified as NOT_NORMAL, it can be updated to any simstate
other than NORMAL.
6. If the -simstate option is specified as NORMAL, CORRUPT, or CORRUPT_ON_ACTIVITY, it
cannot be updated to any other simstate other than the one originally specified.
7. A partially defined state can be used in the -logic_expr of a group or a domain.
The following example shows successive refinement for a supply set state:
The new intent added to the state at each level are marked in bold font.
1. Define a supply set state with a name
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {}
2. Add -supply_expr to the state, but without voltage
add_power_state SS1 -state ON { -supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON}} }
3. Add voltage to -supply_expr
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON 1.0}}}
4. Add -logic_expr to the state
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON 1.0}} \
-logic_expr {net1} }

Successive Refinement of a Supply Set State
5. Add -simstate to the state
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON 1.0}} \
-logic_expr {net1} \
-simstate {NORMAL} }
Supported Successive Refinement Styles
The following sections describe different successive refinement styles that are supported
as part of this feature:
Updating an Existing Supply Set State
This section describes the following topics:
Updating an Existing Supply Network Expression
The following example shows how the supply network expression (-supply_expr) can
be updated. Here, voltage information and functional nets are incrementally added to
-supply_expr using the -update option.
Example 124 test.upf
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON}}}
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {ground ==
{FULL_ON}}} -update
add_power_state -supply SS1 -state ON {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON

Updating an Existing Logic Expression
You can use the -update option to update an existing logic expression (-logic_expr).
The following example shows how a logic expression can be updated using the -update
option:
Example 125 test1.upf
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-logic_expr {net1}}
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-logic_expr {net2}} -update
The above UPF is interpreted as follows. This is in line with the UPF 2.1.
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-logic_expr {net1 && net2}}
Updating an Existing Simstate
You can use the -update option to update an existing simstate (-simstate).
The following example shows how a simstate can be updated using the -update option:
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-simstate {NOT_NORMAL}}
add_power_state SS1 -state ON {-simstate {CORRUPT}} -update

Permitting Supply Set States that do not Have a Supply Network Expression in
Group/Domain State
VCS NLP allows you to refer to a supply set state in a group irrespective of whether the
supply set state has a -supply_expr defined or not. The -supply_expr definition for
the supply set state can come later in the flow, after the group is defined. Consider the
following example:
Example 128 test4.upf
add_power_state SS1 -state ON1 {-supply_expr {power == {FULL_ON 0.8}}}
add_power_state SS1 -state ON2 {-simstate NORMAL}

create_power_state_group GROUP
add_power_state -group GROUP -state GS1 {-logic_expr {SS1 == ON1}}
add_power_state -group GROUP -state GS2 {-logic_expr {SS1 == ON2}}
-update
For the above UPF, group states GS1 and GS2 are created successfully.
Excluding Ports from the set_port_attributes Command
As per the UPF 3.0, a port is removed from the candidate set if the port name appears in
the -exclude_ports list.

Excluding Ports from the set_port_attributes Command
VCS NLP supports the -exclude_ports option of the set_port_attributes command.
This option provides flexibility for specifying ports for the set_port_attributes
The ports in the list of -exclude_ports are excluded from the current
set_port_attributes command.
• If a port is listed in -exclude_ports of the current set_port_attributes, its previous
set_port_attributes setting continues to apply.
• If all the objects in -exclude_ports do not exist in the design, the entire command is
an error and has no effect.
• If only some, but not all, objects in -exclude_ports do not exist in the design, the
command is applied to the existing objects, and a warning is issued for the non-existing
object.
• If both -exclude_ports and -model are specified, the specified ports of the model are
excluded during candidate set creation. When specified with -model, arguments to the
-exclude_ports option should be simple names. VCS NLP issues an error message if
rooted names are specified in this usage.
Consider the following figure:
Case-1: -exclude_ports with -ports. In the following example, top_in1 is excluded:
set_port_attributes -ports {top_in*} -exclude_ports {top_in1} -attribute
-clamp_value z

The following features are not supported:
• -elements with -exclude_elements
• -elements with -exclude_ports
• Interface/modport support
• VHDL Support
• Bit-level support for -model -exclude_ports
The following attributes are not supported:
• iso_source
• iso_sink
• repeater_power_net
• repeater_ground_net

set_retention command is enhanced to support the -exclude_elements option in
the UPF. You must use the
-power=ret_exclude
-power=ret_exclude compile option to enable this feature.
This feature allows you to exclude some instances, blocks, or registers from a retention
strategy.
You can use the -exclude_elements option at the time of creating a retention strategy.
set_retention retention_name
-domain domain_name
[-elements element_list]
[-exclude_elements exclude_list]
[-no_retention]
set_retention RET2 -domain PD1 -elements {u2} -exclude_elements {u2/reg2}
The element u2/reg2 is excluded.
This feature is also supported with the -update option.

set_retention RET1 -domain PD1 -elements {u1}
set_retention RET1 -domain PD1 -exclude_elements {u1/reg2} -update

I1 I2 I3
I1/J1 I1/J2
I1/J1/K1 I1/J1/K2
I1/J1/K1/L1 I1/J1/K1/L2

Setting Attributes on UPF Objects
The set_design_attributes command is enhanced to allow setting attributes on
UPF objects. The UPF objects can be specified using the -elements option of the
set_design_attributes command. The attributes are specified using the -attribute
UPF Objects
The following UPF objects are supported in the -elements option of the
set_design_attributes command:
• Supply net
• Logic net

The set_design_attributes command also allows you to set the attribute on the logic/
supply nets that have HDL implementation.
Wildcards are supported for UPF objects.
Attributes
The set_design_attributes command allows you to set user-defined attributes and
Synopsys predefined attributes. When user-defined attributes are set, VCS NLP issues a
warning and ignores it.
set_design_attributes -elements {Supply_nets/Logic_nets} -attribute
<attribute> <attribute value>

logical_supply_net TRUE
set_design_attributes -elements {LogicNet} -attribute
user_defined_attribute TRUE
set_design_attributes -elements {inst1/VDD*} -attribute logic_supply_net
TRUE
Attributes logical_supply_net, user_defined_attribute,
logic_supply_net are user-defined attributes.
The UPF information model captures the power management information which is the
result of application of UPF commands on the user design. It consists of a set of objects
containing information and various relationships between them.

Figure 95 UPF Information Model Flow
The UPF information model consists of a collection of objects. The information is present
on these objects in the form of properties, which can be accessed through APIs. Each
object is denoted by a unique identifier (ID) called UPF handle which is used by the APIs
to access information present on it.
The objects and properties in the information model can be accessed by a HDL object of
upfHandleT type.
The class IDs are unique strings that represent class names in the information model. The
class names are represented in capitalized words with a upf prefix and T suffix.
Example: upfPowerDomainT, upfHdlScopeT
The property IDs are unique strings that represent the properties present on the object.
The property names are denoted by lowercase words separated by a “_” (underscore
character) and a upf prefix.
Examples: upf_name, upf_parent
The classes in the information model are identified in HDL by the enumerated values
defined in upfClassIdE enumerated type. Refer to section 11.2.2.5 of the IEEE Std
1801-2015 LRM for information on mapping between information model classes and
corresponding class id in HDL type.
The HDL interface to the information model allows you to create abstract testbenches to
manipulate UPF objects directly in simulation.
For more information on the UPF information model, see the IEEE Std 1801-2015 LRM.
VCS NLP supports HDL access functions (UPF Package 3.0 APIs) as defined in the
IEEE Std 1801-2015 LRM. For more information, see Supported APIs. You must use the
-power=svapi compile time option to enable this feature.

This feature provides a standard interface that can be used to access power management
information.

upf_get_handle_by_name
VCS NLP supports the following types of handles:
• Object Handles
References to the objects in the UPF information model. These handles can be
compared using a == operator.
• Iterator Handles
Iterators to containers in the UPF information model. These handles can be reused as
iterators are scoped objects and get deleted after the iteration is complete. You must
not use the iterator handles with the == operator for comparison.
• Property Handles
References to property value wrapper. These handles are same for all integer/Boolean
properties, real, string, and supply type properties. You must not use the iterator
handles with the == operator for comparison.
Table 16 Get Handle By Name
Description Returns the handle to the object in the information model from the given path
name.
upf_get_handle_by_name
upfHandleT upf_get_handle_by_name(upfStringT pathname,
upfHandleT relative_to = null);
Example Example: Get handle to a strategy
upfHandleT scope = upf_get_handle_by_name("/top/ dut_i");
upfHandleT iso = upf_get_handle_by_name("pd", scope);
end
Arguments pathname - A string representing handle ID for an object.
relative_to - An optional handle to the object from which the relative path
name is given.
Return Value Returns the handle to the specified property or null if not found.
The path name starts with ‘/’ followed by the object or scope below power top. This API
returns following types of handles:
• Objects
• Iterators

This UPF Package 3.0 API allows you to query properties on a given object. The
properties are both static and dynamic as follows:
Static properties – These are populated at the time of UPF compilation.
Dynamic properties – These are populated during the simulation and always have the

Searching Specified Scope and Its Descendant Hierarchy
The find_objects command searches for instances, nets, ports, supply ports, or
processes within a scope.
A leaf cell is any cell having no descendants. Standard cells and macros are always
considered to be leaf cells. Any hierarchy with the terminal_boundary attribute is also
considered as a leaf cell. For macros, a UPF_is_hard_macro attribute value of TRUE on
a model or a UPF_is_soft_macro attribute value of TRUE on an instance indicates that it
shall be treated as a leaf cell.
VCS NLP allows you to search the specified scope and its entire descendant hierarchy
without considering the terminal_boundary/UPF_is_soft_macro marking using the
-traverse_macros option. Following is the syntax:
find_objects scope
-pattern search_ pattern
[-object_type <model | inst | port | supply_port | net | process>]
[-direction <in | out | inout>]
[-transitive [<TRUE | FALSE>]]
[-regexp | -exact]
[-ignore_case]
[-non_leaf | -leaf_only]
[ -traverse_macros]
• When you specify the -traverse_macros option, the traversal stops at a standard cell
and hard macro boundaries.
• If the -traverse_macros option is specified, then -transitive TRUE is implicitly
specified.
• The -traverse_macros option is supported only for -object_type model | inst
• VCS NLP issues a warning message when you specify object type ( -object_type)
other than model | inst . For example:
find_objects . -pattern in1 -object_type port -traverse_macros

Searching Specified Scope and Its Descendant Hierarchy
Following is the sample warning message:
Warning - [UPF_FIND_OBJECTS_TRAVERSE_MACROS_INVALID_OBJECT_TYPE]
Invalid object type for -traverse_macros option
File - ./soft_macro.upf: Line No - 41
Option -traverse_macros can be specified only with '-object_type
model/inst' in command 'find_objects'. The option will be ignored.
'-traverse_macros' can be specified only with '-object_type
model/inst'.
• VCS NLP issues a warning message when object type ( -object_type) is not
specified. For example:
find_objects . -pattern ret_i* -traverse_macros
Following is the sample warning message:
Warning - [UPF_FIND_OBJECTS_TRAVERSE_MACROS_DEFAULT] Only return some
objects when -object_type isn't specified
File - ./soft_macro.upf: Line No - 45
By default, instances, named processes, logic ports, and nets are
returned when -object_type is not specified. When -traverse_macros is
specified, tool continues to return the default types outside macros,
but returns only objects of type 'instance' inside macros.

MID3 are scopes:

Support for Two Input Supply MUX in PG Function Expression
VCS NLP supports specifying expressions in the pg_function attribute of a liberty cell.
The expression is a 2:1 MUX where the select is a signal pin and the two data inputs are

Support for Two Input Supply MUX in PG Function Expression
PG pins. The MUX pg_function support is only implemented for two input supply MUX
power switch with a select pin.
For example, the following figure shows a single liberty cell with two input supplies at the
top, and signal pins at the left and right. The two green power switches are internal to the
liberty definition.
Following are the examples of the pg_function expression specification in the liberty file:
pg_pin (vdda) { … } pg_pin (vddb) { … }
pin (s1) { … }
pg_pin (vddc) {
direction : internal;
pg_function : "(s1 vdda)+(!s1 vddb)";
switch_function : "1"
}

pg_pin (vdda) { … } pg_pin (vddb) { … }
pin (s2) { … } pin (s2) { … }
pg_pin (vddc) {
direction : internal;
pg_function : "(s1 vdda)+(!s1 vddb)";
switch_function : "s2"
}
The following are the invalid scenarios:
Scenario-1: AND function is not allowed in the pg_function expression.
pg_pin (va) { … } pg_pin (vb) { … }
pin (s1) { … }

Support for Two Input Supply MUX in PG Function Expression
pg_pin (vc) {
direction : internal;
pg_function : "s1 & va"; /* AND function not allowed */
}
Scenario-2: Switch function name cannot be same as the pin name in the pg_function
expression.
pg_pin (va) { … } pg_pin (vb) { … }
pin (s2) { … }
pg_pin (vc) {
direction : internal ;
pg_function : "(s1 va)+(!s1 vb)";
switch_function : "s1" /* same as pg_function not allowed */
}
• You can specify the pg_function attribute without switch_function on a PG pin.
• You can specify both signal pin and PG pin in the pg_function boolean expression.
• The signal pin and PG pin number specified in the pg_function has no limitation.
However, at least 1 PG pin is required.
• The PG pin specified in the pg_function is not limited to primary or backup power/
ground; It can be internal power/ground.
• This feature is supported only for Verilog DB cells.
• The MUX pg_function when successfully processed is logged in the
library_mapping.rpt file.
Following is the sample report:
PG Function : ((VDD && LS) || (VDDA && ~(LS))) : MUX Function : Select

Instrumentation for pg_function Attribute
The instrumentation for pg_function attribute takes the following scenarios into
consideration:
• Scenario-1: PG pin is power aware and wire type with HDL drivers
In this case, the wire value is used to drive the stage, and voltage is driven by MUX as
inferred from the liberty file.
• Scenario-2: PG pin is power aware and wire type with no HDL drivers
In this case, the PG pin gets the supply_net_type value from the inferred MUX, and
the wire value is a VCT version of the supply_net_type value.

Simulation Control Commands Support
• Scenario-3: PG pin is power aware and supply_net_type with HDL drivers
In this case, the inferred MUX is not instrumented and the supply_net_type value is
used as is.
• Scenario-4: PG pin is power aware and supply_net_type with no HDL drivers
In this case, the supply_net_type value is driven by inferred MUX instrumentation.
• Scenario-5: PG pin is not power aware
In this case, the supply_net_type node is added and the supply_net_type value is
driven by inferred MUX instrumentation.
Simulation Control Commands Support
This section describes the sim_corruption_control, sim_assertion_control, and
sim_replay_control simulation control commands in the following sections:
• Using the sim_corruption_control Command
• Using the sim_assertion_control Command
• Using the sim_replay_control Command
Using the sim_corruption_control Command
The sim_corruption_control command allows you to turn off corruption semantics for
specific set of design elements. This command allows behavioral modules (for example,
real number modules) to operate correctly in a low power environment. This command is
only applicable for functional verification.
The following is the syntax of the sim_corruption_control command:
sim_corruption_control
[-elements element_list]
[-model model_name]
When -elements is specified, the elements shall be a list of variables, registers, signals
of the specified hierarchical instances. If the element is an instance, then by default the
command applies to all objects defined in that instance and all dependent subtrees.
Wildcards are supported with this option.
When -model is specified, only names that are declared in the model can be referenced
in the -elements option, and all names are interpreted relative to the topmost scope of
the model. You must use this option along with the -elements option, otherwise VCS NLP
issues an error message.

Simulation Control Commands Support
When -elements is specified along with -model, then the specified elements should be
local to the model.
set_port_attributes -ports {in_bus} -driver_supply
PD3_primary sim_corruption_control -elements {in_bus} -model {top}
Following are the limitations of this command:
• This command does not apply to modules instantiated by the bind_checker
• Bit select with -elements is not supported.
• The following options are not supported:
-type, -exclude_elements, -domain, and -transitive
Using the sim_assertion_control Command
The sim_assertion_control command provides a mechanism to disable assertions
during low power verification. This enables the use of non-power-aware assertions in a
power-aware environment. This command is only applicable for simulation.
The sim_assertion_control for each assertion is active when the primary supply of the
domain in which that assertion is instantiated is not NORMAL and becomes inactive when
the primary supply returns to NORMAL simstate.
The following is the syntax of the sim_assertion_control command:
sim_assertion_control
[-domain domain_name]
[-type <reset>]
If -domain is specified, then assertions and instances that are part of the specified domain
are included.
The -type option determines the type of assertion control. The following type is
supported:
reset - Assertions are suspended and reset when the sim_assertion_control is active
and re-enabled when the it becomes inactive. The reset clears the assertions of any
internal state and sequences.
The following command selects all assertions inside the instances that belong to domain
PD1.

Simulation Control Commands Support
sim_assertion_control -domain PD1 -type reset
Following are the limitations of this command:
• The sim_assertion_control command does not apply to assertions within instances
instantiated by the bind_checker command.
• The following options are not supported:
-type kill , -elements, -transitive, -model, -control_expr,
-controlling_domain
Using the sim_replay_control Command
The sim_replay_control command specifies the list of initial blocks which needs to be
replayed when the power is restored after it has been switched off. This command is only
applicable for simulation.
Each initial block targeted by this command is replayed when the primary supply set of the
domain that contains the initial block transitions into the NORMAL state.
The sim_replay_control command provides the ability to reinitialize logic in behavioral
modules of ROM’s or PLL’s during power state transitions in low power simulation.
The following is the syntax of the sim_replay_control command:
sim_replay_control
[-elements element_list ]
[-exclude_elements exclude_list]
[-model model_name]
[-domain domain_name]
The -elements option specifies a specific list of initial blocks and/or instances. If the
element is a named initial block, the command applies to the specified block. The element
is referenced by the hierarchical path and label of the statement. If the element is an
instance, then by default the command applies to all initial blocks defined in that instance
and all dependent subtrees.

The -exclude_elements option can be used to exclude specific initial blocks or instances.
If the element is an instance, then by default all initial blocks defined within that instance
and its dependent subtree are excluded.
If the -domain option is specified, then only initial blocks and instances in the element

Support for Excluding Instances from a Power Domain
When -model is specified, only names that are declared in the model can be referenced
in the arguments to this command, and all names are interpreted relative to the topmost
scope of the model.
VCS NLP issues error message for the following cases:
• Instance specified in the -elements list is already covered by a sim_replay_control
command with -model.
• If neither -elements, -model, nor -domain is specified.
The following command selects all initial blocks whose label starts with L, but excludes
those blocks whose label starts with L1:
sim_replay_control
-elements [find_objects . -pattern "L*" -object_type process]
-exclude_elements [find_objects . -pattern "L1*" -object_type process]
The following command selects all initial blocks inside the modules that belong to domain
PD1:
sim_replay_control -domain PD1
The following command selects all initial blocks labeled InstX/block1 in the module
modA:
sim_replay_control -model modA -elements InstX/block1
Following are the limitations of this command:
• This command does not apply to modules instantiated by the bind_checker
• The following options are not supported:
-transitive, -controlling_domain
Support for Excluding Instances from a Power Domain
VCS NLP supports the -exclude_elements option with the create_power_domain
command. Following is the syntax:
create_power_domain domain_name
[-elements element_list]
[ -exclude_elements exclude_list ]
[-update]

Support for Excluding Instances from a Power Domain
Where, -exclude_elements specifies the list of the design elements to exclude from
the effective element list (set of elements to which the command applies). The effective
element list is constructed from the arguments provided to the command.
When create_power_domain -exclude_elements option is specified, elements listed in
-exclude_elements are not considered as part of the power domain. For example, for the
following command, the effective element list is { A B/b2 B/b3 … } :
create_power_domain PD -elements {A B/*} -exclude_elements {B/b1}
• VCS NLP issues the following error message when the excluded elements does not
belong to any other power domain:
Error-[UPF_EXCLUDED_ELEMENT_NOT_IN_ANY_POWERDOMAIN] Excluded element
not in any power domain
• VCS NLP allows you to specify duplicated elements in the -exclude_elements
list. For example, the following command contains duplicated element B in the
-exclude_elements list:
create_power_domain PD -elements {A B} -exclude_elements {B B}
• Wildcards are supported in the -exclude_elements list. For example,
create_power_domain PD -elements {A B/*} -exclude_elements {B/*}
• You can specify empty elements list for the -exclude_elements option. For example,
create_power_domain PD -elements {A B} -exclude_elements {}
• VCS NLP issues an error message when the elements specified in the
-exclude_elements option are not part of the current design. For example, VCS NLP
issues an error message for the following command as the element C is not found in
the design.
create_power_domain PD -elements {A B} -exclude_elements {C}
• All elements specified with the -exclude_elements option must be part of any other
power domain, else VCS NLP issues an error message. For example, VCS NLP issues
an error message for the following command because element A is not part of any
other power domain:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -elements {. A} -exclude_elements {A}
The following command is legal because element A belongs to the power domain PD_A:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -elements {. A} -exclude_elements {A}
create_power_domain PD_A -elements {A}

Support for Overriding Design Connection With UPF Connection on a Power Switch
Acknowledgment Signal
VCS NLP issues an error message for the following command because power domain
of A/a1 is not specified:
create_power_domain PD_TOP -elements {.}
create_power_domain PD_A -elements {A A/a*} -exclude_elements {A/a1}
• When the -exclude_elements option is specified with the -update option, the power
domain is updated to exclude elements listed in the -exclude_elements option. The
effective element list is computed when all UPF commands are read. For example, for
the following commands, effective element list is {A}.
create_power_domain PD -elements {A}
create_power_domain PD -exclude_elements {B} -update
create_power_domain PD -elements {B} -update
• VCS NLP allows you to specify multiple -exclude_elements and -update options. For
example, for the following commands, effective element list is {A}.
create_power_domain PD -elements {A B C}
create_power_domain PD -exclude_elements {B} -update
create_power_domain PD -exclude_elements {C} -update
create_power_domain PD -exclude_elements {C} -update
• The -exclude_elements option works with empty power domain. For example, for the
following commands, effective element list is {A}.
create_power_domain PD -elements {} // empty power domain
create_power_domain PD -exclude_elements {B} -update
create_power_domain PD -exclude_elements {C} -update
create_power_domain PD -elements {A B C} -update

Support for UPF Power-Aware Converters
In the above example, there are four instances of module bloc in the design and three
power switches in the UPF whose acknowledgment ports are driven from the design (with
a continuous assignment).
When you use the -power=disable_ack_design_driver option at compile time, VCS
NLP disables the HDL driver for acknowledgment ports.
Following are the limitations of this feature:
• XMR driver is not supported
• Partition Compile is not supported
• The following scenarios are not supported when acknowledgment port is an input port:
◦ Interface modport in highconn of the input port
◦ XMR in highconn of the input port
◦ Struct member in highconn of the input port
Support for UPF Power-Aware Converters
The following sections describe the support for UPF power-aware converters:
• Introduction
Converter modules convert signal values from one type to another. There will be no
specification of liberty for converter modules. A converter module has two scalar ports of
two different types (input and output). A converter is instantiated between a port and the
signal that is connected at the high-conn of the port connection.
One of the major challenges during simulation in presence of UPF is to correctly simulate
the converter modules that are inserted by the tool at real-logic boundaries. For a logic-to-
real converter, when a logic signal information is sent to a block, the corresponding supply
(that is, power, ground) associated with that logic signal should play a role to determine
the real number value.

Support for UPF Power-Aware Converters
On the other hand, for a real-to-logic converter, when the real output pin changes its value,
the corresponding supply associated with this pin should be considered to convert the real
number value to corresponding logic value.
VCS supports UPF power-aware converters. The following sections describe how the
converter modules behave in presence of the power sources defined in UPF.
This feature is enabled by default. However, you must specify all the relevant options
that are required for inserting converter modules. For more information, refer to the VCS
Converters section in the VCS User Guide.
If you want to disable the feature, use the following compile-time option:
%vcs -power=disable_supply_aware_converter
Supply-Aware Converter Module
You must provide a converter module whose conversion functionality depends on two
SystemVerilog variables declared locally inside the module. The attributes of the two
variables are snps_cm_power and snps_cm_ground respectively. These two local
variables should be of type UPF::supply_net_type.

the module. Following is the converter module example:

variable has an attribute snps_cm_power and the other variable has snps_cm_ground.
If the above converter module is instantiated in the UPF power-managed region (under
UPF power-top), the local initializations are removed, and the two variables are driven

Following are the limitations of this feature:
• SPA/SRSN as supply is not supported.
• Merged-mode insertion is not supported.
• Super-bidir adapters and local converters are not supported.
• Inout converters+FGP is not supported.
• To have more correct simulation behavior, the -coerce option should be used.

Heterogeneous fanout is a cross-domain net that drives multiple fanouts with different
sink supplies. This feature enables VCS NLP to insert isolation cells in the extent of the
location domain rather than the exact logical hierarchy of the domain boundary.
With this support, the isolation strategy with the -sink or -diff_supply_only option
inserts isolation cells when the fanouts have different supplies and the location is self/
parent.
For example, the following case is supported for isolation heterogeneous fanout support:
set_isolation iso1 -domain PDB1 -location parent -applies_to output -sink
ss1
set_isolation iso2 -domain PDB1 -location parent -applies_to output -sink
ss2
To enable this feature, you must set the design attribute hetero_fanout_isolation to
TRUE as follows:
set_design_attributes -elements {.} -attribute {hetero_fanout_isolation
TRUE}

ation iso2 -domain PDB1 -location parent -applies_to output -sink
ss2
To enable this feature, you must set the design attribute hetero_fanout_isolation to
TRUE as follows:
set_design_attributes -elements {.} -attribute {hetero_fanout_isolation
TRUE}
The attribute must be specified for the top design instance. If the attribute is specified
anywhere in the UPF (for any scope), then it must be defined also for the top scope with
the same value. VCS NLP issues an error message if the attribute value from a block is
different from the value specified for the top.

Isolation Insertion on Heterogeneous Fanout Paths
The following points describe the support for isolation insertion on heterogeneous fanout
paths:
• This feature improves the granularity of the set_isolation -sink/-
diff_supply_only option. Also, this support changes the isolation conflict resolution
by allowing two isolation strategies to have the same options other than -sink/-
diff_supply_only.
• VCS NLP can insert isolation cells wherever they deem fit as long as they do not
violate the isolation constraints. Also, heterogeneous fanout support does not insert
isolation cells as less as possible.
• The heterogeneous fanout isolation cells can be inserted at any hierarchy boundary
provided that they reside at the power domain specified by the strategy (and do not
cross the power domain).
• Each path is isolated by its highest precedence strategy (assuming all filters are
satisfied) only, otherwise it is not isolated.
• If isolation insertion is not possible due to the location violating the filters, a lower-
precedence strategy is not applied (-diff_supply_only/self, no filters/parent/self).
• The following warning message is issued when the highest precedence strategy is not
applied due to the location violating the -diff_supply_only/-source/-sink filters.
Warning-[UPF_ISO_HETEROGENEOUS_FANOUTS] Isolation skipped due to
hetero fanout
• The heterogeneous fanout isolation cells from the -applies_to input strategy can be
closer to the output of the power domain boundary than the input.
• An error message is issued if both conservative_diff_supply_isolation and
hetero_fanout_isolation are enabled. Following is the sample error message:
Error-[UPF_ATTRS_CONFLICT] Conflicting design attributes specified
./test.upf, 4
Attribute 'conservative_diff_supply_only_isolation' conflicts with
attribute 'hetero_fanout_isolation' specified at ./test.upf, 2.
Please remove one of the conflicting attributes.
• The -diff_supply_only option adds a criteria to filter isolation at sinks. Therefore, the
heterogeneous fanout isolation cell insertion results can be changed with this option.

set_isolation iso2 -domain TOP -location self -applies_to input -sink ss2

Example-2
Inserted isolation cells should not violate isolation constraints for all paths. The following
example shows an alternate insertion point:
set_isolation iso1 -domain PDB1 -location parent -applies_to output -sink
ss1
set_isolation iso2 -domain PDB1 -location parent -applies_to output -sink
ss2
Example-3
Heterogeneous fanout support does not insert isolation cells as less as possible. In the
following example, VCS NLP does not insert ISO2 cell before the fork instead of two cells
because it is located far away from the domain boundary (1 or 2 ISOs).

set_isolation iso1 -domain TOP -location self -sink ss1 -elements {B1}
-applies_boundary lower
set_isolation iso2 -domain TOP -location self -sink ss2 -elements {B1}
-applies_boundary lower
Example-4
For a slightly different design (but the same UPF), ISO2 can be inserted either at M1(as
depicted above) or inside M2.
set_isolation iso1 -domain TOP -location self -sink ss1 -elements {B1}
-applies_boundary lower

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
set_isolation iso2 -domain TOP -location self -sink ss2 -elements {B1}
-applies_boundary lower
Example-5
set_isolation iso1 -pd PDB1 -sink ss3 -no_isolation
set_isolation iso2 -pd PDB1 -diff_only -location parent
• The strategy iso1 has no isolation for -sink ss3 .
• Strategy iso2 is applicable on both paths.
• Strategy iso1 is the highest precedence strategy for path A->B.
• Only the path A->C is isolated with iso2.
Example-6

set_isolation iso1 -domain PDB1 -diff_supply_only true -parent
set_isolation iso2 -domain PDB1 -sink ss2 -no_isolation
• The isolation iso1 is applied on A->E since it is the highest precedence strategy.
• The strategy iso2 (no_iso) is applicable on paths A->C and A->D.
• Strategy iso1 is the highest precedence strategy for the path A->B. However, it cannot
be applied since it would violate the -no_isolation requirement on paths A->C and A-
>D.
• A warning message is issued for the path A->B since it remains unisolated.
VCS NLP compile-time reports are dumped by default inside the mvsim_native_reports
directory. For large designs, a lot of information is dumped in each of these reports
resulting in large file sizes. However, you may not need all the reports for diagnostic
purposes. Therefore, this leads to performance degradation and resource utilization.
You can use the -power_report=<switch> compile option to control the dumping of
reports. You can use this option to enable or disable the reports that are dumped in the low
power analysis stage based on your requirement.
This feature improves compile performance for large designs by dumping only the required
reports. Also, you can the disable dumping of all reports by default in the regression mode.

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
The following topics describe this feature in detail:
• Enabling and Disabling Dumping of Individual Reports
• Enabling and Disabling Report Groups
• Precedence Details
• Supported Reports
• Examples
The following is the use model:
% vcs design.v -upf design.upf -sverilog -power_report=<switch>
All reports will have a separate switch name that can be passed to -power_report=
prefixed with either the - sign to disable the report or the + sign to enable the report.
If an invalid switch name is provided, VCS NLP issues a warning message with
the NLP-UNKNOWN-PWR-RPT-OPT tag. If multiple switch names are provided and
one of them is an invalid option, then the warning message is printed only for
the invalid option. The remaining switches are processed without any issues.
Enabling and Disabling Dumping of Individual Reports
This section describes how to enable and disable the dumping of individual reports
using switch. Following is the use model to enable/disable the dumping of the individual
reports:
% vcs -power_report=+/-<report_name>
Examples:
-power_report=+db_inside_db
Enables the dumping of the db_inside_db.rpt files inside the mvsim_native_reports
directory during compilation.
-power_report=-db_inside_db
Disables the dumping of the db_inside_db.rpt files inside the mvsim_native_reports
directory during compilation.

Multiple reports can be enabled/disabled to control individual report dumping. For
example,
-power_report=-srsn_spa_association-upf_supply_net-upf_supply_port
Disables the dumping of the srsn_spa_association.rpt, upf_supply_net.rpt,
and upf_supply_port.rpt files inside the mvsim_native_reports directory during
compilation.
-power_report=new_isolation_association-upf_supply_source
Dumps the new_isolation_association.rpt report that is disabled by default and
disables the upf_supply_source.rpt report that is dumped by default.
Enabling and Disabling Report Groups
The -power_report=<switch> option also provides the feature to enable/disable a group
of reports by passing a single switch. The reports are classified under the following groups
to enable/disable a group of reports:
Group Name Description Group Name
Customer Consumable (CC) Reports used by the users all
NONE Allows you to disable all reports none
DIAG All diagnostic Reports all_diag
STATS Includes profiling reports and reports
containing statistics
stats
SNAPSHOT Includes the snapshot reports snapshot
Using the group feature, you do not have to pass individual reports to the switch. Instead,
the group name can be passed. Following is the use model:
% vcs -power_report=+/-<group_name>
Examples:
-power_report=-all_diag
Disables the dumping of all the diagnostic reports which are dumped by default.
-power_report=stats or -power_report=+stats
Enables the dumping of all the profiling reports and reports containing statistics details.

Precedence Details
The -power_report=<switch> option follows a predefined order in which the switches
are processed. Groups take the lowest precedence, and individual reports have the
highest precedence.
Consider the following case:
% vcs design.v -upf design.upf -power_report=-all_diag+latch_inference
+flop_inference -sverilog
This compile command shows the design being compiled by disabling the all_diag
group and enabling the flop_inference.rpt and latch_inference.rpt reports. These
reports belong to the diagnostic group. The -power_report= feature follows precedence
order and dumps flop_inference.rpt and latch_inference.rpt reports during
compilation.
The following table shows the precedence order for groups:
Group Name Group Name Precedence
Customer Consumable (CC) all 0
NONE none 1
DIAG all_diag 2
STATS stats 2
SNAPSHOT snapshot 2
The following are the key points considered for precedence:
• The CC group has the least precedence regardless of it being prefixed with + (to
enable the group) or - (to disable the group). That is + and - are processed in the
same way. For example,
-power_report=all, -power_report=+all, or -power_report=-all
Enables the dumping of all the CC reports. The all group will not honor the disable (-
sign) option.
• Next in the precedence order is the NONE group. This group too does not honor + and
-. That is, regardless of it being prefixed with + or - it will have the same precedence.
• Next in the precedence order is the remaining groups having precedence number 2.
Here, prefixing the switch name of the group with - will have higher precedence than

prefixing the switch name of the group with +. Groups having the same number have
equal precedence.
• Finally, the individual reports will have the highest precedence. Here too, prefixing the
switch name of the report with - will have higher precedence than prefixing the switch
name of the report with +.

-power_report=stats
All reports in the STATS group are dumped.

All reports in the STATS group except lp_sig_tree_stats.rpt are dumped. The reason
is that the individual reports have higher precedence than groups.
-power_report=lp_sig_tree_stats-stats
All STATS reports are disabled except lp_sig_tree_stats.rpt. This is because the
individual reports have higher precedence than groups. Note that even though disable has
higher precedence, the precedence of individual reports will have higher priority in this
case.
-power_report=all-stats
All reports that belong to the CC group are dumped and reports of the STATS group are
disabled. If there is any report that belongs to both groups, it is disabled because the
STATS group has higher precedence than the CC group.

-power_report=-all+stats
All the CC and STATS group reports are dumped. The CC group does not honor - sign.
-power_report=+all_diag-snapshot
In this case, all diagnostic reports are dumped, and the snapshot reports are disabled.
Both these groups have equal precedence. Hence, if there is a report that belongs to both
groups, then it is disabled since disable has higher precedence.
-power_report=stats-stats
All STATS reports are disabled due to the higher precedence of - sign. This case is not
valid for CC and NONE groups.
-power_report=upf_supply_source-+-lp_sig_tree_stats--+stats
If multiple signs are passed, the immediate sign before the report name or
group name is taken into consideration. That is, the above option is equal to
-power_report=upf_supply_source-lp_sig_tree_stats+stats.

Semantics of the create_logic_net Command
The create_logic_net command creates a wire type net in the scope of the command.
This command accepts a simple name for a net. If the same name net already exists,
then VCS checks its type. If the type of existing net is one of logic, reg, or wire, then it is
the implementation of the UPF net specified in the command. The existing net must be a
scalar of a compatible type (logic, reg, or wire).

Table 45 create_logic_net Command
Purpose Define a logic net
Syntax create_logic_net net_name
Arguments net_name. Specifies a simple name.
Return value Return an empty string if successful. If not, issue a TCL_ERROR.
If the net type is not compatible or is not a scalar, then VCS reports an error message
when the command is processed during UPF reading. If the net type of the existing net is
compatible and is a scalar, then VCS issues a warning message, considers the existing
net as the implementation of the UPF net, and uses the existing net wherever the UPF net
is used.

Semantics of the connect_logic_net Command
The connect_logic_net command is used to establish a connection between a logic
net and a port. This command accepts a simple name for a net in the current scope.
Hierarchical net names are not allowed.
Table 49 connect_logic_net Command
Purpose Connect a logic net to logic ports.
Syntax connect_logic_net net_name-ports port_list[-reconnect]
Arguments net_name: Specifies a simple name.
-ports port_list : Specifies a list of ports on the interface of the current
scope and/or on instances that are located in the current scope and its
descendants.
-reconnect: Allows a port that is already driven by a constant representing a
default value to be driven instead of control signal net_name.
Return value Return an empty string if successful. If not, issue a TCL_ERROR.
Without -reconnect
If -reconnect is not specified, then
• If the port is in the same scope, then it should not have a lowconn connection.
• If the port is in the lower scope, then it should not have a hiconn connection.
If the connection is already existing, then VCS issues a warning message and ignores the
connect_logic_net command.
With -reconnect
When the -reconnect option is specified, VCS issues a warning message and overrides
the existing connection when the lower scope port has a hiconn connection or the same
scope port has a lowconn connection.
