Support for the sim_assertion_control -control_expr Command
The sim_assertion_control command is a UPF 3.1 command that allows you to control
the behavior of user-defined assertions during low-power verification in a domain or
instance.
VCS NLP now supports the -control_expr option with the sim_assertion_control
command. You must use the -power=sac_ctrl_expr compile option to enable this
feature. Following is the syntax:
sim_assertion_control
[-domain domain_name]
[-control_expr boolean_expression]
[-type <reset | suspend | kill>]
The following sections describe the semantics of these commands:
Any other option specified with the sim_assertion_control command is parsed and
ignored.
• The -type option determines the type of assertion control when the command is
active/inactive:
suspend — Assertions are suspended when sim_assertion_control is active, and
re-enabled when sim_assertion_control becomes inactive.
reset — Assertions are suspended and reset when sim_assertion_control is active
and re-enabled when sim_assertion_control becomes inactive. The reset clears the
assertions of any internal state and sequences.
kill — Assertions are killed when sim_assertion_control is active and the
assertions are not re-enabled or reset.
• The -control_expr option allows you to control all assertions in the design. Consider
the following command:
sim_assertion_control -domain Island_pd_gated -type reset

Support for the sim_assertion_control -control_expr Command
This command disables all the assertions that are started in this power domain as soon
as the power goes down. Once the power comes back, the assertions are restarted.
However, it might take a few cycles for signals to be stabilized and could still be X.
Therefore, if the assertions start immediately on wake-up, it can still cause failures.
The -control_expr option provides another way, where you can delay enabling the

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
er, it might take a few cycles for signals to be stabilized and could still be X.
Therefore, if the assertions start immediately on wake-up, it can still cause failures.
The -control_expr option provides another way, where you can delay enabling the
assertions until signals are stabilized after power-up.
When this option is specified, the sim_assertion_control command is controlled
by the Boolean value of the expression. If the expression evaluates to TRUE, the
command is active and when it evaluates to FALSE, the command goes inactive. When
the command is active, the assertions controlled by sim_assertion_control are
disabled.
sim_assertion_control -type suspend -control_expr a&&b
For the above command, assertion control is active with type KILL for all power
domains when the control expression a&&b becomes TRUE. When activated, all
assertions in those domains get suspended and are resumed when the control
expression a&&b becomes FALSE.
The sim_assertion_control command can be specified globally or on a particular
domain. The global specification can be overridden by a domain-level specification.
Consider the following commands:
1. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD1}
2. sim_assertion_control -type suspend
3. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD2}
The first and third commands enable the assertion control on PD1 and PD2. The second
command specifies the assertion control type as suspend globally on all domains, but
this does not override the domain-level specification in the other two commands as the
domain-level specification takes priority over the global specification.
The same override semantics are applied even in the presence of -control_expr.
Some commands can use domain state, and some can use -control_expr for
controlling assertions. Consider the following commands:
1. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD1}
2. sim_assertion_control -type suspend -control_expr {a == 1'b1}
3. sim_assertion_control -type reset -domain {PD2} -control_expr {b ==
1'b1}
In the above example, assertions in PD1 are controlled by domain state (command
1) and assertions in PD2 are controlled by expression b == 1'b1 (command 3).
Assertions in all other domains are controlled with the expression a == 1'b1
(command 2).

Support for the sim_assertion_control -control_expr Command
Following are the limitations of the sim_assertion_control -control_expr command
support:
• Using UPF logic nets or logic ports in -control_expr is not supported.
• Using power state expressions in -control_expr is not supported.

Overriding Default Bindings
This chapter describes how to override VHDL default bindings using an externally-supplied
file.
This chapter consists of following sections:
• Introduction
VCS allows you set bindings for every instance of a component, or for just one instance,
using a single line.
Suppose your design uses mainly VHDL, and you need to substitute certain instances
with modules from a different library. This other library can be a SPICE library, or a Verilog,
SystemVerilog, or another VHDL library. The standard method is to create a VHDL
configuration. This configuration must include explicit bindings for each component and
instance that you want to change from the default. If these components are located in
many places in your design, the configuration must go through much of the design. This
can make the process complex and hard to manage.
Similarly, specifying architecture other than the most recently analyzed architecture for a
default binding of a given component, the current method is complex.
To avoid errors from nested VHDL configuration syntax, use the -vhdl_bind_override
filename compile-time option to override the default VHDL binding.
This option is described in the following use model.

Chapter 22: Overriding Default Bindings
The option to override default bindings is as follows:
You can use the -vhdl_bind_override filename compile-time option to override default
binding in VHDL. You can apply it to all instances of a component, or to a single unit
(either a VHDL entity or a Verilog module) within a chosen logical library.
Specify non-default bindings using a subset of the Verilog 2K syntax, excluding everything,
except cell and a subset of the use clause.
This option reads the commands from filename, as follows:
cell [orig_library_name.] name liblist library_name [library_name ]
This command uses the library names followed by liblist when creating a default
binding for instances of component name. If present, restrict this to bindings in
orig_library_name.
cell [orig_library_name.] name use [library_name.] entity_name
[(arch_name)]
Same as the command mentioned above, except bind to entity_name. If arch_name is
present, then use it as the architecture, instead of the most recently analyzed architecture.
Examples:
• cell adder use lib1.adder
• cell lib2.adder liblist lib1 lib2
• Only one -vhdl_bind_override command is supported.
For example, vcs <other options> -vhdl_bind_override filename
• If the override file contains two commands for the same component, the first command
takes priority.
• Extended identifiers in the file are supported.
For example, cell adder use lib1.\adder__leaf\
• Comments can be added in the file ( -- or /* - */ ).

Chapter 22: Overriding Default Bindings
The following are the limitations of overriding default bindings:
• Overriding library or entity bindings is not supported for VHDL entities instantiated from
Verilog.
• Currently, only cell-based command is supported. Instance-based command override is
not supported.

You must pass the sv keyword to the $set_gate_level_monitoring system task to
monitor SystemVerilog datatypes in SystemVerilog designs. If you want to dump SAIF

Usage Examples
Enabling SystemVerilog SAIF Dumping Using System Task
The following example shows how to dump SAIF file for SystemVerilog using the
$set_gate_level_monitoring system task:
$set_gate_level_monitoring("rtl_on", "sv");
$set_toggle_region(top);

$toggle_start;
a = 0;
#2 a = 1;
$toggle_stop;
$toggle_report("new.saif", 1e-9, top);

Enabling SystemVerilog SAIF Dumping Using UCLI Command
The following example shows how to dump SAIF file for SystemVerilog using UCLI
command:
% simv -ucli
ucli% power -gate_level on sv
ucli% power <scope>
ucli% power -enable
ucli% run 100
ucli% power -disable
ucli% power -report <saif_filename> <timeUnit> <modulename>
ucli% quit
Supported SystemVerilog Data Types
The following SystemVerilog data types are supported in the SAIF file:
• Integer data types: byte, int, shortint, longint
• Logic, bit
• Enum type

Support for SimProfile Signal Based Profile View

FGP Features
This chapter explains how to use the FGP features in this release, in the following
sections:

Low Activity Event Profiler
Events Per Cycle (EPC) impacts simulation performance, particularly with FGP when
run with higher number of threads. Event activity is one of the primary limiting factor for
FGP performance. The low event activity can be test or design specific. You can use the
low EPC profiler to identify the sources of low event activity, and to explore the scope for
addressing them to improve event activity.
The use model is as follows:
•
-lowepcprof
% vcs <test_name>.v -sverilog -lowepcprof
• % simv -lowepcprof=lowEPCth:N[ optional]+ maxLowEPCevts:N[ optional]
•
lowEPCthN
lowEPCth:N:This sub-option profiles all the time cycles with number of events less
than the threshold number N, where N is an integer value. The default value of N is
1000.
•
maxLowEPCevtsN
maxLowEPCevts: Here, N is an integer value and the default value of N is 100.This sub-
option reports only the top N events.
•-lowepcprof
•-lowepcprof=lowEPCth:20+maxLowEPCevts:200
•-lowepcprof=lowEPCth:10

Chapter 25: FGP Features

Please compile with '-lowepcprof' to enable low EPC profiler at
run time.

VCS Performance Tuning Using Dynamic
Performance Optimizer (DPO)
VCS performance is an important aspect that impacts the verification and project time
lines. Traditionally, simulation performance has been a function of CPU performance,
memory efficiency, and serial algorithm. VCS has multiple options to improve the simulator
performance depending on certain characteristics of the design environment that is being
compiled and simulated. These options allow you to identify performance bottlenecks
and tune the command-line arguments and/or coding styles to extract best possible
performance.
Dynamic Performance Optimizer (DPO) is an intelligent automated approach that
enables necessary diagnostics during VCS compile and simulation and leverages AI to
recommend the appropriate set of options for enabling maximum performance without
manual intervention.
DPO supports performance analysis of the full regression or multiple tests per simv.
Enabling DPO With VCS
DPO is enabled by adding the -dpo option to the vcs compile command line. DPO specific
options are enabled using the -dpo_opts <option=value> option. For the complete list
of DPO options, see DPO Options.
-dpo is ignored when specified inside arguments passed to -f/-F/-file. This
option should explicitly be passed on the vcs command line.
DPO Flow
Typical DPO flow involves the following two steps:
Step-1: Learn and Merge
Learn — This step performs analysis and stores learnings/recommendations in the
database. The -dpo_opts mode=learn option at the compile time enables Learn mode.

title: 6 connectmodules
text:
DPO Options
Merge — This step merges the learnings across the designs/tests. This step is mandatory
for applying the learnings. For more information, refer to Merging Learn Databases.
Step-2: Apply
Apply — Learnings/Recommendations are fetched from the merged database and applied
automatically. This step is enabled by default when the -dpo_opts mode option is not
specified or when the -dpo_opts mode=apply option is explicitly specified.
The Apply mode is valid only when a merged learn database is available.
The recommended usage is to run all designs/tests in Learn mode once and then merge
the learnings. You can switch to Apply mode for all subsequent runs.
DPO Options

default configuration values. Table 51 describes the DPO options.

Supported Apps
You can specify multiple DPO options in the following two ways:
Separate -dpo_opts for each option
% vcs -dpo -dpo_opts <option1>=<value> -dpo_opts <option2>=<value> …
Using ‘+’ as the option separator
% vcs -dpo -dpo_opts <option1=value> +<option2=value> …
By default, the DPO options specified at vcs stage are used by simv.
If any DPO option is specified at simulation, the option values specified at compile are
overridden.
Supported Apps
The following Apps are supported in the current release of DPO:
• plilearn
Analyzes and optimizes the debug/PLI capabilities to set at compile to improve the
simulation performance.
• gates_sk
Explores the scope to improve simulation performance for the gate-level simulations.
• tbopt
Explores potential for simulation performance improvement for the UVM-based
environments.
• ctopt
Analyzes and suggests the options to improve the compile-time.
• fgp
Explores the applicability of the FGP technology for the given design environment
and suggests necessary capabilities to set at compile time to improve simulation
performance.
• lint

Supported Apps
The DPO Lint or Option Recommender (lint) App tries to optimize the simulator
performance by recommending the following:
◦ Removal of command-line options that are not performance friendly.
◦ Addition of certain options that optimize/constrain the default behavior/functionality
of VCS for better performance.
◦ Turning OFF certain default behavior/functionality either coming from language or
simulator.
You can use the -dpo_opts apps=lint compile option to enable this App.
• upfopt
The Low Power or UPF (upfopt)App suggests the options to improve the performance
of the UPF enabled simulation environment. You can use the -dpo_opts apps=upfopt
compile option to enable this App.
• pgates
The Partition Gates (pgates)app suggests the gate-level partitioning options to
improve the compile time. You can use the -dpo_opts apps=pgates compile option to
enable this feature.
• gates_ml
The Gates ML (gates_ml) app utilizes Machine Learning (ML) to explore the scope
and to improve simulation performance for the gate-level simulations. Multiple ML
models predict the potential based on the data generated during the learn simulation.
Usage of multiple models increases the reliability of prediction. You can use the
-dpo_opts apps=gates_ml compile option to enable this app. For more information,
refer to Gates ML App.
• gate_keeper
The Gate Keeper (gate_keeper) app parses all options passed to vcs/simv through
command line/-f/-F/-file or nested files and dumps them in vcs_args.json/
simv_args.json inside dpo_workdir. It provides flexibility to monitor a vcs/simv
option with a user script and exit or warn at compile/simulation in its presence.
You can enable the gate keeper app using -dpo_opts in command line. For more
information, refer to Gate Keeper App.
• mg_help
Identifies the necessary Backward Compatibility IDs (BCIDs) during the release
migration. For more information, refer to Migration Helper App.

Design Tag and Test Name
• Automg
The VCS Release Migration Helper (automg) app automates the process of iterative

• Automg
The VCS Release Migration Helper (automg) app automates the process of iterative
refinement of BCID/MHIDs during VCS release migration to ease the migration effort.
You can use -dpo_opts apps=automg on the vcs command line to enable the automg

◦ The lint, upfopt, and pgates Apps must be explicitly enabled using the
-dpo_opts apps=<apps> compile option in both learn and apply modes.
◦ The fgp App is ON by default in the learn mode, and must be explicitly enabled in
the apply mode.
Design Tag and Test Name
The DPO design_tag and test_name options allow you to distinguish the compile and
simulation respectively.
You must make sure that every design is compiled or every unique simulation executable
(simv) built has a unique design tag.
Following is the syntax to set the design tag:
-dpo_opts design_tag=<design name>
If design tag is not set, the default design tag dpo_design is used.
Test name can be set using any of the following runtime options:
Table 52 Runtime Options to Set Test Name
Option Priority
-dpo_opts test_name=<test name>
+DPO_TESTNAME=<test name>
+UVM_TESTNAME=<test name>
+OVM_TESTNAME=<test name>
-cm_test <test name>
-cm_name <test name>
Highest
Default (dpo_default_test) Lowest

Design Tag and Test Name
Test name must contain only alphanumeric and/or special characters except '\',
'?', '*', '$', '(', ')', '/', '&' with maximum length of 255. DPO internally replaces the
forbidden special characters specified in the name, if any, with an underscore
'_'.
Getting the Desired Test Name
You can use the test_type dpo option to override the default priority order of picking
test_name. Following is the use model:
-dpo_opts test_type=<dpo|uvm|ovm|cm_test|cm_name>
dpo – Selects the test name from +DPO_TESTNAME if it is specified, otherwise default order
of priority is used.
uvm – Selects the test name from +UVM_TESTNAME if it is specified, otherwise default order
of priority is used.
ovm – Selects the test name from +OVM_TESTNAME if it is specified, otherwise default order
of priority is used.
cm_test – Selects the test name from -cm_test if it is specified, otherwise default order of
priority is used.
cm_name – Selects the test name from -cm_name if it is specified, otherwise default order of
priority is used.
• If test_type is specified and if the relevant argument is missing, the default order is
considered.
• If test_type is not specified, the default order is considered.
• Specifying -dpo_opts test_name in simulation command line overrides all above,
omitting test_type.

The dporg utility allows you to merge the learn database, dump recommendations into a
csv file, and generate HTML report using the following options:
• merge: Merges learn databases. For more information, see Merging Learn Databases.
• dump: Dumps recommendations for lint and upfopt apps. For more information, see
Dumping Recommendations to the csv File.
• report: Generates HTML report. For more information, see Generating HTML Report.
◦ Each driver should be invoked separately.
You can use the dporg utility as follows:
% $VCS_HOME/bin/dporg <merge/dump/report> <sub-options>

Reviewing and Enabling Recommendations
The following sections are applicable to the lint and upfopt apps and describe the
recommendation review and enable process in detail:
• Merging Databases and Dumping Recommendations

Reviewing and Enabling Recommendations
Merging Databases and Dumping Recommendations
The DPO Report Generator (dporg utility) supports merging the databases and dumping
the recommendations to the CSV file. You can use the following commands to merge the
database and dump recommendations.
% $VCS_HOME/bin/dporg merge -dpo_dbdir
% $VCS_HOME/bin/dporg dump -d dpo_dbdir
You can dump the following two csv files with the dump command:
• dpo_reco.csv
• dpo_reco_detail.csv (use the -detail option with the dump command)
◦ The dpo_reco_detail.csv file must be used only for reviewing the
recommendations.
◦ The dpo_reco.csv file must be reviewed and updated before passing it to the apply
stage.

Sample Content of the dpo_reco_detail.csv File
Detail recommendation file is useful to review the recommendation per test. The
_AT_LEAST_ONE_ entry in the testname or test_variant column of the dpo_reco.csv

recommendation.
Enabling the recommendation in such scenarios might potentially lead to errors during the

captures the recommendations per test and decide if a particular recommendation should
be enabled. Sample content of the dpo_reco_detail.csv file is as follows:

Reviewing and Enabling Recommendations
lint,REMOVE,"[['-assert','enable_diag']]",dpo_design,
test1,1,Yes,vcs,"['RT', 'CT']",None,Assertion,Remove heavy assertion
debug flag for regressions

to improve sim performance
Enable/Disable Recommendations in Apply Mode
You must review the dumped CSV file after the learn phase and modify the value
of column enable (Y/N) to have either Y or N. If you want to enable a particular
recommendation, then the value of the field enable (Y/N) must be set to Y. If it is set to N,
then the App considers it as a disabled recommendation.
These feedbacks can be passed to App using either of the following:
• Through the DPO configuration file using the -dpo_opts cfg option. Specify the
recommendations CSV file pointer with App configuration parameter reco_file.
• Through the following DPO option reco_file:
-dpo_opts reco_file=<path_to_reco_csv_file>
◦ Priority is given to the -dpo_opts reco_file option.
◦ If no -dpo_opts reco_file or config options are passed in the Apply phase,
recommendations that are ON by default are applied.
Following is the sample content of DPO configuration file. You can specify reco_file
either at app_configs (applies reco_file globally) or at app as follows:
app_configs:
reco_file : <dpo_reco.csv>
lint:
reco_file : <dpo_reco.csv>
upfopt:
reco_file : <dpo_reco.csv>
The reco_file entry under the app section gets higher priority over the entry under the
app_configs section. For an entry under the app section, only the recommendations
specific to the App are picked from the CSV file.
Dumping recommendations for user review and update is currently enabled for
the lint and upfopt Apps only.

Configuration File
Configuration File
Optional configuration file can be specified by using the -dpo_opts cfg=<config file
path> option to set the necessary DPO specific logging modes, and App parameters to
override any default values for Apps.
The following sections describe this feature in detail:
• Configuration File Syntax
• Supported Message Logging Modes
• Supported App Configuration Variables
Configuration File Syntax
Following is the configuration file syntax (YAML format ^^):
app_configs:
<Message Logger variables>
< app1_name>:
<app specific config variables>
<config>: <path to app specific config file with
config variables> **
<app2_name>:
<app specific config variables>
<config>: <path to app specific config file with
config variables> **
All variables are specified in the key: value format.
^^ YAML mandates four white spaces for every indentation. Do not use <tab>.
** You can also choose to specify the variable values in an App-specific configuration file
(YAML format).
Sample Configuration File
Following is the sample configuration file:
Example 133 Sample Configuration File
log_output: file
log_level: error
plilearn:
ELAPSED_TIME_THRESHOLD: 600
fgp:
config: /home/cfg_files/fgp_config.yaml

Configuration File
Following is the sample fgp_config.yaml file:
MAX_NUM_THREADS: 6
Supported Message Logging Modes
Messaging is primarily configurable using log_level to choose the severity and
log_output to choose the target for logging. Specify logging related variables in the
app_configs: section of the configuration file. Following is the syntax:
log_level: <info/warning/error> (info is default)
• info: Report messages with info, warning, error severity
• warning: Report messages with warning and error severity
• error: Report messages with error severity
log_output: <stdout/file/quiet> (file is default)
Table 56 Supported Message Logging Modes
Mode Target
file (default) info/warning/error to stdout and dpo_workdir log files
stdout info/warning/error to stdout only
quiet info/warning/error to dpo_workdir log files only
Messages logged to stdout are also captured in the user-specified vcs/simv
log files.

DPO Messages
Recommendations from Learn Mode and action taken during Apply mode are logged to
compile and simulation logs by default.
Learn Mode:
[DPO][APP_MGR] [INFO] DPO mode is set to 'learn'.
[DPO][PLILEARN] [INFO] RECOMMENDATION: NO ACCESS PERFORMED during
simulation. User pli tab files have access capabilities specified.
Please use the updated plilearn tab file with '+applylearn+'.
[DPO][GATES_SK] [INFO] RECOMMENDATION: Potential for improving simulation
time with GATES_SK. Add '-hsopt=gates' as compile command option.

DPO Messages
Apply Mode:
[DPO][APP_MGR] [INFO] DPO mode is set to 'apply'.
[DPO][PLILEARN] [INFO] [PLI MERGE] 'PLI_MERGE_MODE' is set to
'MERGE_ALL'. Considering pli tab files from all learn records in DB.
[DPO][APP_MGR] [INFO] Compile Options: Added:
['+applylearn+<path>/dpo_demo__dpo_pli_merged.tab', '-hsopt=gates'
The following points explain the format of the DPO messages:
• [DPO]: Indicates that the message comes from DPO.
• [APP_MGR]/[<DPO App>]/[<DPO utility>] : Indicates which phase or utility of DPO
is currently running, whether it is app manager, DPO apps, or DPO utilities.
• [INFO]: Indicates severity of the message (info, error, or warning).
• "String": Displays message content.
Following are the DPO message examples:
• [DPO][APP_MGR] [INFO]: DPO mode is set to 'learn'.
The message indicates the DPO mode, whether it is set to Learn or Apply.
• [DPO][CTOPT] [INFO] NO RECOMMENDATION: Elapsed time 5.41 sec for
compile is under the threshold of 100 sec.
The message indicates no recommendation and provides details about the elapsed
time for compile.
• [DPO][DBMERGE] [INFO] DB Merge Summary: Total Input Records = 6,
Records Merged = 6. All records merged successfully.
The message provides the database merge summary.
• [DPO][DBMIGRATE] [INFO] DB Migration Summary: Total Input Records =
1, Records Migrated = 0 and Records NOT migrated = 1. Refer to the
warning/error(s) in /slowfs/vgcs19/snps/IVP_DPO/REGR/probe/6/update/
td/1/db_migrate.log.
The message displays the database migration summary.
• [DPO][DPORG] [INFO] Dpo Dashboard created as …
The message displays details related to the DPO report generation.

Reference Mode for Performance Comparison
Reference Mode for Performance Comparison
Reference mode is an optional step to compile/simulate the design with the DPO enabled
and to capture the performance data into the database. Performance data can then be
compared between the Reference and Apply modes using dporg.
• Reference mode is turned ON using the -dpo_opts apps=vcsgd compile option. No
performance overhead is incurred in reference mode.
• You can choose to have a separate database directory for reference using the
-dpo_opts dbdir=<ref_db_name> compile option.
• Value of DPO options design_tag/test_name must be same as in the Learn/Apply
modes for the corresponding design.
• You can also optionally tag the run using the DPO option user_tag to uniquely identify
the record in the database as reference.
Gates ML App
The Gates ML (gates_ml) app utilizes Machine Learning (ML) to explore the scope and to
improve simulation performance for the gate-level simulations. Multiple ML models predict
the potential based on the data generated during the learn simulation.
Usage of multiple models increases the reliability of prediction. You can use the
-dpo_opts apps=gates_ml compile option to enable this app.
Following is the use model:
% vcs -dpo -dpo_opts apps=gates_ml <other vcs options>
When gates_ml app is enabled, DPO starts analyzing/optimizing for possible designs.
After the Learn run, you must dump the dpo_reco.csv file using the dporg utility to review
the recommendation, as follows:
In the Apply run, the -dpo_opts reco_file=dpo_reco.csv command is passed to the
command line.
For more information, see Reviewing and Enabling Recommendations.
Gate Keeper App
The Gate Keeper (gate_keeper) app parses all options passed to vcs/simv through the
command line/-f/-F/-file or nested files and makes them available to be processed by

Gate Keeper App
the user script on the fly. It provides flexibility to monitor for one or more vcs/simv options
with a user script and exit or warn at compile/simulation in their presence.
The generated vcs/simv options file in JSON format is passed as input to the user script
with --args_in option. User script is invoked by gate_keeper app as <user_script> --
args_in <args JSON file> .
• User script can be written in any language (python, csh, and so on).
• Ensure that the user script has executable permission before launching vcs/simv with
gate_keeper app enabled.
• User script can read in the args file and do the necessary processing.
• To exit the vcs/simv process from the user script, call exit(1).
Following is the use model:
1. Mention the local script paths for vcs and simv under app_configs, as follows:
% cat cfg
app_configs:
gate_keeper:
vcs_user_script: <User script to monitor/process compile
time options>
simv_user_script: <User script to monitor/process runtime
options>
2. Enable the gate_keeper app using -dpo_opts in command line, as follows:
% vcs <other vcs options> -dpo -dpo_opts apps=gate_keeper+cfg =<path to
config file>
Example: Monitor the VCS options for existence of -debug_access+all and quit compile
if found.
% cat vcs_opts.csh

#!/bin/csh

set args = $argv[2]
echo "ARGS file: $args"
grep "\-debug_access+all" $args
if ($status == 0) then
echo "\nERROR: Option -debug_access+all found. Exit VCS compile.\n"
exit(1)
endif

% cat cfg

DB Migration Utility
app_configs:
gate_keeper:
vcs_user_script: vcs_opts.csh
simv_user_script: simv_opts.csh

% vcs test.v -dpo -dpo_opts apps=gate_keeper+cfg=cfg -lca +nospecify
-debug_access+all

DB Migration Utility
The DB migration utility (dpo_db_migrate) allows you to update the existing learn db
(from older version) to the current version without the need to re-learn.
Following is the use model:
dpo_db_migrate [-h] [-d DB_DIR] [-f filelist] [-l logfile]
-d - Specifies the comma separated list of DB directories
-f - Specifies the list of DB directories in a file
-l - Specifies the log file

Plilearn App
• By default, the migrated databases are available in the original directory. DPO saves
the old databases at the database directory level in a new directory <basename>.old/.
All the old .db files are renamed with an extension .db.old.
• If DB migration tool ran on a DB, which has already migrated to the supported version,
DPO issues an info message and will not run any migration.
• When the existing DB version is older than the currently supported tool version, the tool
automatically migrates up.
Plilearn App
The plilearn app supports the following four modes or types of PLI Learn supported by
VCS:
+vcs+learn+pli Enables the module level PLI learn.
+vcs+learn+pli+instpli Enables the instance level PLI learn.
+vcs+learn+pli+sigpli Enables signal PLI learn at the module level.
+vcs+learn+pli+sigpli
+vcs+learn+pli+instpli
Enables signal PLI learn at the instance level.
You can configure the required PLI Learn mode for a design run using the following dpo
option:
-dpo_opts cfg=dpo_plilearn.cfg
PLI_LEARN_MODE is the configuration variable that decides the type of PLI Learn mode for
a design run. It accepts the following valid values:
MODULE_PLI [Default mode] Generates module PLI tab file.
INSTANCE_PLI Generates instance PLI tab file.
MODULE_SIGNAL_PLI Generates module signal PLI tab file.
INSTANCE_SIGNAL_PLI Generates instance signal PLI tab file.
The dpo_plilearn.cfg file contains the following content:
app_configs:
log_level: info

Automg App
log_output: stdout
plilearn:
PLI_LEARN_MODE: MODULE_SIGNAL_PLI
The default PLI_LEARN_MODE is MODULE_PLI. When the PLI Learn mode is not specified in
the cfg file, then the DPO plilearn app generates the module pli tab file.
Incremental Learn Support
The plilearn app is enhanced to run on a set of new or updated tests to incrementally
learn the pli access capability requirement and update the existing learn database. The
incremental learn feature is enabled using the incr_learn dpo option. This option can be
enabled only when the dpo mode is set to learn (mode=learn). If this option is enabled, the
run is considered as incremental learn.
Following is the use model:
% vcs -sverilog test.v -dpo -dpo_opts mode=learn -dpo_opts apps=plilearn
-dpo_opts incr_learn
This feature supports the following flow:
1. Run full regressions in LEARN mode.
2. Continue to run in APPLY mode until RTL/TB changes requiring additional pli access
capabilities come in. When RTL/TB changes, new tests get added and/or existing tests
are updated resulting in the need for additional PLI access capabilities.
3. Run new or set of updated tests with incremental learn for the plilearn app and
generate new learn data.
4. Merge the incremental learnings using dporg merge to update the learn database.
5. Once the learn data is merged, DPO considers the pli learn tab files from step 3 and
step 1 for next apply run.
6. Back to step 2.
This allows you to run a subset of tests to quickly update the learn database ensuring that
the new or updated tests do not fail in the apply regression due to insufficient pli access
capabilities in the learn db.
Automg App
Automg app helps automate the process of iterative refinement of BCID/MHIDs during
VCS release migration to ease the migration effort.

Automg App
BCID provides functionality-related backward compatibility and MHID provides
performance-related backward compatibility. The automg app identifies the appropriate
feature-specific BCIDs and MHIDs automatically for the VCS release migration which
reduces manual effort.
The following is the usage of dpo_automg:
dpo_automg [-h] [-w WORKDIR] [-i] [-b REFERENCE_VERSION] [-u REGID] [-s
{PASS,FAIL}] [-r] -c/--run_script <run script>[--bc_file <bc_file_path>]
[--mh_file <mh_file_path>]
-h/--help displays the help message and text.
-w/--workdir WORKDIR creates automg setup at the specified <dir> instead of the
default directory (default: <current directory>/automg_workdir ).
-i/--init initializes the automg process.
-b/--reference_version REFERENCE_VERSION points to the reference VCS version
where the status of the run_script results in a PASS. For example, 2020.03, 2019.06.
-u/--update REGID provides pointer to the iteration ID. For example, REGID1.
-s/--status {PASS,FAIL} captures status of the run.
-r/--recommendation provides suggestions and the status of the automg process.
--run_script points to the user run script that executes the vcs/simv commands and
updates the status using dpo_automg --update $DPO_REGID --status $run_status
--workdir $AUTOMG_WORKDIR .
--bc_file <bc_file_path> is a pointer to the BCID setup file if already being used in
the reference environment.
--mh_file <mh_file_path> is a pointer to the MHID setup file if already being used in
the reference environment.
The following is the use model:
1. User run script capturing PASS/FAIL status
-dpo_optsapps=automgvcs <other vcs options> -dpo -dpo_opts apps=automg
-lca
simv <other simv options>
MY_STATUS=<user defined pass criteria to return PASS/FAIL>
$VCS_HOME/bin/dpo_automg --update $DPO_REGID --status $MY_STATUS
--workdir <automg workdir path>

Automg App
Sample run_script:
#!/bin/csh
rm -rf csrc simv simv.daidir ucli.key vcs.cfg

vcs test.sv -sverilog -dpo -dpo_opts apps=automg -lca
-l vcs.log
simv -l simv.log
grep 000abcd88000000a simv.log
if ($status == 0) then
set MY_STATUS="PASS"
set MY_STATUS="FAIL"
endif
echo $MY_STATUS
$VCS_HOME/bin/dpo_automg --update $DPO_REGID --status $MY_STATUS
--workdir <automg workdir path>

% dpo_automg --reference_version <passing stream> --run_script <path
to script that launches the run and passes the status of the run back

% dpo_automg --reference_version 2020.12 --run_script ./bm_run.csh --
init

Reference Mode for Performance Comparison
Reference Mode for Performance Comparison
Reference mode is an optional step to compile/simulate the design with the DPO enabled
and to capture the performance data into the database. Performance data can then be
compared between the Reference and Apply modes using dporg.
• Reference mode is turned ON using the -dpo_opts apps=vcsgd compile option. No
performance overhead is incurred in reference mode.
• You can choose to have a separate database directory for reference using the
-dpo_opts dbdir=<ref_db_name> compile option.
• Value of DPO options design_tag/test_name must be same as in the Learn/Apply
modes for the corresponding design.
• You can also optionally tag the run using the DPO option user_tag to uniquely identify
the record in the database as reference.
Gates ML App
The Gates ML (gates_ml) app utilizes Machine Learning (ML) to explore the scope and to
improve simulation performance for the gate-level simulations. Multiple ML models predict
the potential based on the data generated during the learn simulation.
Usage of multiple models increases the reliability of prediction. You can use the
-dpo_opts apps=gates_ml compile option to enable this app.
Following is the use model:
% vcs -dpo -dpo_opts apps=gates_ml <other vcs options>
When gates_ml app is enabled, DPO starts analyzing/optimizing for possible designs.
After the Learn run, you must dump the dpo_reco.csv file using the dporg utility to review
the recommendation, as follows:
In the Apply run, the -dpo_opts reco_file=dpo_reco.csv command is passed to the
command line.
For more information, see Reviewing and Enabling Recommendations.
Gate Keeper App
The Gate Keeper (gate_keeper) app parses all options passed to vcs/simv through the
command line/-f/-F/-file or nested files and makes them available to be processed by

Gate Keeper App
the user script on the fly. It provides flexibility to monitor for one or more vcs/simv options
with a user script and exit or warn at compile/simulation in their presence.
The generated vcs/simv options file in JSON format is passed as input to the user script
with --args_in option. User script is invoked by gate_keeper app as <user_script> --
args_in <args JSON file> .
• User script can be written in any language (python, csh, and so on).
• Ensure that the user script has executable permission before launching vcs/simv with
gate_keeper app enabled.
• User script can read in the args file and do the necessary processing.
• To exit the vcs/simv process from the user script, call exit(1).

time options>

options>

DB Migration Utility
The DB migration utility (dpo_db_migrate) allows you to update the existing learn db
(from older version) to the current version without the need to re-learn.
Following is the use model:
dpo_db_migrate [-h] [-d DB_DIR] [-f filelist] [-l logfile]
-d - Specifies the comma separated list of DB directories
-f - Specifies the list of DB directories in a file
-l - Specifies the log file

Plilearn App
• By default, the migrated databases are available in the original directory. DPO saves
the old databases at the database directory level in a new directory <basename>.old/.
All the old .db files are renamed with an extension .db.old.
• If DB migration tool ran on a DB, which has already migrated to the supported version,
DPO issues an info message and will not run any migration.
• When the existing DB version is older than the currently supported tool version, the tool
automatically migrates up.
Plilearn App
The plilearn app supports the following four modes or types of PLI Learn supported by
VCS:
+vcs+learn+pli Enables the module level PLI learn.
+vcs+learn+pli+instpli Enables the instance level PLI learn.
+vcs+learn+pli+sigpli Enables signal PLI learn at the module level.
+vcs+learn+pli+sigpli
+vcs+learn+pli+instpli
Enables signal PLI learn at the instance level.
You can configure the required PLI Learn mode for a design run using the following dpo
option:
-dpo_opts cfg=dpo_plilearn.cfg
PLI_LEARN_MODE is the configuration variable that decides the type of PLI Learn mode for
a design run. It accepts the following valid values:
MODULE_PLI [Default mode] Generates module PLI tab file.
INSTANCE_PLI Generates instance PLI tab file.
MODULE_SIGNAL_PLI Generates module signal PLI tab file.
INSTANCE_SIGNAL_PLI Generates instance signal PLI tab file.
The dpo_plilearn.cfg file contains the following content:
app_configs:
log_level: info

Automg App
log_output: stdout
plilearn:
PLI_LEARN_MODE: MODULE_SIGNAL_PLI
The default PLI_LEARN_MODE is MODULE_PLI. When the PLI Learn mode is not specified in
the cfg file, then the DPO plilearn app generates the module pli tab file.
Incremental Learn Support
The plilearn app is enhanced to run on a set of new or updated tests to incrementally
learn the pli access capability requirement and update the existing learn database. The
incremental learn feature is enabled using the incr_learn dpo option. This option can be
enabled only when the dpo mode is set to learn (mode=learn). If this option is enabled, the
run is considered as incremental learn.
Following is the use model:
% vcs -sverilog test.v -dpo -dpo_opts mode=learn -dpo_opts apps=plilearn
-dpo_opts incr_learn
This feature supports the following flow:
1. Run full regressions in LEARN mode.
2. Continue to run in APPLY mode until RTL/TB changes requiring additional pli access
capabilities come in. When RTL/TB changes, new tests get added and/or existing tests
are updated resulting in the need for additional PLI access capabilities.
3. Run new or set of updated tests with incremental learn for the plilearn app and
generate new learn data.
4. Merge the incremental learnings using dporg merge to update the learn database.
5. Once the learn data is merged, DPO considers the pli learn tab files from step 3 and
step 1 for next apply run.
6. Back to step 2.
This allows you to run a subset of tests to quickly update the learn database ensuring that
the new or updated tests do not fail in the apply regression due to insufficient pli access
capabilities in the learn db.
Automg App
Automg app helps automate the process of iterative refinement of BCID/MHIDs during
VCS release migration to ease the migration effort.

Automg App
BCID provides functionality-related backward compatibility and MHID provides
performance-related backward compatibility. The automg app identifies the appropriate
feature-specific BCIDs and MHIDs automatically for the VCS release migration which
reduces manual effort.
The following is the usage of dpo_automg:
dpo_automg [-h] [-w WORKDIR] [-i] [-b REFERENCE_VERSION] [-u REGID] [-s
{PASS,FAIL}] [-r] -c/--run_script <run script>[--bc_file <bc_file_path>]
[--mh_file <mh_file_path>]
-h/--help displays the help message and text.
-w/--workdir WORKDIR creates automg setup at the specified <dir> instead of the
default directory (default: <current directory>/automg_workdir ).
-i/--init initializes the automg process.
-b/--reference_version REFERENCE_VERSION points to the reference VCS version
where the status of the run_script results in a PASS. For example, 2020.03, 2019.06.
-u/--update REGID provides pointer to the iteration ID. For example, REGID1.
-s/--status {PASS,FAIL} captures status of the run.
-r/--recommendation provides suggestions and the status of the automg process.
--run_script points to the user run script that executes the vcs/simv commands and
updates the status using dpo_automg --update $DPO_REGID --status $run_status
--workdir $AUTOMG_WORKDIR .
--bc_file <bc_file_path> is a pointer to the BCID setup file if already being used in
the reference environment.

Automg App
Sample run_script:
#!/bin/csh
rm -rf csrc simv simv.daidir ucli.key vcs.cfg

vcs test.sv -sverilog -dpo -dpo_opts apps=automg -lca
-l vcs.log
simv -l simv.log
grep 000abcd88000000a simv.log
if ($status == 0) then
set MY_STATUS="PASS"
set MY_STATUS="FAIL"
endif
echo $MY_STATUS
$VCS_HOME/bin/dpo_automg --update $DPO_REGID --status $MY_STATUS
--workdir <automg workdir path>
2. Initialize DPO automg app
% dpo_automg --reference_version <passing stream> --run_script <path
to script that launches the run and passes the status of the run back
to DPO> --init
Following is the sample command:
% dpo_automg --reference_version 2020.12 --run_script ./bm_run.csh --
init
It generates a wrapper script that launches run_script with different BCID and MHID
setups.
3. Launch the wrapper script
% sh $PWD/automg_workdir/automg_wrapper.sh
It calls run_script automatically for every iteration.

Migration Helper App
Migration Helper App
You can use the Migration Helper (mg_help)app during release migration when you
encounter compile errors in the current VCS release, but passing in the older VCS
release. The DPO mg_help app allows you to quickly identify the necessary BCIDs during
release migration and migrate with ease.
Following is the use model:
% vcs -dpo -dpo_opts apps=mg_help <other vcs options>
If the mg_help app finds any applicable BCIDs, it lists the BCID, provides
recommendation, and generates a BCID file, for example:
[DPO][MG_HELP] [INFO] Recommended BCIDs: 'ASSOC_ARRAY_DELETE_METHOD'
[DPO][MG_HELP] [INFO] RECOMMENDATION: Applicable BCIDs are listed in
'//mg_help_test/mg_help_synopsys_bc.setup' file. Please point the
environment variable SNPS_SIM_BC_CONFIG_FILE to the file and re-compile.
[DPO][MG_HELP] [INFO] Please refer to '//mg_help_test/mg_help_bc.log'
for more information regarding BCIDs.
Once recommendation is manually applied and compile is successful, the mg_help app
issues the following message:
[DPO][MG_HELP] [INFO] NO RECOMMENDATION: VCS compile is successful.
Once the compilation is successful, the subsequent compiles need not enable the
mg_help app.
• DPO is not supported with the following:
◦ Verdi interactive mode
◦ VHDL-top environment
◦ Save/Restore flow
◦ Reverse debug/Checkpoint
• The ctopt App is not supported with Partition Compile (PC)

• Every unique simulation executable (simv) built represents a unique design tag from
DPO perspective. For example, a regression environment with 'N' compiles require 'N'
unique design tags.
• Historical data is saved/retrieved based on the combination of design_tag and
test_name. You must ensure that these variables are set to the same value across
Learn and Apply modes.
• If common DPO database directory ( dbdir) is planned to be used across multiple
designs, ensure each design has unique name specified using the design_tag option.
Otherwise, it is recommended to have a separate database directory per design tag.
• It is recommended to re-learn by enabling Learn mode periodically, if:
◦ Simulation environment has undergone a significant change due to source code
(design/testbench) updates and/or integration of new blocks.
◦ Addition of PLI access capabilities on new modules/signals.
◦ Degradation in simulation performance over the previous runs after any updates to
design/testbench and/or VCS command-line options.
• The plilearn app optimizes PLI access capabilities based on the simulation in the
Learn mode. If the current run in Apply mode requires additional access capabilities, it
is advisable to turn OFF the plilearn app or re-learn by enabling the Learn mode.

Next Generation Parallel Compiler
To improve compile time for a large RTL or GLS design in VCS, use the Next Generation
Parallel Compiler feature with the -parallelcomp option. This method provides significant
compile time reduction through advanced parallelization techniques. Parallel Compile,
• Creates balanced partitions for maximum parallel efficiency.
• Uses lightweight elaboration engines for faster incremental builds.
• Scales automatically as design size increases.
As parallel compile (-parallelcomp) extends partition compile (-partcomp), designs that
use -parallelcomp also inherit the following partition-compile benefits:
• Supports incremental compilation (only modified partitions recompiled).
• Enables shared partition libraries using -partcomp_sharedlib.
• Enables autopartitioning of the design.
• Supports cross-module references (XMRs).
• Supports relocatable databases for sharing compiled partitions.
Parallel Compile enables faster scratch compilation, reduced incremental compile time,
and better memory scalability for large RTL or GLS designs.
Use the -parallelcomp compile option to enable the parallel compiler. Following is the
usage:
vcs -parallelcomp <other_options>
The -parallelcomp option compiles 4 partitions in parallel by default. In larger designs
where the number of partitions is high, the user can override the default 4 parallel
processes by using -parallelcomp=jN, where, N is the required number of parallel
compilations. You can choose N number based on the cores available in the grid. In
addition to this, parallel compile has improved global analysis time and faster elaboration
during the subsequent compilation stages.

Distributed Compilation
Every next generation, the increase in size of SOCs impacts the time and memory it takes
to build them.
VCS partition compile technology helps resolve this issue by dividing the big SOCs into
smaller partitions and compiling them in parallel. It scales well by increasing the number
of partitions as SOC size increases, keeping per partition compile time and memory pretty
much the same with every next generation. However, this parallelism is ultimately limited
by the number of available cores and total available memory on a single machine. In other
words, even with partition compile technology, with the increasing size of SOC, compile
time is not scalable as parallelism is limited by available resources on a single machine. In
order to realize the full potential of parallelism, one has to upgrade the compute farm with
more cores and more memory per machine. This is not cost-effective as one must invest in
new hardware and existing hardware becomes obsolete.
VCS Distributed Compile technology helps realize the full parallelism potential with the
existing compute farm, therefore scaling compile time with ever increasing SOCs without
needing to upgrade the hardware.
VCS Distributed Compile technology allows users to compile different partitions created by
partition compile technology on different machines, thus utilizing the compute farm to its
fullest potential.
This chapter includes the following topics:
• Distributed Compile Configuration File
• Examples of Configuration Files
• Distributed Compile Diagnostic Messages
• Profile Report
• Limitation

Distribute compile is enabled using the options -dist=jN and -dist_cfg=<config file>
on top of regular partition compile technology that is enabled by the option -partcomp.
Use the following command to support distributed compilation:
% vcs -dist=jN -dist_cfg=<configuration_file> -partcomp <other_options>
• -dist=jN: N is the number of partitions to be compiled in parallel.
• -dist_cfg=<configuration_file>: Option to specify json configuration file that
allows user to specify grid commands and other grid related options.

"cdpl":{
"hosts":[

]
}
}

Dynamic Test Loading
Dynamic Test Loading (DTL) is an approach to load and run any test dynamically at any
time during simulation. The test loaded at runtime can include different UVM tests or
sequences.
For detailed information on DTL, refer to Dynamic Test Loading chapter in VCS User
VCS introduces a simplified use model of DTL (2-step) flow, referred to as DTL single-step
flow. This can be enabled using -dtl option. See Use Model section for details on how to
enable DTL single step flow.
Following are the steps to use DTL using simplified single-step flow:
1. Encapsulate all test classes derived from UVM classes in SystemVerilog packages.
2. Compile the test packages using DTL Single-Step Flow. Note that this step is simplified
and fastest way to enable DTL by using -dtl option. Add the -dtl option to the
existing partition compile setup and convert into DTL flow.
◦ Use -dtl=<package_name> at the compile step.
◦ At the compile step, use the -dtl option and the package name that corresponds
to the dynamic test package along with other partition compile options, top module,
and static test package.
% vcs -partcomp DUT base_test_pkg -dir=IP_BASE_TEST
-dtl=test1_pkg,test2_pkg
-partcomp
Enables Partition Compile flow.
-dir
Specify the directory to record the partition database.

Chapter 29: Dynamic Test Loading
-dtl
Enables DTL flow.
◦ DTL single-step flow generates partition database for the static package in the
IP_BASE_TEST directory and generates simulator executable followed by the
compilation of dynamic test packages and reuses the partition database generated
by the static package.
◦ The partitionlib directory for the test package is generated in the following
format:
partitionlib_<test_pkg_name>
This step reuses the partition information as per the -sharedlib option and
simv executable is not generated. You can observe a very fast compilation
for dynamic tests.
3. Simulate base test. Save the Simulation state after the common initial sequence (until
reset_phase in the following example ) of the test is executed.
% simv +UVM_TEST_NAME=base_test -ucli -i save.cmds
save.cmds
UCLI command file.
stop -in uvm_component::post_reset_phase -once -continue -command {run
0; save saveddesign; ; run}
◦ You can use VCS save restore feature using UCLI commands or from the $save/
$restore calls from Verilog code.
◦ When the simulation state is restored, the setup and restore portions are executed
in one continuous simulation.
◦ In case of only one UVM run phase in the test and there are no sub-phases:
The test is saved in the middle of the UVM run_phase of base_test, then at restore
it resumes execution and completes the run_phase of base_test. Once the current
phase execution is completed, UVM switches to the next phase of dyn_test.
◦ For DTL $save and $restore, the UVM run phase must have at least two sub-
phases so that you can save the simulation in one sub-phase, and upon restoration,

Chapter 29: Dynamic Test Loading
the subsequent sub-phase can be triggered for the dynamic test. Hence the
test must have at least two sub-phases to successfully change to the dyn_test
run_phase during the restore operation.
4. Run other tests by dynamically loading the test packages. Restore simulation state
after the common part is over and save on simulation TAT.

time=%0t",test_name,$time);
root.refresh_test(test_name);
In a typical UVM verification environment, dynamic test contents can
perform the following:
◦ Define and launch new sequences.
◦ Extend the post run() built-in phase methods: extract(), check(), finalize().

HyperSim: Hyper-Scaling Simulation
Performance
In the past, simulation speed was limited by CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and
serial algorithms. However, with multicore processors and new vector instruction sets,
simulation productivity has improved.
With more cores and better vector capabilities, HyperSim helps design teams to use
this computing power for faster simulations. This helps to meet the growing demands of
complex verification.
HyperSim offers the following key features:
• Efficient parallelism at the design level, using advanced engines to break down HDL
blocks into flip-flops and latches.
• Enhanced optimizations for large blocks, loops, and vectors to make parallel
processing more efficient.
• Emulation-like behavior to increase event density and improve parallel efficiency.
• A modern parallel engine that schedules and balances simulation tasks during runtime.
• The ability to detect passive simulation elements, such as DPI monitors, and run them
on separate cores.
• The ability to run modern testbench components, such as UVM testbenches, on
separate cores.
HyperSim is included in the APEX licensing package. For additional information,
refer to “VCS Licensing” in the VCS Release Notes.
In addition to the APEX key, HyperSim requires a separate license feature
named VT_JAGUAR. To obtain access to this license key, contact the Synopsys
field team.
The following sections explain how to use HyperSim:
• Design Profiling for HyperSim Technology
• Enabling VCS HyperSim Technology

Design Profiling for HyperSim Technology
• Additional Performance Optimization
• Limitations of HyperSim
Design Profiling for HyperSim Technology
VCS HyperSim technology works best for designs with high activity. VCS provides
diagnostics to help you see if the design is suitable for VCS HyperSim. The tool estimates
performance gains with 4, 8, or 16 cores. It also highlights factors that might limit
parallelism and reduce these gains. You must review these diagnostics and make changes
in your design if possible.
Profiling works with VCS two-step, three-step, single compile, partition compile, and
parallel compile flows. However, for profiling, run the simulation using only one core.
This section consists of the following topics:
• Use Model of Creating Profiling Data
• Content of hypersim.summary
Use Model of Creating Profiling Data
To run diagnostics, use the -diag=hypersim compile-time option during VCS compilation.
The following is the use model for these options:
% vcs -full64 -diag=hypersim <other compile time options>
%./simv
When the simulation completes, the following message confirms that the profiling data is
created:
Generating HyperSim Summary
Info-[JDS-DONE] HyperSim diag summary successfully generated in
hypersim.summary
During simulation, VCS creates intermediate profiling data files and directories.
These include diag_dir, dprof.dir, profileReport, profileReport.txt,
profileReport.html, profileReport.json, and simprofile_dir.
After the simulation ends, VCS uses this data to automatically generate a final summary
file called hypersim.summary. For details about the hypersim.summary file, refer to
Content of hypersim.summary.

Design Profiling for HyperSim Technology
Content of hypersim.summary
The hypersim.summary report includes the following key sections:
• Run Summary
• Design Summary
• Testbench Unblocking Stats
• Low Time-Per-Time Step Stats
Run Summary
This section provides general simulation details such as VCS version, VCS build date,
machine name, simulation time, and clock time. The following figure shows the run
summary section of the hypersim.summary file:
Figure 116 Run summary
Design Summary
This section explains the expected performance gains when running simulations on
4, 8, or 16 cores. The estimated gains are based on comparing the time spent in DUT
components with the time used by non-DUT parts. The non-DUT parts include the UVM
testbench, PLI/DPI tasks, or FSDB dumping.
The section displays the difference between time spent in high-activity design cycles and
low-activity design cycles. For best results, more than 90 percent of the total runtime must
be in DUT execution with over 90 percent of cycles classified as high activity. Use these
numbers as general guidelines.
The following figure displays an example of Design Summary

Design Profiling for HyperSim Technology
Figure 117 Design summary
The design summary consists of the following details:
• Time Summary: It consists of the following three rows:
◦ Time-0: Time spent at time “0” before parallel simulation starts. High values here
limit parallel gains.
◦ DUT + Verification Collateral: Time spent in DUT and passive elements, such
as assertions and DPI, collectively is called verification collateral. Higher values
indicate better speedup potential.
◦ Testbench + other Non-Parallelizable: Time spent in testbench, such as time
spent in classes, monitors, scoreboards, and drivers. This part runs on a single
thread and cannot be parallelized. Keep the value below 10 percent for optimal
performance. For more details on time spent in testbench, refer to Testbench
Unblocking Stats.
• Time-Per-Time Step: A higher percentage in the potential to accelerate row indicates
better parallel performance. To improve this metric, refer to Low Time-Per-Time Step
Stats.

Design Profiling for HyperSim Technology
• Runtime Gain Projections With HyperSim: This displays the potential gain when you
run simulations on 4, 8, or 16 cores.
If the design is not suitable, this section displays the following information:
Figure 118 Runtime Gain Projections With HyperSim
Testbench Unblocking Stats
This section explains features of the UVM testbench. In HyperSim, the UVM or a similar
testbench system runs on the main simulation thread. This main thread also starts
design-level event activities on other threads during the same simulation time step. If the
testbench has too many blocking events, the main thread must wait until each blocking
event is resolved. An example of a blocking event is @(posedge interface.clk) .
Blocking can increase when monitors use a fast interface clock. Blocking can also happen
when there are too many monitors, especially if some monitors are not required for the
test.
This section explains the main causes of this activity and gives more details about where
these performance issues come from. The following figure displays an example:
Figure 119 Testbench unblocking stats
Low Time-Per-Time Step Stats
This section explains the main reasons for low-design activity during a simulation time
step. Review these points to help improve performance with HyperSim. Low activity in a
time step can have many causes. To get better results, address all issues.

Enabling VCS HyperSim Technology
The section organizes these causes into groups. Each group covers one or more related
files. The groups appear with the highest impact at the top and the lowest at the bottom.
This helps you address the most important issues first.
Figure 120 Low time-per-time step stats
The following are key suggestions:
• Avoid using #1 delays in always or forever blocks that run without stopping. It is better
to gate the always block with the relevant signal.
• Designers use PLLs to model analog blocks with high accuracy. For most tests, you
can replace detailed PLL models with slower, behavioral models to simplify simulation.
Enabling VCS HyperSim Technology
After the design is ready, use the following options to enable HyperSim:
Compile-Time Options
• -dut_top_modules=<module_name_or_comma_separated_list_of_module_names>
This option specifies the name of the top-level DUT module or a list of module names
where HyperSim technology is enabled. This option is a mandatory compile-time
Use the module definition name, not the instance name from the testbench.
• -hypersim=bringup_mode
This option enables VCS HyperSim technology. It enables all engines except congruent
mode, passive mode, and testbench mode. You can learn how to enable these modes
in later sections to improve performance. This is a mandatory compile-time option.

Runtime Option
• -hypersim=num_threads:N
This option specifies N cores for distributing events. VCS also uses one extra core for
synchronization and for events that cannot run in parallel. Therefore, if you set N cores,
VCS needs a total of N+1 cores.
VCS HyperSim technology selects cores based on their current load and checks if they
are free from other HyperSim jobs. If VCS cannot find N+1 available cores, it displays
the following affinity error:
Error-[HYPERSIM_AFFINITY_FAILED] cpu_affinity/auto_affinity failed
Failed to allocate CPU cores: Simulation threads requested 29 cores,
but only 24 cores are available in system.
For more details on status of CPU cores, use the runtime option,
-hypersim=diag.
• -hypersim=allow_less_cores
Use the -hypersim=allow_less_cores runtime option with
-hypersim=num_threads:N to choose up to N+1 cores.
If HyperSim cannot secure all N+1 cores, the simulation continues without an affinity
error. However, if no cores are available, HyperSim reports an affinity error.
• -hypersim=min_num_cores:<value>
The -hypersim=min_num_cores:<value> runtime option sets the minimum number of
cores required by simulation. If the number of available cores is less than the value set
by min_num_cores, the simulation stops.
You must use -hypersim=min_num_cores:<value> along with
-hypersim=num_threads:N and -hypersim=allow_less_cores.
Using -hypersim=min_num_cores:<value> without
-hypersim=num_threads:N results in an error. If you
use -hypersim=min_num_cores:<value> without
-hypersim=allow_less_cores, it does not work.
VCS HyperSim offers advanced technologies, for example,
• Congruent mode that improves parallelization
• Passive mode that runs on different threads
• Testbench simulation that runs on its own thread

For more details on the additional performance of HyperSim, refer to the following topics:
• Enabling Congruent Mode to Improve Parallelization
• Enabling Passive Mode
• Enabling Testbench Mode
• Enabling Optimal Debug Performance Mode
Enabling Congruent Mode to Improve Parallelization
The event-driven simulation of Verilog can cause race conditions at the RTL level. This
happens when several parallel processes update signals at the same simulation time,
without a set order. This can lead to results that do not match real hardware behavior.
To avoid this, design teams use nonblocking assignments for sequential logic and blocking
assignments for combinational logic. They also add timing offsets or use structured
clocking to separate data and clock events. These methods ensure predictable simulation
and easier debugging.
Sometimes, adding delays between clock and data to prevent races can slow down
parallel performance. This is because extra time steps are needed to transfer data.
VCS HyperSim congruent mode solves this by removing delays from inferred flip-flops and
latches. It keeps the simulation race-free by sampling the old data value when clock and
data change together. This increases events at clock edges and improves parallelization.
To enable congruent mode for more constructs such as continuous assignment, use the
-hypersim compile-time option.
Remove the -hypersim=bringup_mode option, as it overrides congruent mode.
To disable congruent mode on specific modules, you can use the following configuration
file syntax:
module {<module_name_or_comma_separated_list_of_module_names>}
{noJagCongruency}
Then, add the configuration file with the following compile-time option:
+optconfigfile+<cfg_file_name>
Enabling Passive Mode
Passive elements are parts of your design that only read the simulation state. They do not
change or write to the simulation state.

A module that has only input ports and does not have any output ports is called a passive
element. If the module does not change any value during simulation, either through cross-
module references, or by using a PLI application, it is also considered passive.
The following is an example of a passive module:
module (input a);
always @(a) $display(a);
HyperSim can detect and automatically mark passive modules based on how they are
used.
By default, all DPI functions are considered non-passive. This is because their behavior
in C code is unknown. If you have a DPI function which is passive, you must mark it as
passive in the configuration file.
Use Model to Apply Auto-Inferred Passive Elements
When you use the -hypersim or -hypersim=bringup_mode compile-time option,
HyperSim infers passive modules and creates a file called auto_passive_module.cfg in
the current working directory.
You can use this file in the following two ways:
• Apply auto-inferred passive elements directly.
If you want to apply the auto-inferred passive elements as is, use the following compile-
time option:
-hypersim=passive:apply_auto_module
• Review and edit the file.
If you want to review or edit the file,
◦ Save the file with a new name, such as modified_passive_config.cfg.
◦ Use the following compile-time option in the next compile to apply passive
elements:
+optconfigfile+<modified_passive_config.cfg>
-hypersim=passive:module
For both ways, you must use the following runtime option to enable passive elements
during simulation:
-hypersim=passive

The passive thread uses one core. For example, if you set
-hypersim=num_threads:3, HyperSim uses a total of four cores. One core
runs the main thread, one core runs the passive thread, and the other two cores
run the parallel simulation.
Example of Passive Elements
Consider the following test cases. The checker module is passive because it only has
inputs. The dpi_checker module is also passive if the DPI-C function only reads data.
Test case 1
reg i;
wire o;
dut I1(i, o);

always @(i, 0)
$display("%m [%0t] simulation module i=%0b o=%0b",$time,i,o);
end

i = 0;
repeat (10)
#1 i = ~i;
end
end

module dut(i, o);
input i ;
output o ;

assign o = i;

checker chk(i,o);
dpi_checker dpichk(i,o);

Test case 2

module checker (i,o);
input i, o;

always @(i, 0)

$display("%m [%0t] checker i=%0b o=%0b",$time,i,o);
end

module dpi_checker (i,o) ;
input i, o;

import "DPI" function void displaylogic(logic i, logic o);

always @(i, 0)
displaylogic(i,o);
end
HyperSim infers passive module list as follows:
// List of automatically inferred passive modules

module {checker} {passive};
// Following modules are identified as conditionally passive
// Check if the set of DPI/PLI functions under each module can be
configured as passive
// If all dependent PLI/DPI functions mentioned for a module can be
passive, uncomment all the lines for corresponding module so that it can
be marked as passive

//module {dpi_checker} {passive};
// dpi {displaylogic} {passive};
For this test, HyperSim generates an auto-inferred passive module list as follows:
• The checker module is passive because it only has inputs.
• The dpi_checker module is currently marked as passive. Its entry and associated
DPI functions are commented out. After you confirm that it is truly passive, you can
uncomment these lines and use the following options in your next compilation:
+optconfigfile+<modified file> & -hypersim=passive:module
Deviation From Regular Simulation
The passive thread uses a separate scheduler that is not linked to the main simulation.
The simulation time for the passive thread is different and is always at least one timestamp

behind the main simulation time. This can cause the following differences from a regular
simulation:
• Order of Simulation Log
The simulation logs from the passive thread and the main thread can overlap and are
not sorted by simulation time. For example, a display at time t in the passive thread
might appear after a display at time t+5 in the main thread.
• Difference in Finish Time
If the passive thread stops because of an error, the main thread might continue running
past the error time. As a result, the simulation finish time and the error time might not
be the same.
Enabling Testbench Mode
Modern testbench methods, such as UVM, are widely used. UVM gives design and
verification teams a strong and standard way to work. It supports projects from small IP
blocks to large SoCs. UVM helps teams reuse code by using modular components. It also
makes it easier to create test stimulus with constrained random methods. This leads to
better coverage and higher-quality silicon.
In the default HyperSim flow, UVM-based testbench activities run on the main thread. The
main thread waits until all testbench actions are complete.
With HyperSim testbench mode, testbench activities can run on a separate thread.
DUT activities can run on other threads at the same time. This can improve simulation
performance, especially if the testbench workload is less than 20 percent of the total.
To enable the testbench mode, use the following compile-time option:
-hypersim=tb
HyperSim testbench mode uses one CPU core. For example, if you set
-hypersim=num_threads:3, HyperSim uses 4 cores in total. One core is for
the main thread, one for the testbench thread, and the other two for parallel
Enabling Optimal Debug Performance Mode
Performance and debug instrumentation are closely linked. When you add more debug
features to a design, simulation performance can slow down. In the early block-level
development stages, wide visibility and full read or write access might be required to
identify problems quickly. As the design becomes more stable, keeping this high level
of debug access can cause extra overhead and reduce simulation speed. At the SoC

level, where designs are larger and more complex, this slowdown is even greater. VCS
HyperSim technology is built for large SoC projects. It includes specific features to control
and improve debug options. This provides visibility you need without losing performance.
This section consists of the following topic:
• Sources of Debug Capabilities
• Handling HyperSim-Specific Debug
Sources of Debug Capabilities
You can enable debug capabilities in the following two ways:
• Using command-line options, -debug_access
◦ -debug_access+r: Applies read capability for the entire design.
◦ -debug_access+w: Applies write capability for the entire design.
◦ -debug_access+f: Applies force capability for the entire design.
◦ -debug_access+wn: Applies write-net capability for the entire design.
• Using a PLI tab file
◦ Module-based capabilities
▪ acc=r:chip: Applies read capability to the chip module.
▪ acc=w:ip1,ip2: Applies write capability to the ip1 and ip2 modules.
▪ acc=w:*: Applies write capability to the entire design.
◦ Instance-based capabilities
▪ acc=r:top.chip1: Applies read capability to the top.chip1 instance.
◦ Signal-based capabilities
▪ acc=r:top.chip1.q: Applies read capability to the top.chip1.q signal.
Handling HyperSim-Specific Debug
By default, HyperSim uses the debug capabilities you set on the command line or in the
PLI or VPI tab file.
To improve simulation performance, HyperSim handles debug capabilities in a specific
way. When you use the -hypersim=debug_perf compile-time option, HyperSim limits
debug capabilities—whether you set on the command line or in the tab file—to only
the outputs of sequential elements. HyperSim automatically detects these sequential
elements.

Limitations of HyperSim
For example, in the following always block, HyperSim sees q as the output of a sequential
element. The signals clk, reset, and d are other related signals.
always @ (posedge clk or negedge reset)
if (!reset)
q <=0 ;
q <=d ;
end
When you run the % vcs -hypersim -debug_acc+f test.v command, the force
capability is applied to clk, reset, d, and q.
When you run the % vcs -hypersim -debug_acc+f -hypersim=debug_perf test.v
command, with -hypersim=debug_perf, the force capability is applied only to q.
If you set signal-based debug capabilities in the tab file,
-hypersim=debug_perf still honors them.
Limitations of HyperSim
HyperSim has the following limitations:
• HyperSim does not support the dynamic reconfiguration feature.
• HyperSim does not support SDC.
• The HyperSim testbench flow does not support the save-restore feature.
• HyperSim does not support the reverse debug feature.
• The HyperSim passive flow is disabled in the DTL flow.
• The +vcs+loopreport option disables the HyperSim passive flow.
• HyperSim does not support analog or mixed-signal (AMS) flows.
• Remove the -hypersim=num_threads* option from the runtime options to use
simprofile for simulation profiling.
• Expect the compile time to increase by up to 1.5 times during a scratch compile.
• HyperSim does not support the +allmtm option.
• HyperSim and FGP are both multi‑core technologies. However, HyperSim offers a
wider set of features compared to FGP, as described in the HyperSim: Hyper-Scaling
Simulation Performance section.

Limitations of HyperSim
The -hypersim and -fgp options cannot be used together in the same compilation. If
both options are specified, the compiler reports the following error:
Error-[HYPERSIM_FGP_INCOMPAT] Incompatible options
'-fgp' and '-hypersim' cannot be used together in the same
compilation.

Migration Helper App
You can use the Migration Helper (mg_help)app during release migration when you
encounter compile errors in the current VCS release, but passing in the older VCS
release. The DPO mg_help app allows you to quickly identify the necessary BCIDs during
release migration and migrate with ease.
Following is the use model:
% vcs -dpo -dpo_opts apps=mg_help <other vcs options>
If the mg_help app finds any applicable BCIDs, it lists the BCID, provides
recommendation, and generates a BCID file, for example:
[DPO][MG_HELP] [INFO] Recommended BCIDs: 'ASSOC_ARRAY_DELETE_METHOD'
[DPO][MG_HELP] [INFO] RECOMMENDATION: Applicable BCIDs are listed in
'//mg_help_test/mg_help_synopsys_bc.setup' file. Please point the
environment variable SNPS_SIM_BC_CONFIG_FILE to the file and re-compile.

for more information regarding BCIDs.
Once recommendation is manually applied and compile is successful, the mg_help app
issues the following message:
[DPO][MG_HELP] [INFO] NO RECOMMENDATION: VCS compile is successful.
Once the compilation is successful, the subsequent compiles need not enable the
mg_help app.
• DPO is not supported with the following:
◦ Verdi interactive mode
◦ VHDL-top environment
◦ Save/Restore flow
◦ Reverse debug/Checkpoint
• The ctopt App is not supported with Partition Compile (PC)

• Every unique simulation executable (simv) built represents a unique design tag from
DPO perspective. For example, a regression environment with 'N' compiles require 'N'

• Historical data is saved/retrieved based on the combination of design_tag and

• If common DPO database directory ( dbdir) is planned to be used across multiple

Otherwise, it is recommended to have a separate database directory per design tag.

◦ Simulation environment has undergone a significant change due to source code
(design/testbench) updates and/or integration of new blocks.
◦ Addition of PLI access capabilities on new modules/signals.
◦ Degradation in simulation performance over the previous runs after any updates to
design/testbench and/or VCS command-line options.
• The plilearn app optimizes PLI access capabilities based on the simulation in the
Learn mode. If the current run in Apply mode requires additional access capabilities, it
is advisable to turn OFF the plilearn app or re-learn by enabling the Learn mode.
