Inherited Supply Support for Connect Modules
The ams_cdef_net_cm -inherited_supply command supports inheritance of supply
nets for connect modules. This enhancement allows connect module power and ground
nets to inherit supply values directly through power attributes when port based supply
information is not available. You must specify this option only in the VCS optconfig file.
Automatic Handling of Verilog Force on Mixed-Signal Nets
The behavior of Verilog force/release on a mixed-signal net is enhanced such that the
Verilog force becomes the only driver for the Spice net. That is, in case of a Verilog force,
the force value is sent to the analog side. The analog engine considers it as the only
contribution to the respective Spice net. This force value is maintained on the Spice net
until a Verilog release happens on that mixed-signal net. To enable this feature, you must
use the -adopt msv_force_release compile option.
For more information, refer to “Automatic Handling of Verilog Force on Mixed-Signal Nets”
in the VCS LCA User Guide.
Leaf-Level Verilog-AMS Support in the SystemVerilog-Spice Flow
VCS MSV supports SystemVerilog-Spice flow having a leaf-level Verilog-AMS
(VAMS) module to be used as an electrical instrument. You must use the -adopt
msv_with_leaf_vams compile option to enable the leaf-level Verilog-AMS support. This
feature only supports VAMS block at the leaf level of the hierarchy in the SV-Spice flow.
For more information, refer to “Leaf-Level Verilog-AMS Support in the SystemVerilog-
Spice Flow” in the VCS LCA User Guide.
Super-Net Support for Multi-Voltage Designs
Starting with this release, VCS supports automatic insertion of converter module using the
-xlrm enable_converter compile option. This option allows you to connect a signal to a
port of different type. You must provide the converter modules and converter rules using a
VCS opt-config file.
Also, VCS now allows you to use the ams_cm commands to configure the parameters
of the converters inside a Super-Net. This feature is enabled using the -xlrm
enable_converter compile option.
For more information, refer to “Super-Net Support for Multi-Voltage Designs” in the VCS
LCA User Guide.

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
Support for Scope-Based Type-Coercion
Starting with this release, VCS supports scope-based type-coercion in the RNM designs
using the ams_coercion commands. This feature allows you to confine the effects of type-
coercion to specific parts of the design hierarchy.
For more information, refer to “Support for Scope-Based Type-Coercion” in the VCS LCA
User Guide.
Parameterization of Converters Using Hierarchical Tracing
The enhanced hierarchical tracing feature enables a tracing algorithm that looks upward
for the applicable ams_cm command. It also checks the interconnected segments in the
adjacent hierarchies to handle the feedthrough scenarios.
To enable traversal algorithm, add the following command to the OptConfig file:
ams_converter_parameterization=traversal;
For more information, refer to “Parameterization of Converters Using Hierarchical Tracing”
in the VCS LCA User Guide.
Name Mapping Between SPICE View and Digital View for XMR in RTVS
VCS supports handling of name mapping between the SPICE and digital views of an
RTVS instance. This enhancement only supports X-prefix, case sensitivity, port map, and
bus format consideration for the XMR token resolution between the SPICE and digital
views in RTVS flow.
To enable this feature, use the option: -adopt rtvs_xmr .
For more information, refer to “Name Mapping Between SPICE View and Digital View for
XMR in RTVS” in the VCS LCA User Guide.
Dumping of Attributes Not Understood by VCS
Starting with this release, VCS performs the following:
• Reports all the attributes that are not understood by VCS in a text file, and ignores
them during compilation. VCS also generates warning messages for every occurrence
of the attribute that are not understood by VCS.
• Supports execution of a general-purpose pre elaboration user script.
• Reads the commands generated by the user-defined script before mixed-signal
elaboration.
For more information, refer to “Dumping of Attributes Not Understood by VCS” in “Analog
Mixed Signal Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.

Support for Multiplicity Factor Parameter
The Verilog-AMS LRM defines M-factor as the shunt multiplicity factor of the instance, that
is, the number of identical devices that should be combined in parallel and modeled.
This feature now enables you to specify the definition of the ams_mfactor command in
the optconfigfile file or equivalent Verilog-2001 (V2K) attributes in the netlist directly to
provide hierarchical M-factor information.
For more information, refer to “Support for Multiplicity Factor Parameter” in “Analog Mixed
Signal Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for the Bind Feature in Mixed-Signal Simulation
In the Eldo SPICE netlist format, the .bind command is used to map a sub-circuit with
another sub-circuit. VCS supports this command in the Mixed Signal Verification (MSV)
flow as well.
For more information, refer to “Support for the Bind Feature in Mixed-Signal Simulation” in
“Analog Mixed Signal Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for `worklib and `view Compiler Directives
VCS uses the `worklib and `view compiler directives to compile enclosed modules into
logical libraries.
The `worklib and `view directives enable different modules in the same file, for example,
netlist.vams, to be analyzed into different libraries. Names of the logical libraries are
assumed as a concatenation of the values of the worklib <value> and view <value>
directives through an underscore symbol.
For more information, refer to “Support for `worklib and `view Compiler Directives”in
“Analog Mixed Signal Features”in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
SPICE-Top Support in RTVS
The Real-Time-View-Swapping (RTVS) feature enables you to dynamically switch
between SPICE and Verilog views of a cell at runtime as the simulation progresses. You
can get high simulation accuracy by selecting the SPICE view for certain time windows.
For other time periods, its Verilog view is simulated to get high simulation performance.
This feature supports RTVS instances in the SPICE view and eliminates the restriction to
instantiate the RTVS Verilog and RTVS SPICE views in the Verilog view.
For more information, refer to the “SPICE-Top Support in RTVS” in “Analog Mixed Signals

Support for the ams_cdef_inst Option
The ams_cdef_inst command overrides connectivity to power and ground nets given
from ams_cdef_net commands. This command is used when specific instances in the
designs have different power and ground connections.
For more information, refer to “Connect Definition Commands” in “Analog Mixed Signals
Donut Configuration Support in RTVS
The RTVS feature is enhanced by supporting instantiations of SPICE sub-circuit under the
RTVS Verilog view and Verilog module under the RTVS SPICE view.
For more information, refer to “Donut Configuration Support in RTVS” in “Analog Mixed
Signals Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
UPF Support for SPICE-on-Top Design Configurations
You can use VCS AMS with UPF in a SPICE-on-top design flow. In SPICE-on-top design
topologies, the top level of a design is modeled in analog languages (such as Spice/
Spectre). Digital blocks are instantiated under Spice. In Spice, the supplies are typically
created in the subckt definition only, while the supply network for digital blocks is present
in the UPF file. In such a design configuration, the supply may be generated from Spice
which then is connected to the UPF supply network to propagate supplies to digital blocks
of the design.
For more information, refer to “UPF Support for SPICE-on-Top Design Configurations” in
“Analog Mixed Signals Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for Packed type of Wreal/Nettype/Real/Integer
In Verilog-AMS, the packed vector of nettype/wreal/real/integer is used frequently. Support
for the packed vector of these types is required to compile and simulate generated netlist.
These types are inherently unpacked in nature, so you must convert the packed vector of

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
cked vector of nettype/wreal/real/integer is used frequently. Support
for the packed vector of these types is required to compile and simulate generated netlist.
These types are inherently unpacked in nature, so you must convert the packed vector of
these types to the unpacked array internally.
Starting with this release, the VCS-AMS supports packed vector of net type (both built-in
and user-defined) using the -xlrm nettype_array XLRM option.
For more information, refer to “Support for Packed Type of Wreal/Nettype/Real/Integer” in
“Analog Mixed Signals Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Configuring the Converters through the ams_cm Command
The ams_cm command enables parameter overrides of the datatype converters used in
analog mixed-signal designs and digital mixed-signal designs.
To fine-tune the accuracy of type conversions, it is allowed to override the parameters of a
set of auto-inserted converter instances in the design.

The ams_cm command enables parameter overrides of the datatype converters used in
analog mixed-signal designs and digital mixed-signal designs.
For more information, refer to “Configuring the Converters Through ams_cm Command” in
“Analog Mixed Signals Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Attribute-Based Inherited Connection and Supply Sensitivity
In the Verilog-AMS flow, the interfaces between analog and digital blocks are realized by
automatic insertion of connect modules. To configure a connect module instance, you
need the ability to associate the proper supply information with it. Other than connect
modules, Verilog-AMS users may also need to pass the supply information through the
design hierarchy where the components may not have supply (power, ground) ports.
These functionalities can be supported through inherited connection where you specify
the supply information through attributes in the design. This feature supports an
attribute-based inherited connection solution using the ams_supply, ams_cdef_net, and
ams_cdef_inst commands.
For more information, refer to “Attribute-Based Inherited Connection and Supply
Sensitivity”in “Analog Mixed Signals Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
UPF Support for SPICE-on-Top Design Configurations
In SPICE-on-top design topologies, the top level of a design is modeled in analog
languages (such as Spice/Spectre). Digital blocks are instantiated under the Spice. In
Spice, the supplies are typically created in the subckt definition only, while supply network
for digital blocks is present in the UPF file. In such a design configuration, the supply may
be generated from Spice which may then be connected to the UPF supply network to
propagate supplies to digital blocks of the design.
For more information, refer to UPF Support for SPICE-on-Top Design Configurations” in
“Analog Mixed Signals Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Inherited-Connection-Based Supply Specification for Verilog-AMS Designs
This feature supports supply routing via Verilog-AMS netlist through inherited connection
and associate this supply with the connect module instances and the SPICE or Verilog-
AMS blocks those need this information for simulation purposes.
For more details, refer to “Inherited-Connection-Based Supply Specification for Verilog-
AMS Designs” in “Analog Mixed Signals Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for User Accessible DRS
In order to model a Digital Mixed Signal (DMS) behavior with bidirectional ports, it is
mandatory to differentiate the “external drivers” from the “internal drivers” of a port. This
technology is referred a Driver/Receiver Segregation (DRS), which is default in Verilog-
AMS. The idea is the same as in the concept of DRS in Verilog AMS. DRS requires that

ordinary drivers and loads of a mixed signal be segregated through the digital inout port
of a connect module. Ordinary drivers/loads, also called as external drivers/loads, are
drivers/loads outside the connect module. In contrast, connect drivers/loads, or the internal
drivers/loads are drivers/loads inside the connect module. DRS supports the following:
• All the connect loads will see the resolved value of the external drivers.
• All the external loads will see the resolved value of the connect drivers.
For more details, refer to the “Support for User Accessible DRS section” in “Analog Mixed
Signals Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Bidirectional Converter Support with UPF
System-Verilog does not allow designers to connect a signal to a port if their types are
incompatible. For example, VCS issues "Port-Connection Type Mismatch" error if a wreal
net is connected to a logic port. For the ease of use (under -xlrm enable-converter
option), VCS supports automatic insertion of converter module to bridge up a signal with
a port of incompatible types. You need to provide converter modules and converter-rules
through VCS opt-config file.
For unidirectional conversion (such as logic-to-real or real-to-logic), converter modules
can be developed easily. However, if the dataflow is bidirectional, then developing such
converter is challenging. Besides, bidirectional converters need additional support from the
tool for core-simulation purpose.
For more information, refer to “Bidirectional Converter Support with UPF” in “Analog Mixed
Signals Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for Connect-Module Port Based ams_cm Command
In the Verilog-AMS flow, the interfaces between Analog and Digital blocks are realized
by the automatic insertion of Verilog-AMS connect-modules. These connect-modules are
inserted in the design using the connect-rules.
To fine-tune the Verilog-AMS discipline resolution and connect-module insertion
algorithms, you require the ability to override the disciplines of some net-segments in the
Verilog-AMS design. Along with that, you need to override Verilog-AMS connect-rules and
associated connect-module parameters, and insertion-modes (merge/split). One of the

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
u require the ability to override the disciplines of some net-segments in the
Verilog-AMS design. Along with that, you need to override Verilog-AMS connect-rules and
associated connect-module parameters, and insertion-modes (merge/split). One of the
most common requirements is the ability to override the supply-voltage parameter and the
threshold parameters of a particular or a set of connect-module instances in the design.

Support for Partition Compile in Mixed-Signal Simulation
VCS supports SystemVerilog SPICE design configuration with VCS-XA in partition compile
flow. You can create partitions in two ways:
• User-defined partitions: SPICE cannot be specified as user-defined partitions. By
default, VCS creates one partition for SPICE.
• Auto-partitions: The partitions are automatically created by the tool.
Both, user-defined partitions and auto-partitions are supported in two-step flow and three-
step flow.
This feature is a VCS feature and requires VCS installation. However, you do not need any
VCS licenses or special licenses. Verilog-only users can use the existing licenses for this
feature.
For more information, refer to “Partition Compile Flow” in “Analog Mixed Signals Features”
in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Verilog-AMS Enhancements With Custom Compiler
This section describes the enhancements that fine-tunes the Verilog-AMS discipline
resolution and connectmodule insertion algorithms. Also, commands are introduced to
override Verilog-AMS connect-rules and associated connect-module parameters, and
insertion-modes (merge/split), override the supply-voltage parameter and the threshold
parameters of a particular or a set of connectmodule instances in the design.
For more information, refer to “Hierarchal Configurations of Connect Modules” in “Analog
Mixed Signals Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Bidirectional Converter Module in Mixed-Signal Simulation
In RNM simulation, you can use converters to connect load and drivers of different types.
With Bidirectional converter you can separate the drivers and load from both inside and
outside of the converter module.
For details about this feature, refer to “Bidirectional Converter Module in Mixed-Signal
Simulation”in “Analog Mixed Signals Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
UVM Support for Analog Mixed Signal
UVM Analog Mixed Signal (UVM-AMS) is a UVM application package that is used to verify
analog IPs either at block level or at SoC level in a UVM environment. In addition, UVM-
AMS enables you to create reusable verification environments for Analog Mixed Signal
DUTs.

UVM-AMS comprises a set of built-in base classes, assertions, checkers, and source
generators that help you to,
• Introduce analog verification planning.
• Model your specific traffic shapes.
• Define analog toggle coverage.
• Check protocol consistency of your analog DUT.
• Drive your DUT with a predefined voltage source generator.
• Build a scalable and reusable verification environment by leveraging the SystemVerilog
Testbench language constructs.
For more information, refer to “Overview” in “Introduction” in the UVM Analog Mixed Signal
Connecting Wreal to Nettype
Wreal net behaves as the nettype when the wreal net is connected to any of the
predefined nettypes.
For details about this feature, refer to the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Assertions LCA Features and Enhancements
The following are the Assertions LCA features and enhancements:
• Support for Assertion hier file During Compile Time With MX Flow in Single Compile
• Generating Warning Message for Invalid Signature Path
• Support for Signature-Based Control in Immediate and Concurrent Assertions
• Support for Signature-Based Control in Initial and Final Blocks
• Signature-Based Control for Deferred Assertions and Unique-Case or Priority-Case
Violation Checks
• Enabling Fail-Only Feature
• Support for Dynamic Data Types in Assertions
Support for Assertion hier file During Compile Time With MX Flow in Single Compile
Assertion hier file is supported during compile time with MX flow. This feature improves the
runtime performance.

Generating Warning Message for Invalid Signature Path
VCS generates a warning message, if the static path of the signature is not valid. The
following is the example warning message:
Warning-[RA-INVSTR] Not found in design
"Test.m1.m2.blk2.A1" not found in design. Ignored in "$assertoff".

"tx.v", 21: Test.m1.m2.blk1.A1: started at 0s failed at 0s
Offending 'a'
[Signature: "Test.m1.m2.blk1.A1"]
For more information on this feature, refer to “Generating Warning Message for Invalid
Signature Path” in “Assertion Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for Signature-Based Control in Immediate and Concurrent Assertions
VCS supports signature-based control for immediate and concurrent assertions. VCS
supports the following features for immediate and concurrent assertions:
• Block-level exclusion of assertions
• Using the “*” wildcard character in the regular expressions for exclusion of assertions
For more information on this feature, refer to “Support for Signature-Based Control in
Immediate and Concurrent Assertions” in “Assertion Features” in the VCS LCA Features
Guide.
Support for Signature-Based Control in Initial and Final Blocks
VCS supports signature-based control for assertions in the initial and final blocks. For
example, consider the following code which contains initial block:
Example 1 test.v
module top;

initial begin : INI //Behavioral
for(int i=0;i<1;i++) begin : LOOP
A1: assert final (0);
end
end

endmodule
Following is the simulation output for the above code:
"test.v", 5: top.INI.LOOP.A1: started at 0s failed at 0s
Offending '0'
#0 in top.INI.LOOP.A1 at test.v:5
#1 in loop with i= 0 at test.v:4
[Signature: "top.INI.LOOP[0].A1"]

In the above simulation output, top.INI.LOOP[0].A1 is the signature generated by VCS
for assertion A1 in the initial block.
For more information on this feature, refer to “Support for Signature-Based Control in Initial
and Final Blocks” in “Assertion Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Signature-Based Control for Deferred Assertions and Unique-Case or Priority-Case
Violation Checks
VCS provides an enhanced way to control unique-case or priority-case violation checks
and deferred assertions (labeled assertions) using the “signature” method.
VCS generates a “signature” in addition to the regular assertion message from the
deferred assertions and unique-case or priority-case violation checks.
A signature is a string made up of tokens extracted from the function call stack trace of
assertions, and is separated by dots. You can use signature to enable or disable deferred
assertions and unique-case or priority-case violation checks at compile time or runtime
using the static configuration file.
For more information, refer to “Signature-Based Control “ in Assertion Features” in the
VCS LCA Features Guide.
Enabling Fail-Only Feature
VCS supports the -assert failonly compile-time option which enables fail-only
mode for concurrent assertion. Starting with this release, VCS supports the -assert
select_failonly option that can move the selected assertions or covers to fail-only
mode. Use the following options to move the selected assertions or covers to fail-only
mode:
• auto
• fastcover
• <filename>
where <filename> can be any user-defined ASCII file.
The fail-only mode improves the runtime performance and decreases the runtime memory
requirement.
For more details, refer to “Enabling Fail-Only Feature” in “Assertion Features” in the VCS

Support for Dynamic Data Types in Assertions
VCS supports dynamic data as specified in IEEE Std 1800-2012 Section 16.6 Boolean
expressions by using the -assert allow_dynamic option at compile time. The dynamic
data types supported are as follows:
• String data types
• Dynamic array size and static array value
• Functions on queues ( queue.size() and queue.empty() and static queue values)
• Static class functions and members
For more information, refer to “Support for Dynamic Data Types in Assertions” in
“Assertion Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Compile LCA Features and Enhancements
The following are the Compilation LCA features and enhancements:
• Support for Fast Compilation
• Support Multi-Dimensional Array of Interface/Module Instances and Interface ports
Support for Fast Compilation
VCS has a new compile-time performance optimization called fast compilation that can
be used to reduce compile time for your design (and therefore, to reduce the overall
turnaround time). You can enable fast compilation using the -fastcomp compile-time
option.
There are two levels of fast compilation, specified by the -fastcomp=0 and -fastcomp=1
compile-time options:
• -fastcomp=0 is same as the -fastcomp option (without the argument). This is
the recommended fast compilation mode. This option accelerates the compile
time by suppressing internal optimizations in VCS front end with moderate runtime
degradation.
• -fastcomp=1 is same as the -fastcomp=all option. This option applies more
aggressive compile-time performance than the default mode. However, the runtime
degradation is high compared to the default mode.
The above options are a trade-off between the compile time and the runtime. You can
choose the option based on which performance is more important to you.
For more information, refer to “Fast Compilation” in “Compilation Features” in the VCS

Support Multi-Dimensional Array of Interface/Module Instances and Interface ports
VCS supports multi-dimensional array of interfaces/module instances and interface ports
using the -mda_inst option.
For more information, refer to “Support Multi-Dimensional Array of Interface/Module
Instances and Interface ports” in “Compilation Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Coverage LCA Features and Enhancements
The following are the Coverage LCA features and enhancements:
• Precomputed Scores Mode
• Merging of Identical VDBs
• Support for LRM-Compliant Escaped Identifiers
• Monitoring Coverage for RDC and SDC
• Monitoring FSM Coverage for Multi-Dimensional Arrays

Precomputed Scores Mode
When creating a merged coverage database (VDB), you can direct URG to precompute
scores at the region level. This can significantly speed up Verdi startup time for larger
designs.
For more information, refer to “Precomputed Scores Mode” in the VCS LCA Features
Guide.

Merging of Identical VDBs
When you specify the flex_merge code_union option, VCS Coverage detects the VDBs
that have identical structural constructs and automatically merges them using the basic
merge algorithm. The VDBs with different structural constructs are merged using the
flex_merge code_union option.
The feature is currently under the switch -smart_merge.
For more information, refer to “Merging of Identical VDBs” in “Coverage Features” in the
VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for LRM-Compliant Escaped Identifiers
VCS is enhanced to use escaped identifiers as per the LRM rules using the -cm_instr
lrmnames compile-time switch. In addition, the switch updates the escaped identifiers
already dumped in the coverage database shape and design files.
For more information, refer to “Support for LRM-Compliant Escaped Identifiers” in
“Coverage Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Monitoring Coverage for RDC and SDC
VCS enables you to monitor coverage for Reset Domain Crossing (RDC) and Synopsys
Design Constraints (SDC). To initiate the static flow, use the -static_bug_finding
command at compile time. On the other hand, use the -sdc compile-time switch to enable
coverage computation for SDC.
For more information, refer to “Monitoring Coverage for RDC and SDC” in “Coverage
Monitoring FSM Coverage for Multi-Dimensional Arrays
VCS supports monitoring Finite-State Machine (FSM) coverage for FSMs modeled in
multi-dimensional arrays (MDAs), that is, an array of arrays or an array of arrays of arrays.
To monitor FSM coverage for MDAs, use the -cm_fsmopt mda switch at compile time.
For more details, refer to “Monitoring FSM Coverage for Multi-Dimensional Arrays” in
“Coverage Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Merging Coverage of All Subtrees of a Module
VCS reports the combined score of all its instances of a module in the same hierarchy
instead of showing just individual instances' score. To enable this feature, use the
-modtreefile option at report time.
For more information, refer to “Merging Coverage of All Subtrees of a Module” in
“Coverage Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.

text:
Union Merge of Code Coverage
VCS provides the -flex_merge union switch to enable URG to support a flow where
coverage from both the base and input VDBs are combined for a module, even if the
objects are different, as long as the source code itself has not changed.
For more information, refer to “Union Merge of Code Coverage” in “Coverage Features” in
Excluding Generic Values for Coverage
When generic values are used in conditional expressions, some combinations of values
tracked by VCS for condition coverage may not be possible to cover. You can direct VCS
to try to automatically exclude such condition vectors from coverage monitoring using the
-cm_cond vhdl_noconst_generics switch
For more information, refer to “Excluding Generic Values for Coverage” in “Coverage
Features“ in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Improving Compile Time in the Partition Compile Flow
You may instruct VCS to dump a folded view of a design instead of its elaborated view
during compilation in a partition compile flow. If the total number of instances in a design
is very large and its hierarchical depth is relatively small, the -cm_instr folded_design
switch enables you to improve compile-time performance for the design.
For more information, refer to “Improving Compile Time in the Partition Compile Flow” in
“Coverage Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Plan-Based Grading
Plan-based grading computes a minimized set of test runs for the coverage targets in each
feature in a Verification plan that covers all coverage targets in the features. To use plan-
driven grading, you need a verification plan in an .hvp format and a coverage database
containing the generated coverage data for all the test runs to be graded. To use plan-
based grading, use the -grade plangrade switch with URG.
For more information, refer to “Plan-Based Grading” in “Coverage Features” in the VCS
Unifying Hierarchical Configuration Files
VCS enables you to define a single hierarchical configuration file to control monitoring of
coverage for both code and assertion coverage. To use this feature, specify your hier file
to the -cm_hier switch (compile time) or the -hier switch (URG) as normal, and add the
-cm_common_hier switch to enable the common hier mode.
For more information, refer to “Unifying Hierarchical Configuration Files” in “Coverage

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
Monitoring FSM Coverage for Arrays of Structures
VCS supports monitoring Finite-State Machine (FSM) coverage for FSMs modeled in
fields of structures contained in arrays. For each element of such an array, VCS can detect
the FSM modeled in the structure field and monitor it for coverage computation.
To monitor FSM coverage for FSMs modeled as structure fields in an array of structures,
use the -cm_fsmopt structarr compile-time option with the -cm fsm compile-time
option.
For more information, refer to “Monitoring FSM Coverage for Arrays of Structures” in
“Coverage Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for Procedural Sampling
Echo analyzes procedural context to find targetable coverpoints. Echo supports the
following two aspects of procedural sampling:
• Sampling a non-random variable that is assigned with a targetable random variable.
Echo targets a non-random coverpoint when the non-random variable is assigned with
an expression of random variables.
• Randomizing a sibling class of sampled variables. At runtime, Echo collects targetable
holes from the sibling classes. Echo currently supports only one level of inheritance.
Note that all the variables involved in the expression of a cover point must be inherited
from the targeted base class.
For more information, refer to “Support for Procedural Sampling” in “Coverage Features” in
Crosses With Non-Random Coverpoints
You can target a cross with non-random cover points using Echo. The cross must contain
at least one random cover point.
While collecting Echo targetable cross holes for non-random cover points, VCS ignores
cross-bin combinations with bins that are not sampled. However, if a non-random cover
point is properly sampled during the first few cycles, it is collected as a targetable hole at
the next collection.
If transition bins are involved in cover points that contribute crosses, VCS ignores the
cross bins (including transition bins) when collecting the holes.
For more information, refer to “Crosses With Non-Random Coverpoints” in “Coverage

Enhancements to Echo Procedural Sampling
Echo procedural sampling technique supports the following three new coding styles:
• Sampling a non-random variable that has been assigned a targetable random variable
present as a member of another class.
• Passing a randomized object through function or task parameter.
• Standalone covergroups.
For more information, refer to “Echo Procedural Sampling Enhancement” in “Coverage
VCS NLP LCA Features and Enhancements
The following are the VCS NLP features and enhancements:
• Support for Latch-Type Isolation Cell with Set/Reset Pins
• Support to Allow Internal Direction for Supply Port
• Handling Multiple Connections to Virtual Supplies
• Support for SPA -literal_supply Option
• Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation
• Support for Atomic Power Domains
• Support for Modeling Isolation Cell Without Enable Pin in Liberty
• Tunneling SPICE Supply Ports Through UPF Supply Network
• Creating Custom VCTs for Real Data Types
• Support for the SPA -applies_to Option without -elements
• Support for Type Real Option With the sim_corruption_control Command
• Support for Golden UPF
• Support for Excluding Retention Elements From Retention Strategy
• Setting Attributes on UPF Objects
• Searching Specified Scope and Its Descendant Hierarchy
• Support for Two Input Supply MUX in PG Function Expression
• Support for Excluding Instances from a Power Domain
• Support for UPF Power-Aware Converters

• Heterogeneous Fanout Support
• Controlling NLP Report Dumping
• Support for Logic Port/Net and Connections
• Support for the sim_assertion_control -control_expr Command
Support for Latch-Type Isolation Cell with Set/Reset Pins
VCS NLP allows you to specify the connections for the set/reset pins in the
set_isolation command. This feature allows you to model latch type isolation cells with
asynchronous set/reset pins.
VCS NLP supports the following set_isolation command options to enable this feature:
set_isolation
[-async_set_reset { net_name <high | low>}]
[-async_clamp_value <0 | 1>]
[other options]
For more information, refer to “Support for Latch-Type Isolation Cell with Set/Reset Pins”
in “VCS NLP Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support to Allow Internal Direction for Supply Port
You can use a top level virtual net to connect ports of liberty models with direction :
internal. However, when the liberty model is represented with UPF, you can use a new
direction internal with the create_supply_port command, which gives the equivalent
of direction : internal in a liberty model.
The set of possible values for the -direction option of the create_supply_port
command is enhanced to include value internal. This feature allows seamless switching
between liberty models and UPF models during the design process.
For more information, refer to “Support to Allow Internal Direction for Supply Port ” in “VCS
NLP Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Handling Multiple Connections to Virtual Supplies
Starting with this release, if there are multiple real drivers, you must specify the resolution
for the supply net. If there are only virtual drivers or one real driver along with other virtual
drivers, VCS NLP considers the resolution as parallel.
For example, VCS NLP supports the following usage where VDD_int is a PG pin of a
macro (whose instances are macro_inst1 and macro_inst2) with direction internal.
VDD that is unresolved has two drivers:
create_supply_net VDD
connect_supply_net VDD -ports {macro_inst1/VDD_int macro_inst2/VDD_int}

For more information, refer to “Handling Multiple Connections to Virtual Supplies” in “VCS
NLP Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.

VCS NLP supports the -literal_supply option of the set_port_attributes command.
This option allows you to define the supply to be used to model a literal constant value
(1'b0/1'b1) associated to a pin/port marked with this option.

Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation
VCS NLP supports the set_retention -use_retention_as_primary option. When this
option is specified, the retention supply powers the output driver of the register. That is, the
primary supply of the output pin of the retention register is the retention supply.
Following is the syntax:
set_retention retention_name
-domain domain_name
[ -use_retention_as_primary]
For more information, refer to “Support for use_retention_as_primary for Isolation
Semantics” in “VCS NLP Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for Atomic Power Domains
VCS NLP supports atomic power domains as per 1801-2018 version of the UPF LRM.
As per LRM, extent of an atomic power domain can be modified, that is, updating the
-elements {} and -exclude_elements {} of an atomic power domain is allowed.
You must use the -atomic option of the create_power_domain command to define an
atomic power domain. Following is the syntax for creating an atomic power domain:
create_power_domain <name> -atomic
[-elements element_list]
[-exclude_elements exclude_list]
[…]

For more information, refer to “Support for Atomic Power Domains” in “VCS NLP Features”
in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for Modeling Isolation Cell Without Enable Pin in Liberty
VCS NLP supports modeling of an isolation cell without enable pin in the Liberty file. With
this enhancement, VCS NLP can insert isolation cells without an enable signal pin.
You must use the -isolation_signal option with empty braces (-isolation_signal {})
to specify that the tool to infer isolation cells with no enable pin.
For more information, refer to “Support for Modeling Isolation Cell Without Enable Pin in
Liberty” in “VCS NLP Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Tunneling SPICE Supply Ports Through UPF Supply Network
You can use the -power=ams_tunnel_thru_upf option at compile time to enable
tunneling of SPICE supply ports through UPF supply network. That is, when several
SPICE supply ports are connected to the same UPF supply net (in the same hierarchy or
different hierarchies), the SPICE supply ports are considered as connected inside analog,
and do not get the A2D/D2A interface elements inserted. This tunneling mechanism
replaces the connection with A2D/D2A interface elements by a direct connection inside
analog database.
For more information, refer to “Tunneling SPICE Supply Ports Through UPF Supply
Network” in “VCS NLP Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Creating Custom VCTs for Real Data Types
VCS NLP supports creating custom VCTs for real data types, including wreal and
real-valued SystemVerilog nettype HDL types. You can use the -function option of
the create_hdl2upf_vct and create_upf2hdl_vct commands to perform value
conversions between real data type and UPF::supply_net_type.

release, VCS NLP accepts the -applies_to option of set_port_attributes command

LRM.
For more information, refer to “Support for the SPA -applies_to Option without -elements”
in “VCS NLP Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.

Support for Type Real Option With the sim_corruption_control Command
VCS NLP supports type real option in the sim_corruption_control command. Following
is the syntax:
sim_corruption_control -type real
This feature allows you to disable corruption of real items and is applicable to complete
design hierarchy covered by the UPF.
For more information, refer to “Support for Type Real Option With the
sim_corruption_control Command” in “VCS NLP Features” in the VCS LCA Features
Guide.
Support for Golden UPF
In the UPF flow, each stage of the flow uses a single UPF file that is modified during
synthesis and physical implementation.
The original UPF file written with the RTL description is modified by the Design Compiler,
resulting in the UPF' (UPF prime) file. The UPF' file reflects the changes that occurred
during synthesis, such as, insertion of always-on buffers, isolation and retention cells, and
PG connections to the cells.
The UPF' file is modified by the IC Compiler, resulting in the UPF'' (UPF double prime) file.
The UPF'' file reflects changes that occurred during physical implementation, such as the
insertion of power switch cells.
VCS NLP supports the golden UPF flow. As per golden UPF flow, the Synopsys Galaxy
Implementation Platform offers a method of maintaining the UPF multi-voltage power
intent of the design using the original “golden” UPF file throughout the synthesis, physical
implementation, and verification steps, along with supplemental UPF files generated by
the Design Compiler and IC Compiler tools.
For more information, refer to “Support for Golden UPF” in “VCS NLP Features” in the
VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for Excluding Retention Elements From Retention Strategy
Starting with this release, the
set_retention
set_retention command is enhanced to support the
-exclude_elements option in the UPF. You must use the
-power=ret_exclude
-power=ret_exclude compile
option to enable this feature. This feature allows you to exclude some instances, blocks, or
registers from a retention strategy.
For more information, refer to “Excluding Retention Elements From Retention Strategy” in
“VCS NLP Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.

Setting Attributes on UPF Objects
Starting with this release, the set_design_attributes command is enhanced to allow
setting attributes on UPF objects. The UPF objects can be specified using the -elements
option of the set_design_attributes command. The attributes are specified using the
-attribute option.
For more information, refer to “Setting Attributes on UPF Objects” in “VCS NLP Features”
in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Searching Specified Scope and Its Descendant Hierarchy
Starting with this release, you can use the -traverse_macros option of the
find_objects command to search the specified scope and its entire descendant
hierarchy without considering the terminal_boundary/UPF_is_soft_macro marking
using the -traverse_macros option.
For more information, refer to “Searching Specified Scope and Its Descendant Hierarchy”
in “VCS NLP Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for Two Input Supply MUX in PG Function Expression
Starting with this release, VCS NLP supports specifying expressions in the pg_function
attribute of a liberty cell. The expression is a 2:1 MUX where the select is a signal pin and
the two data inputs are PG pins. The MUX pg_function support is only implemented for
two input supply MUX power switch with a select pin.
For more information, refer to “Support for Two Input Supply MUX in PG Function
Expression” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for Excluding Instances from a Power Domain
Starting with this release, VCS NLP supports the -exclude_elements option with the
create_power_domain command. Following is the syntax:
create_power_domain domain_name
[-elements element_list]
[ -exclude_elements exclude_list ]
[-update]

Where, -exclude_elements specifies the list of the design elements to exclude from
the effective element list (set of elements to which the command applies). The effective
element list is constructed from the arguments provided to the command.
For more information, refer to “Support for Excluding Instances from a Power Domain ” in

Support for UPF Power-Aware Converters
Starting with this release, VCS supports UPF power-aware converters. You must provide
a converter module whose conversion functionality depends on two SystemVerilog
variables declared locally inside the module. The attributes of these two variables are
snps_cm_power and snps_cm_ground respectively. These two local variables are of type
UPF::supply_net_type.
If the converter module is instantiated in the UPF power-managed region (under UPF
power-top), the local initializations are removed, and the two variables are driven from the
inferred power and ground rails specified in the UPF supply network.
For more information, refer to “Support for UPF Power-Aware Converters ” in the VCS
Heterogeneous Fanout Support
Heterogeneous fanout is a cross-domain net that drives multiple fanouts with different
sink supplies. This feature enables VCS NLP to insert isolation cells in the extent of the
location domain rather than the exact logical hierarchy of the domain boundary.
With this support, the isolation strategy with the -sink or -diff_supply_only option
inserts isolation cells when the fanouts have different supplies and the location is self/
parent.
For example, the following case is supported for isolation heterogeneous fanout support:
set_isolation iso1 -domain PDB1 -location parent -applies_to output -sink
ss1set_isolation iso2 -domain PDB1 -location parent -applies_to output
-sink ss2
To enable this feature, you must set the design attribute hetero_fanout_isolation to
TRUE as follows:
set_design_attributes -elements {.} -attribute {hetero_fanout_isolation
TRUE}
The attribute must be specified for the top design instance.
For more information, refer to “Heterogeneous Fanout Support” in “VCS NLP Features” in
Controlling NLP Report Dumping
Starting with this release, you can use the -power_report=<switch> compile option to
control the dumping of reports. You can use this option to enable or disable the reports
that are dumped in the low power analysis stage based on your requirement.
This feature improves compile performance for large designs by dumping only the required
reports. Also, you can disable dumping of all reports by default in the regression mode.

For more information, refer to “Controlling NLP Report Dumping” in “VCS NLP Features” in
Support for Logic Port/Net and Connections
Starting with this release, you can use the -power=logic_port_net compile option to
achieve Synopsys UPF Flow compatibility for the following UPF commands:
• create_logic_net
• create_logic_port
• connect_logic_net
For more information, refer to “Support for Logic Port/Net and Connections” in “VCS NLP
Support for the sim_assertion_control -control_expr Command
Starting with this release, the -control_expr option is supported with the
sim_assertion_control command. You must use the -power=sac_ctrl_expr compile
option to enable this feature. Following is the syntax:
sim_assertion_control
[-domain domain_name]
[-control_expr boolean_expression]
[-type <reset | suspend | kill>]
Any other option specified with the sim_assertion_control command is parsed and
ignored.
For more information, refer to “Support for the sim_assertion_control -control_expr
Command” in “VCS NLP Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
SDC LCA Enhancement
The following is the LCA SDC enhancement:
• Static Bug Finding in VCS
Static Bug Finding in VCS
Starting with this release, VCS leverages the structural analysis engines from VC
SpyGlass to perform dynamic SDC verification. Using this feature, you can inject jitter at
RTL to improve confidence for RDC sign off and verify the correctness of MCP at RTL
level by providing SDC to VCS.
VCS uses the database generated by VC SpyGlass and determines whether a glitch
or RDC property can fail. The database is in the SDC format that contains both user
constraints and property data.

This feature helps you with the following:
• Identify unsafe RDC using reset waveform

For more information, refer to the Static Bug Finding in VCS chapter in the VCS LCA

SystemVerilog LCA Features and Enhancements
The following are the SystemVerilog LCA features and enhancements:
• Support for Tagged Union
• Support for Unpacked Union
• Support for Pattern Matching of Tagged Union
• Support for Net with Data Types
• Changing Default Port Kind
• Support for Struct Type in DPI Python
• Support for Unpacked Tagged Union
Support for Tagged Union
A tagged union is a type-checked union. Typically, for an ordinary (untagged) union,
VCScan write union data values from one type and read the data values as another type
of the union. This is a potential loophole because it can write data based on one member
and then by mistake misread the stored data using another type.
Tagged union declarations prevent such accidental misuse of a union by enforcing type-
checking for each read and write on any of the members of the union. If you use a tagged
union instead of an untagged union, VCSdoes not read or write using a different member
from the member that was previously read from or written to.
For more information, refer to “Support for Tagged Unions” in “SystemVerilog Features” in

Support for Unpacked Union
Starting with this release, VCS supports unpacked union as specified in Section 7.3 of the
IEEE Standards for SystemVerilog LRM 1800-2012.
For more information, refer to “Support for Unpacked Union” in “System Verilog Features”
in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for Pattern Matching of Tagged Union
VCS supports the pattern of tagged union expressions in if-else conditional statements.
Starting with this release, VCS also supports the pattern matching of tagged union
expressions in case statements as specified in the Section 12.6 of the IEEE Standard
SystemVerilog LRM 1800-2012.
For more information, refer to “Pattern Matching for Tagged Union” in “SystemVerilog
Support for Net with Data Types
VCS supports net declaration with explicit data types as defined in the SystemVerilog
LRM. It also supports declaration of explicit port kind. You can use any of the net type
keywords or the keyword varto declare the explicit port kind. If you omit the keywords
during port declaration, the port kind is determined as per rules specified in the IEEE
SystemVerilog LRM Std. 1800-2012, Section 23.2.2.3.
VCS supports port kind in both ANSI and non-ANSI mode. In case of ANSI declaration,
rules are applied as per rules specified in the IEEE SystemVerilog LRM Std. 1800-2012,
Section 23.2.2.3. In case of non-ANSI declaration, net or variable declaration is complete
in itself and does not depend upon the I/O declaration that comes before or after the type
declaration.
For more information, refer to “Support for Net with Data Types” in “SystemVerilog
Changing Default Port Kind
For scalars, vectors, and packed structures or unions, you can use the
-sv_net_ports=packed option. This option treats ports with implicit port type and explicit
data type as net, as specified in LRM Section 23.2.2.3 Rules for determining port kind,
data type, and direction.
For more information, refer to “Changing Default Port Kind” in “SystemVerilog Features” in
the VCS User Guide.
Support for Struct Type in DPI Python
VCS supports struct type in DPI Python for import and export methods.

For more information, refer to “Support for Struct Type in DPI Python” in “SystemVerilog
Support for Unpacked Tagged Union
VCS supports packed tagged union. Starting with this release, VCS also supports
unpacked tagged union as specified in section 7.3.2 of the IEEE Standards for
SystemVerilog LRM 1800-2012.
For more information, refer to “Support for Tagged Unions” in “System Verilog Features” in
Verification Planner LCA Features and Enhancements
The following are the Verification Planner LCA features and enhancements:
• Supporting Enum Values for the Result Metric
• Enhancements to the Result Metric
• Support for Verification Planner Doc Annotator
• Support for Low Power Sub-Plans in HVP
Supporting Enum Values for the Result Metric
The result metric is enhanced to support enum-type values. When a new result metric
is added in an HVP plan, one new column is added for the metric and one column is
added for each of its enum values in XML plan, URG, and Verdi reports.
For more information, refer to “Supporting enum Values for the Result Metric” in
“Verification Planner Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Enhancements to the Result Metric
The enum-type result metric is enhanced to support the following:
• Derived percent
◦ When an enum-type result metric is created, a derived percent metric is created
automatically for each enum value.
• Goal expressions
◦ The goal expression evaluates the goal status for each score in the current plan/
feature scope.
• Metric expressions
◦ When a metric has no score in a feature, the metric is set to NULL. If a NULL metric
is used in an expression, that expression is evaluated to true.

Support for Verification Planner Doc Annotator
Verification Planner document annotator enables the creation of verification plans using
Microsoft Office (.doc) documents. It also enables back-annotation of coverage and other
scores into the .doc plan. The .doc verification plan must be formatted properly with
predefined styles and keywords built into the Verification Planner doc annotator.
You can use MS-Word 2003 and later versions to create the .doc verification plan. For
more information, refer to “Verification Planner MS Doc Annotation” in “Verification Planner
Support for Low Power Sub-Plans in HVP
Verification Planner provides support for adding Low Power (LP) plans into a normal HVP
plan as sub-plans. This feature helps in providing a complete overview of all the metrics
being considered for coverage. The added LP sub-plan is an instance in a normal HVP
plan. The score calculated for the plan is the average score of all metrics, including LP
metrics. You can then view the LP elements in the URG reports.
For more information, refer to “Support for Low Power Subplans in HVP” in “Verification
Planner Features” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Constraints LCA Features and Enhancements
The following are the Constraints features and enhancements:
• Constraints APIs for User-Defined ML Flow
• Using Constraints Debug Option for Detecting Conflict Error Caused by Hard
Partitioning
• Support for New Solver Mode and New Orchestration
Constraints APIs for User-Defined ML Flow
VCS provides a callback mechanism to call the API functions before or after each
randomize call to the constraint solver. These API functions influence the constraint solver
(without modifying the SV code) before each randomize call and get feedback after the
randomize task is done.
You must provide SystemVerilog design and C++ files. At compile stage, VCS compiles
the SystemVerilog design to generate simv and compiles the user-provided C++ files to
the shared library.
At runtime, simv imports the generated shared library and triggers callbacks in the shared
library. In your application, constraints and the values of variables can be observed or

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
modified through the Solver API call flow. This feature allows you to control the constraint
solver through APIs without modifying the SystemVerilog code.
For more information, refer to the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Using Constraints Debug Option for Detecting Conflict Error Caused by Hard
Partitioning
VCS provides the runtime option +ntb_solver_debug=<value> to detect the conflict error
that occurs due to hard partitioning. The following are the reasons for the hard partitioning:
• Solve before hard
• Array.size()
• Function call
The following is the use model of this feature:
% simv +ntb_solver_debug=<value>
For example,
%simv +ntb_solver_debug=cif_rca
Where,
<value>, can be cif_rca to generate Root Cause Analysis (RCA) report about
inconsistency. For more information, refer to the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Support for New Solver Mode and New Orchestration
Starting with this release, VCS provides the +ntb_solver_mode=6 option to enable
another solver mode. When set to 6, it is similar to 2 (which is with word-level solver), but
mode 6 is with bit-level solver that may work better with the constraints with arithmetic or
bitwise operations.
VCS provides the +ntb_solver_orch=value option which allows you to choose one of
constraint solver orchestration mode for the default solver mode (+ntb_solver_mode=3).
When set to 1, the orchestration uses the solvers in solver mode 1 and 2. When set to 2,
the orchestration uses solvers in solver mode 1, 2, and 6. The default orchestration mode
is 1.

Simulation LCA Features and Enhancements
The following are the Simulation LCA features and enhancements:
• Enhancement to RETAIN Calculation for Accurate Simulation Behavior
• Enhancement to Apply Module, Instance, and Hierarchical Tree Level Delays for
Sequential UDPs
Enhancement to RETAIN Calculation for Accurate Simulation Behavior
Starting with this release, the RETAIN calculation is delayed to the time when the delayed
signal changes for accurate simulation behavior. This feature is enabled with -sdfretain
and +neg_tchk options.
For more information, refer to “Delay in RETAIN Calculation for Accurate Simulation
Behavior” in “Gate-Level Simulation “ in the VCS LCA Features Guide.
Enhancement to Apply Module, Instance, and Hierarchical Tree Level Delays for
Sequential UDPs
Starting with this release, the -add_seq_delay option is enhanced to add delays in
module, instance, hierarchical tree level using a configuration file. For example, if you
consider the following modules:
module top; module A; module B;
A a1(); B b1(); udp u();
A a2(); B b2(); endmodule
endmodule endmodule
You can apply the following type of delays:
• defaultvalue n ns : Applies a delay of n ns in all UDP instances in the design.
• instance top.a1.b1.u n ns : Applies a delay of n ns to only one UDP instance.
• module top n ns : Applies a delay of n ns to all UDP instances in that module.
• tree top.a1 d n ns : Applies a delay of n ns to all UDP instances below top.a1 and
depth upto d.
• modtree A d n ns : Applies a delay of n ns to all UDP instances below A and depth
upto d
For more information, refer to “Applying Module, Instance, and Hierarchical Tree Level
Delays for Sequential UDPs” in the VCS LCA Features Guide.

FGP LCA Features and Enhancements
The following are the FGP LCA features and enhancements:
• Low Activity Event Profile
• Reducing Compile Time for FGP Grouping Analysis
Low Activity Event Profile
Starting with this release, a low EPC profiler is introduced to identify the sources of low
event activity, and help explore scope for addressing them to improve event activity.
For more information, refer to “Low Activity Event Profiler” in “FGP Features” in the VCS
Reducing Compile Time for FGP Grouping Analysis
You can use the -fgp=hier option to reduce the compile time and compile memory. This
option is particularly useful for gate-level simulation (GLS) designs.

• You must change the link from /bin/sh to /bin/bash (from /bin/dash).

Compile Script in the Master-Slave Flow
With the use of the master-slave flow, the vcs_tls.o file needs to be explicitly linked with
the main executable by using the following command:
% gcc master.c $VCS_HOME/<linux | linux64>/lib/vcs_tls.o -ldl
An executable file can be generated after compiling the vcs_tls.o file by using the
following command:
%g++ -m64 -ldl test.c main.c -I${VCS_HOME}/include -L${PWD}
$VCS_HOME/linux64/lib/vcs_tls.o -rdynamic -o ./master_exec

title: Verification Continuum™

VCS SystemC Cosimulation Interface
While these commands continue to be relevant, you can alternatively use the shared
object file from the VCS installation directly. Therefore, you can generate the executable in
any of the following two ways:
• By linking the libvcs_tls.so file with the master executable file as shown in the
following example:
%g++ -m64 -ldl test.c main.c -I${VCS_HOME}/include -L${PWD}
$VCS_HOME/lib/libvcs_tls.so -o ./master_exec
• By loading the executable file using LD_PRELOAD as shown in the following example:
setenv LD_PRELOAD $VCS_HOME/lib/libvcstls.so
%g++ -m64 -ldl test.c main.c -I${VCS_HOME}/include -L${PWD}
-o ./master_exec
Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL)
Starting with the V-2023.12-SP1 release, you can run VCS Base on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS on
Windows 10 through WSL1 or WSL2 with the Linux64 library. The VCS Base feature is
qualified on the 16 GB memory WSL/Windows 10 machines. The following packages are
required for Ubuntu 22.04 LTS:
• dc
• g++
• gcc
• make
• time
VCS does not support SystemC on WSL.

Download and Installation of the VG_GNU_PACKAGE
Several GNU GCC compiler versions are provided in the VG_GNU_PACKAGE along
with GNU tools (linker, assembler, and so on). Use the VG_GNU_PACKAGE for SystemC
compilation.

Download and Installation of the VG_GNU_PACKAGE
Installing and Using GCC 13.3.0
Use one of the following methods to install GCC 13.3.0:
• Installing and Setting Up GCC 13.3.0 Outside a VCS Image
• Installing and Setting Up GCC 13.3.0 Without Sourcing the source_me File
• Installing and Setting Up GCC 13.3.0 Inside a VCS Image
The Linux host must have a 64-bit OS and CPU.
Installing and Setting Up GCC 13.3.0 Outside a VCS Image
Follow the instructions provided in this section in either of the following scenarios:
• Installing the VG_GNU_PACKAGE outside the VCS image.
• Using the package for all VCS applications but not for SystemC.
You must add both gcc and binutils to the path. To update your path, use the
source_me scripts.
To install the default GCC version, perform the following steps:
1. Set up your environment by using the following commands:
% mkdir -p <path_to_vg_gnu_directory>/gnu
% cd <path_to_vg_gnu_directory>/gnu
2. Download the tar.gz file from the FTP server.
3. Untar the package.
4. Set the following VG_GNU_PACKAGE environment variable:
Bash (sh) users must execute the following commands:
% export VG_GNU_PACKAGE=<path_to_vg_gnu_directory>/gnu/linux
% $VG_GNU_PACKAGE/source_me.sh
C Shell (csh or tcsh) users must execute the following commands:
% setenv VG_GNU_PACKAGE
<path_to_vg_gnu_directory>/gnu/linux
% source $VG_GNU_PACKAGE/source_me.csh
When you source the source_me setup script from the VG_GNU_PACKAGE, the path to the
GCC shared libraries is prefixed with the LD_LIBRARY_PATH.

Download and Installation of the VG_GNU_PACKAGE
Installing and Setting Up GCC 13.3.0 Without Sourcing the
source_me File
This setup applies to Linux32 and Linux64 only.
If you cannot source one of the source_me files, use the xbin directory as an alternative.
Refer to Installing and Setting Up GCC 13.3.0 Outside a VCS Image to download and
install the VG_GNU_PACKAGE. However, do not source the VG GNU source_me file. Instead,
use gcc in the xbin directory. For example,
% <path_to_vg_gnu_directory>/gnu/linux/gcc/xbin/gcc myfile.c
In this case, xbin is used, not the bin. When you call the compiler through the xbin
directory, it automatically selects the corresponding binutils (assembler and linker). You
cannot override the location of binutils.
Installing and Setting Up GCC 13.3.0 Inside a VCS Image
The easiest method to use the VG_GNU_PACKAGE for VCS simulations that contain
SystemC is to install the package inside a VCS image. After installation, VCS
automatically uses this package for the VCS SystemC flow (for example, when you use
the syscan command).
Install the image at $VCS_HOME/gnu. The directory structure must be as shown in the
following figure:
Figure 3 VCS_HOME/gnu Directory Structure
$VCS_HOME/gnu/
linux/
g cc
b inutils
1. Download the linux_gcc1330_default.tar.gz package for your platform by using
the instructions provided in the Installing and Setting Up GCC 13.3.0 Outside a VCS
Image section.
2. Set up your environment by using the following commands:
% setenv VCS_HOME <VCS_installation_directory>
% cd $VCS_HOME

% mkdir gnu
% cd gnu
3. Untar the package by using the following command:
% gtar -zxvf linux_gcc1330_default.tar.gz
Do not set the VG_GNU_PACKAGE environment variable or source any setup script. When
VG_GNU_PACKAGE is set up in this manner, VCS automatically uses $VCS_HOME/gnu for the
VCS SystemC flow.
However, setting the VG_GNU_PACKAGE environment variable to a value disables the
automatic selection of GCC from $VCS_HOME/gnu. Therefore, before you use this feature,
unset the environment variable, as follows:
% unsetenv VG_GNU_PACKAGE
You can override the default with explicit command-line arguments such as -cc, -cpp, or
ld. Command-line arguments always take precedence over the default GNU package. It is
the only method to override the default compiler version.
VCS does not use the VG_GNU_PACKAGE when you are outside the VCS SystemC flow. For
example, calling % vcs top.v without the -sysc argument does not automatically infer
VG_GNU_PACKAGE. Instead, VCS uses the compiler in the current path as usual.
Prefixing the Path to Shared GCC Libraries With
LD_LIBRARY_PATH
As part of sourcing the setup script (by using source) from the VG_GNU_PACKAGE, the
path to the shared libraries of the GCC installation is prefixed with the LD_LIBRARY_PATH
variable. This ensures that the compiler and libraries are in synchronization with each
other.
Appending the path to the location of the libraries with the LD_LIBRARY_PATH can cause
issues.

VCS Documentation
VCS Documentation can be accessed on SolvNetPlus on the VCS landing page or as an
SPF file in the SolvNetPlus Downloads section along with other VCS SPF files. To access
the VCS documentation, log in to SolvNetPlus by using your SolvNetPlus login credentials
at:
https://solvnetplus.synopsys.com/s/
Firefox, Chrome, and Safari are the recommended browsers for SolvNetPlus. It
is recommended to use the latest version of the browser.
You can access the VCS Documentation in the following ways:
Accessing Documentation From the VCS Landing Page
1. Click the Documentation tab to open the Documentation page.
2. Click VCS to open the VCS landing page.
◦ You can also search for a document by using the SolvNetPlus advanced search
engine available on the SolvNetPlus homepage. The advanced search engine
provides search results from cases, STARs, and documentation. The following
figure shows the Advanced Search:
Figure 4 Advanced Search Engine
For more information about accessing documentation and articles, see the SolvNetPlus
FAQs page.
Accessing Documentation From the VCS Installation
1. Go to the $VCS_HOME/doc/UserGuide directory of your VCS installation.
You can view the HTML and PDF files and SmartSearch directories.

VCS SmartSearch is an application of Artificial Intelligence that uses Natural Language

It also enables you to specify the documents to search in. You can either search
the entire documentation set or only the selected documents using the Settings ->

Accessing Documentation for Archived Releases of VCS
You can access archived documentation in one of the following ways:

Archived Releases page.
On the Archived Releases page, click VCS to go to the VCS® Archived Releases
page.
• Alternatively, click Documentation > VCS. On the VCS landing page, choose
Additional Resources > Archived Releases to go to the VCS® Archived Releases
page.
Click the release number in the list to download the files for the required release.

VCS QuickStart Guide
The guide is intended for verification of both Verilog/SystemVerilog and VHDL designs and
describes only the three-step flow. You can access this document from SolvNetPlus by
searching for the VCS QuickStart Documentation article.

Limitations and Known Issues
This chapter describes the limitations and known issues in VCS in this release. A
workaround may be provided under each limitation.
• Limitations
• Known Issues
Limitations
The following are the limitations in this release:
• Maximum Number of Command-Line Characters
• Limitations on Coverage Metrics
• Word Flow Support of the Verification Planner Doc Annotator
• Limitations on VHDL 2008 Support
• Limitations on a VHDL Top Design
• Limitations on Enabling Pragmas for Tasks and Functions
Maximum Number of Command-Line Characters
There is a known limit to the number of characters that can appear on a vhdlan, vlogan,
or vcs command-line. This limit varies from platform to platform, but all platforms have
a limit. You can work around this limitation by using these commands with the -f or -F
options. These options specify a file that can contain compile-time options and source file
names.

Chapter 13: Limitations and Known Issues
Limitations
Limitations on Coverage Metrics
The following are the limitations on coverage metrics:
• VCS does not monitor the following language constructs in the IEEE Std 1364-1995
and 1364-2001 for condition or FSM coverage.
◦ Memories in Condition Coverage
VCS does not monitor condition coverage sub-expressions that contain memory
elements. VCS also does not extract FSMs where the current and next state of the
FSM are in memory elements.
◦ Multidimensional Arrays in FSM Coverage
VCS does not monitor condition coverage or extract FSM coverage for
multidimensional array elements.
Word Flow Support of the Verification Planner Doc Annotator
The Verification Planner Word Doc Annotator does not support OpenOffice XML input.
Only MS Word 2003 or newer versions are supported. This limitation applies only to the
Word flow. The spreadsheet flow supports both MS Excel and OpenOffice.
Limitations on VHDL 2008 Support
The following features are not supported on VHDL 2008 support:
• Enhanced generic-mapped packages
• The VHDL 2008 Local Packages feature is not supported for Coverage, Debug, Xprop,
NLP, and Verdi.
• The Unconstrained Elements in Generics and Generic Types feature has the following
limitations:
◦ The port associations at the VHDL/Verilog boundary is not supported.
◦ The type conversions are not supported.
◦ This feature is not supported for Coverage, Debug, Xprop, NLP, and Verdi.
• The VHDL Unconstrained Generic Formal Sub Element Association (FSA) feature is
not supported for multidimensional arrays FSA.
• The VHDL 2008 Generics in Subprograms feature is not supported in the KDB,
Coverage, and Xprop flows.

• The VHDL 2008 Record Type Conversions feature has the following limitations:
◦ The partially constrained array subtypes are not supported.
◦ Type conversions to a record subtype with unconstrained elements are not

Limitations on a VHDL Top Design
The following are the limitations on a VHDL top design:
• Only line, condition, and toggle coverage are available for the VHDL part of a mixed-
language design.
• ovaan -f file : The -f switch to ovaan is currently not supported.
• The -ova_debug and -ova_debug_vpd options are currently not supported. (Viewing of
assertion results with Verdi is also not supported.)
• The unit versions of the OVA Checker Library standard checkers are currently not
supported. Use only the template versions.
• The following items are not supported in inlined OVA:
◦ Memory in binding. For example,
bind module M : U I (clk, mem[addr]);
Here, mem is a declared multidimensional (two or more) array — for example, reg
[7:0] mem [255:0];
◦ VHDL extended identifiers in the design
◦ Assertions bound to instances inside a generate hierarchy
• OpenVera Assertions in the VHDL part of a mixed-signal design require the SUN
Solaris 9 (5.9 2.9) platform.
• Attributes like 'delayed(20 ns ) are not locally static, and so they are not allowed in
port bindings. They are not allowed in ordinary binding indications (pre-incremental
binding) so they are not supported yet with incremental binding either.
• In the C Language Interface (VHPI), there is a limitation on iteration over all callbacks
on Linux platforms.
Iterators created to get all the callbacks registered in a simulation run do not scan
through the value change callbacks for objects on the event side.

Checkpoint and Rewind
Checkpoint and rewind has not been tested with any of the third-party tool.
Methodology for Save and Restore
The following use models are supported for saving and restoring a simulation:
• Save using UCLI commands and restore using UCLI commands.
• Save the simulation state in Verdi and restore the state in Verdi.
• Save the simulation state in UCLI and restore the state in Verdi.
The following use model is not supported for saving and restoring a simulation:
• Save the simulation state in Verdi and restore the state using UCLI commands

Chapter 13: Limitations and Known Issues
Known Issues
You must close all external applications that communicate with VCS using the VHPI or
PLI, before you save and restore a simulation.
For more information on save and restore, see the Saving and Restarting the Simulation
section in the VCS User Guide, and the Restrictions for Save and Restore Commands
section in the Unified Command Line Interface User Guide.
Using an External Memory Manager
The internal memory manager in VCS relies on the following documented feature of
malloc:
void *malloc(size_t size);
The malloc() and free() functions provide a simple general-purpose memory allocation
package. The malloc() function returns a pointer to a block of at least size bytes suitably
aligned for any use.
Certain restrictive memory managers may choose to enforce a fixed memory alignment.
This can lead to unaligned accesses in some situations, which may produce bus errors.
If you want to use an external memory manager, Synopsys recommends thoroughly
reviewing the memory manager’s documentation for issues related to the alignment of
memory returned.
Displaying Value of Loop Variable in Verdi and UCLI
SystemVerilog enables you to declare the for loop control variable within a for loop. This
creates a local variable within the loop. In some cases, Verdi and UCLI cannot display the
value of a control variable declared within a for loop statement. The value can be printed
using the $display system task. The workaround is to move the declaration of the control
variable outside the for loop.
For example,
initial begin
for (int j=0;j<5;j++) begin
$display("j=%0d\n",j);
end
end
Workaround:
initial begin
int j;

cleared at the update time.

Overview
This document discusses two analysis techniques – merging and grading – that are used
to analyze the results of coverage-enabled regression runs. Merging combines data from
multiple tests and VDBs to produce a single unified VDB that contains the combined
results of all your test runs. Once the data is merged, you can generate reports or load
the merged data into Verdi to analyze the results. On the other hand, grading means
comparing the effectiveness of tests for coverage. Grading is useful when you want to
eliminate redundant tests from a test suite, arrange tests in a best-first order, or analyze
how much new coverage is added by a new regression run.
This document consists of the following sections:
• Merging
• Grading

Merging
For many designs, multiple simulations are required to close on all coverage areas. These
simulations yield coverage databases that represent different flows through the design.
After executing multiple simulations, you can merge the coverage databases that they
produced to get a single merged VDB containing all their combined results.
URG provides two methods of merging – serial and parallel merging. URG uses serial
merging as the default mechanism to merge test results. As the name implies, this
technique merges the coverage data of tests one after the other, serially. Coverage data
can be merged in parallel by specifying the -parallel option on the URG command line
to significantly speed up processing. You can direct URG to do the merging in parallel,
either on a single machine, on multiple machines, or on a compute farm/grid.
This section consists of the following subsections:
• Managing Coverage Data Files
• Merge Techniques
Managing Coverage Data Files
Using coverage produces some additional files and directories at compile and simulation
time. This section discusses how to manage the creation of these files, and how to merge
coverage data from multiple simulations.
When you compile with VCS, the executable name determines the name of the database
created. For example, the following command creates a binary executable simv1 and
a corresponding simv1.vdb directory, which contains compile-time coverage-related
information:
vcs -o simv1 file1.v file2.v -cm line+tgl
This section consists of the following subsections:
• Redirecting Coverage Data to the Directory of Your Choice
• Generating a Merged Database

Chapter 2: Merging
Managing Coverage Data Files
Redirecting Coverage Data to the Directory of Your Choice
To redirect coverage data to the directory of your choice, use the -cm_dir option in the
following ways:
1. Use the -cm_dir Option With Compile and Run Commands
The -cm_dir option is used to dump coverage data of multiple regressions to
a merged directory. For example, to dump compile-time data (design data) to
regress1_design.vdb use the following command:
vcs -cm line+tgl file5.v -cm_dir regress1_design.vdb
You can dump each simulation data (test data) to different directories. For example,
to dump test1 to regress1_run1.vdb and test2 to regress1_run2.vdb, use the
following commands:
simv -cm line+tgl -cm_dir regress1_run1.vdb -cm_name test1
-cm_test /regr1/run1/test1
simv -cm line+tgl -cm_dir regress1_run2.vdb -cm_name test2
-cm_test /regr1/run1/test2
In the example, the -cm_test option is used in conjunction with the -cm_name option
to specify the name of the test on the simv command line. The -cm_name option
designates a unique test name under the directory (created using the -cm_dir option).
The -cm_test option assigns the test an unambiguous name.
2. Use of -cm_dir at Compile Time Only
You can dump all simulation coverage data to the VDB directory specified at compile
time. For example, to dump both design data and test data to the regress2.vdb
directory specified at the compile time, use the following command:
vcs -cm line+tgl+fsm file3.v file4.v -cm_dir regress2.vdb

Generating a Merged Database
To merge all the coverage data collected from multiple regressions, use the -dbname
option on the URG command line. If both design and test data for all simulation runs are in
the same directory regress2.vdb, use the following command to produce a merged VDB
named mymerge.vdb:
urg -dir regress2.vdb -dbname mymerge.vdb

Merge Techniques
You can merge multiple VDB directories by specifying them after the -dir option on the
URG command line. The input VDBs can be generated at compile time, at simulation time,
or by another merge operation. For example:
urg -dir regress2_design.vdb regress2_run1.vdb mymerge.vdb -dbname
simv2.vdb ----_-noreport
This command reads all the specified VDB directories and merges them to create a new
VDB directory named simv2.vdb. The -noreport option does not generate a report at the
same time. It is better to generate reports separately.
If you have a long list of VDB directories to be merged, you can use the -f option to URG.
This option enables you to specify all the databases for merging in a file. For example, the
following urg -f command takes the list of databases for merging from the vdblist file:
urg -f vdblist -dbname final_merge.vdb -noreport
Merge Techniques
This section explains different merging techniques for the following metrics:
• Functional Coverage
• Code Coverage
Functional Coverage
Functional coverage consists of two metric types: covergroups and cover properties/
assertions.
This section focuses on providing information on covergroup merging and consists of the
following subsections:
• Basic Options and Switches for Covergroup Merging
• Covergroup Shapes in a Design
• Covergroup Shape Changes Due to Edits
Basic Options and Switches for Covergroup Merging
If a module contains a covergroup instance, then each instance of the module has a
separate covergroup reported for it. For example, consider the following mymod module:
module mymod;
…
mygroup g1 = new(x, y, z);
endmodule
