title: Verification Continuum™
text:
Introduction to Unreachability Analysis
VCS Unreachability (UNR) is a formal solution that determines the unreachable coverage
objects automatically from simulation. The UNR analysis uses VC Formal Coverage
Analyzer, which is a Synopsys static verification tool for performing formal coverage
analysis. This flow is specific to the structural coverage closure. It can be used in the later
phase of the structural coverage cycle after random simulation has reached a plateau,
beyond which it is not possible to monitor coverage.
Coverage closure functionality enables you to target and achieve a realistic coverage goal.
For example, consider the three colored blocks comprising 100% code coverage that you
intend to cover, as shown in Figure 1. The green colored block shows coverage that can
be achieved using constrained random verification, accounting to about 90% coverage.
The coverage beyond this range that is shown in blue and red color is difficult to achieve.
Figure 1 Coverage Closure Block Diagram
UNR shows unreachable goals in red. This helps you focus on the reduced set of goals,
shown in blue, when you create directed tests for simulation. It uses the coverage
database provided by you and invokes the formal engines for analysis as it is independent
of the stimulus. UNR finds the unreachable lines and conditions, thereby exposing the
hidden defects. You can also exclude an unreachable line or condition during report
generation if it is hindering the coverage closure.
Figure 2 shows how UNR analysis works to eliminate unreal goals and exposes hidden
defects.

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
Chapter 1: Introduction to Unreachability Analysis

Figure 2 Eliminating Unreal Goals
UNR enables you to save the unreachable coverage objects in the form of an exclusion
file. Initially, there are no exclusions as these are generated during the initial run. After the
exclusions are accepted, UNR has the capability to read the user-reviewed exclusions and
ignore these coverage goals for analysis. Therefore, it is not required to review the same
exclusions every time as shown in Figure 3.

Chapter 1: Introduction to Unreachability Analysis

Figure 3 Unreachable Iteration With RTL Change
When the design is stable, ensure that the targets marked as unreachable earlier are still
unreachable as shown in Figure 4.
Figure 4 Unreachable Validation When RTL is Stable

Chapter 1: Introduction to Unreachability Analysis
Coverage Metrics
You can perform the following functions with UNR:
• Import a simulation database.
• Run UNR on the remaining coverage goals.
• Save the unreachable coverage objects in the form of an exclusion file.
• If the design is modified, you can reuse the accepted exclusions and ignore them for
coverage analysis. The same exclusions need not be revisited.
• When the design is stable, you can ensure that the unreachable targets have not
become reachable.
This chapter discusses the following topics:
• Coverage Metrics
• Licensing Key Requirements
• Prerequisites for Using UNR
Coverage Metrics
UNR supports the following types of coverage metrics, which is a measure for verification
accountability:
• Line Coverage
Monitors which lines of code are exercised and which lines are not by your testbench
during a simulation run.
• Condition Coverage
Monitors whether certain expressions and sub expressions in your code evaluate to
true or false.
• Toggle Coverage
Monitors the value changes on signal bits in the design. By default, UNR does not
monitor toggle coverage for input ports of the design. To monitor toggle coverage for
input ports of the design, include the -tglInput option in the configuration file.
• FSM Coverage
In hardware, a Finite State Machine (FSM) uses sequential logic to show the current
state. It also uses combinational logic to decide the next state.

Chapter 1: Introduction to Unreachability Analysis
Licensing Key Requirements
UNR (Unreachability) compiles your design to check FSM coverage. It identifies which
statements in your source code belong to an FSM. Then, during simulation, it monitors
the states and transitions in that FSM.
• Branch Coverage
Branch coverage checks if conditional statements in your design are executed. These
include if/else statements, case statements, and the ternary operator ?:. By default,
Branch coverage analyzes which alternative of these conditional statements is covered
during simulation.
Licensing Key Requirements
UNR is an add-on feature for VCS. To use UNR, you must have the complete VCS license
suite and the following extra license keys:
• VC-STATIC-COMPILE
• VC-STATIC-COV
If you want to run UNR on a grid, you need one VC-STATIC-COV key for each parallel job.
If you have VC-FORMAL license keys, then you should be able to run UNR
without the additional UNR license keys.
Prerequisites for Using UNR
The following are the prerequisites for using UNR:
• It is assumed that the design under verification contains only synthesizable constructs.
If you include a testbench or other modules with non-synthesizable constructs in
the UNR analysis phase, you must wrap these constructs. You can wrap them
using a user-defined compiler directive or by placing them between //synopsys
translate_off and //synopsys translate_on synthesis pragmas.
For example,
module tb;

`ifndef SYNTHESIS
initial
$display(…);
…
initial
$finish;
`endif

Chapter 1: Introduction to Unreachability Analysis
Prerequisites for Using UNR
…
endmodule
During the UNR analysis phase, use the following compiler directive:
% vcs -unr=config.txt <other options> +define+SYNTHESIS
• When running UNR and your top module includes parameters, you can override these
parameter values for coverage analysis. Use the VCS -parameters or -pvalue
options to specify the overridden parameter values for the top module.
To provide a value to a specified parameter, use either one of the following switches
with the vcs command:
-pvalue+<parameter_hierarchical_name>=<value>

-parameters <filename>
For more information about how to use these switches, see vcs -help.
• When your design includes multiple top modules, use the VCS -top option to specify
them. Make sure to include any extra top modules in a file, for example, a .f file. You
have to then pass the *.f file in the VCS command line using the -f option, as shown
in the following command:
% vcs < vcs_options> -top top1 -f extra_top.f
Where,
%% cat extra_top.f
-top top2 -top top3
UNR does not allow you to pass multiple top modules directly in the vcs command
while processing. The following command does not work:
% vcs <vcs_options> -top top1 - top top2 -top top3
• Specify the -unr option directly in the VCS command line. It should not be included in
the file list provided with the -f option to VCS.

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
UNR Use Model
This chapter encompasses the procedures to invoke and compile UNR in different
compilation flows.
This chapter discusses the following topics:
• Performing Unreachability Analysis in a Two-Step Flow
• Performing Unreachability Analysis in the UUM Flow
• Performing Unreachability Analysis in the Single Step Flow
• Performing Unreachability Analysis in the Presence of SystemC Designs
Performing Unreachability Analysis in a Two-Step Flow
To invoke and compile UNR in a two-step flow, execute the following steps:
1. Generate the simulation coverage database for the required coverage metric, line,
conditional, toggle, branch, or FSM coverage. If you want UNR to compile for more
than one type of coverage, use the plus (+) character as a delimiter between the
arguments. For example,
% vcs -cm line+cond+tgl+branch+fsm <other_options>
% simv -cm line+cond+tgl+branch+fsm <other_options>
2. Invoke UNR and find the unreachable coverage using the following syntax:
% vcs -cm line+cond+tgl+branch+fsm -unr=config.txt <other_options>
% unrSimv -unr=config.txt

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
OR

% unrSimv -unr
As the <config.txt> file is not specified during runtime, compile-time configuration file
is used.
OR
You can use the following method only to save an exclusion file. The actual
unreachable analysis is not performed without using the -unr option.

Chapter 2: UNR Use Model
Performing Unreachability Analysis in a Two-Step Flow
% unrSimv -save_elfile=<el_FileName>
When you run unrSimv with the -save_elfile option without passing the -unr option,
exclusion file would be saved only if unreachable targets are already present from a
previous unrSimv run. In this mode, it is not required to pass the configuration file to
unrSimv.
3. Apply the exclusion file that has an unreachable coverage.
% urg -dir simv.vdb -report pre_unr
% urg -dir simv.vdb -report post_unr \
-elfile unreachables.el
Selecting Coverage Metric During Runtime
During runtime, you can choose to run the specific type of coverage metric among the
other metric types that you have specified during compilation. For example, if unrSimv
has been compiled for line and condition coverage, you can run unrSimv by enabling only
condition coverage at runtime using the following command:
% unrSimv -unr=config.txt -cm cond
If -cm is not specified during runtime, the coverage metric types that were specified during
the compilation are run by default.
Performing Unreachability Analysis Incrementally
You can run unrSimv multiple times by incrementally targeting the goals. In each
subsequent run, UNR only targets the goals that are not converged in the previous
session, thus improving the performance. UNR loads the previous session results, if
any, and continues to converge the remaining unsolved goals. The -maxTime variable in
the configuration file can be used to stop the run at the specified time and start the run
incrementally.
UNR does not support this feature if the tool exits because of an unexpected
termination or if you stop the process by pressing the CTRL+C key.
Running the Design Without the Configuration File
The compile-time configuration file is used when the <config.txt> file is not specified
during runtime. To run the design without the configuration file, use the following
command:
% unrSimv -unr

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
Chapter 2: UNR Use Model
Performing Unreachability Analysis in the UUM Flow
Running the Design and Saving the Exclusion File
You can use the following command to save an exclusion file. The actual unreachable
analysis cannot be performed without using the -unr option.
% unrSimv -save_elfile=<elFileName>
When you run unrSimv with the -save_elfile option without passing the -unr option,
the exclusion file is saved only if the unreachable targets are present from a previous
unrSimv run. In this mode, it is not required to pass the configuration file to unrSimv.
Performing Unreachability Analysis in the UUM Flow
To invoke and compile UNR in the Unified Use Model (UUM) flow, which uses the same
three-step flow, follow these steps:
1. Generate the simulation coverage database by instrumenting line, conditional, toggle,
branch, and FSM coverage using the following syntax:
% vlogan <options>
% vhdlan <options>
% vcs -cm line+cond+tgl+branch+fsm <other_options>
% simv -cm line+cond+tgl+branch+fsm <other_options>
VCS UNR supports VHDL for line, condition, branch, FSM, and toggle
coverage metrics. To monitor VHDL designs, set the variable -appVar
fml_enable_vhdl_cov as true.
2. Invoke UNR and find the unreachable targets. Add the -unr option during compilation
using the following syntax:
% vcs -cm line+cond+tgl+branch+fsm -unr=config.txt <other_options>
% unrSimv -unr=config.txt
You do not need to use the -unr option with the vlogan or vhdlan
command during compilation. VCS automatically selects the compiled
libraries based on the commands you run in the same directory or as
specified in the synopsys_sim.setup file.
When performing UNR analysis with VHDL designs, include the -kdb option
with the vhdlan compilation command. Without this option, the source and
instance views appear empty when viewing coverage in vdCov. For example:
$VCS_HOME/bin/vhdlan test.vhd -full64 -kdb

Chapter 2: UNR Use Model
Performing Unreachability Analysis in the Single Step Flow
The -kdb option is required to generate the knowledge database that
enables proper visualization of source code and hierarchy in coverage tools.
This applies to all VHDL files in your design to ensure complete coverage
visualization.
For more information about the usage of unrSimv, see sections Performing Unreachability
Analysis Incrementally and Selecting Coverage Metric During Runtime.
Performing Unreachability Analysis in the Single Step Flow
You can compile and run UNR in a single step using the -R option, as shown in the
following command:
% vcs <other_options> -unr =<configFile> -R
Performing Unreachability Analysis in the Presence of SystemC
Designs
You can use UNR to perform unreachability analysis in designs that include SystemC
designs as well. When you set the top module in the Verilog section of your design, UNR
analyzes only the Verilog part for unreachable code. The SystemC part of the design is not
included in the analysis.

Unreachability Configuration File
The UNR configuration file enables you to provide inputs to set up and run coverage
convergence. You can specify the configuration file using the following command:
% vcs -unr=< config_filename.txt> <other options>
where, <config_filename.txt> is the user-defined configuration file.
The -top option allows you to include the top module name for formal analysis and can be
included as follows:
-top < top_module_name_for_formal_analysis>
• For non-UUM flow, it is mandatory to include the -top option in the configuration file.
• For UUM flow, if you provide -top in the vcs command, it is not mandatory to include
-top in the configuration file. However, if you include -top in the configuration file, then
this gets preference over the -top option passed in the vcs command line.
SystemVerilog data types like interfaces are not supported at the top level
of the design. To workaround this, create a wrapper module. In this wrapper
instantiate the interface and the DUT. Then use the wrapper module as the
top-level module.
The following are the other inputs that you can optionally provide in the UNR configuration
file:
-fmlBase
Enables the Base licensing for UNR.
-fmlElite
Enables the Elite licensing for UNR.
-fmlLegacy
Enables the Legacy licensing for UNR.
-fmlToken
Enables the Token licensing for UNR.

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
-fmlUltra
Enables the VC Formal Ultra Licensing.
-licWait <time>
Enables you to set the time for which the tool needs to wait for license. The <time>
parameter is used to specify the time in minutes.
-clock <clockName> <timePeriod>
Allows you to specify a list of clock names and set the clock period for each clock in your
design. Use the <timePeriod> parameter to define the period for each clock. To add more
than one clock, use the -clock switch multiple times. This option also supports advanced
clocking, including gated clocks and clocks that cross between different domains.
UNR automatically recognizes unspecified clocks if you have not specified -clock in the
configuration file. The clock is extracted automatically for the design and UNR considers
them accordingly while processing the design.
-reset <resetName> <activeValue> <number_Of_Cycles>
Allows you to specify a list of reset names and their reset details for designs that use
resets. Use the <activeValue> parameter to set the active value of the reset signal. The
<number_Of_Cycles> parameter is optional. You can use it to define how many clock
cycles the simulator should run. To provide multiple resets, use the -reset switch more
than once.
-disableClockResetDetection
Allows you to disable the automatic clock or reset detection. By default, UNR detects
the clocks and resets in your design unless you specify them with the -clock or -reset
options.
The correctness of the result depends on proper constraining of clocks and resets. So, for
exhaustive unreachability analysis of the design, clocks and resets must be specified.
-constant <signalName> <constantValue>
Allows you to provide the list of ports or internal registers to be set as constants. Multiple
constants can be provided using multiple -constant switches.
-blackBoxes -type <design|cell> <Module_Or_InstanceName_to_be_blackboxed>
Allows you to provide the list of modules or instances to be black-boxed. To specify
multiple designs or cells of the same type, use the plus (+) separator.
For module-based black-boxing, use the following syntax:
-blackBoxes -type design <Module_Name_to_be_blackboxed>

For instance-based black-boxing, using the following syntax:
-blackBoxes -type cell <Instance_Name_to_be_blackboxed>
To specify multiple black boxes of different types, use multiple -blackBoxes switches.
For -type cell , the instance hierarchy must start below the top module. Do not include
the top module name. This helps VCS to find and black-box the right instance.
Example hierarchy:
```
top
m1
m2
```
To black-box only m2, use m1.m2 as the instance name.
-glassBoxes -type <design|cell> <Module_Or_InstanceName_to_be_glassboxed>
Allows you to provide the list of modules or instances that should be glass-boxed. When
this option is specified, UNR removes the logic inside the corresponding module. However,
all the instance hierarchy within that module is preserved. Note that the logic driving the
port connection of these instances is also removed. To specify multiple designs or cells of
the same type, use the plus (+) separator.
To specify multiple glass boxes of different types, use multiple -glassBoxes switches.
-maxTime <In_Minutes_Or_Hours>
Allows you to provide the maximum runtime. Use M or H as the suffix for Minutes or
Hours respectively. By default, maximum runtime is 24H. The default suffix is “H” if it is not
specified. Use negative value to make it unlimited.
-maxMemory <In_MB_Or_GB>
Allows you to provide the maximum memory usage. Use MB or GB as the suffix. By
default, the memory is 8GB and the default suffix is “GB” if not specified.
-grid <gridFarm> <no_Of_workers>
Allows you to provide the grid options. The gridFarm value can be LSF, SGE, RSH, lsf,
sge, or rsh. For example, -grid RSH 10 enables 10 workers on the current machine.
-gridOpts <extra_Options_To_Be_Sent_To_Grid>
Use the -gridOpts option to specify the additional options that should be sent to the grid.
This option must be used in conjunction with the-grid option.

title: Verification Continuum™
text:
For example, to setup the grid options for VCS UNR flow, use the following settings:
-grid lsf 10
-gridOpts "/home/nv/bin/qsub -C 0 -app affinity -R rusage[mem=16000] -We
720 -q o_cpu_128G_12H"
Note that the qsub command is part of -gridOpts. The -gridOpts option must include all
the options provided under the set_grid_usage control option.
-gridFile < grid_file_name>
Use the -gridFile option to specify the configuration file for a grid job submission. This
option must be used in conjunction with the -grid option.
The syntax of the configuration host file is as follows:
# 1<enable>|0<disable> | host <RSH/SSH only> | number of
workers |location of runtime temp files | grid type |
control string
Example:

title: 1 | M4 | 5 | /SCRATCH | RSH | rsh
text:
-covInput <path_To_Simulation_Coverage_Database>
Enables you to import the simulation coverage database. If no database is specified, it
runs the coverage analysis on the entire set of coverage targets. The entire set implies
that the coverage targets inferred for the entire design that is passed to UNR. If an input
simulation database is passed from outside, this simulation database is used to filter the
existing covered targets.
-covInputLoadAt compile|run|both
Tells UNR when to import the simulation coverage database specified with the -covInput
option. You can specify one of the following sub-options with -covInputLoadAt:
• compile - Imports the simulation coverage database specified with the -covInput
option at UNR compile time. This is the default option.
• run - Imports the simulation coverage database specified with the -covInput option at
UNR runtime.
• both - Imports the simulation coverage database specified with the -covInput option
both at UNR compile time and runtime.

To specify the -covInput option along with the -covInputLoadAt option is
mandatory , else an error message is issued.
-covDUT
<hierarchical_Path_To_The_Block_Instance_In_Coverage_Database_For_UNR>
Allows you to provide the hierarchical path in the simulation database to the module from
which UNR starts coverage analysis. It is optional. However, you must specify the path
if -covInput is provided and if the top module for UNR has multiple instances in the
simulation coverage database.
-fvDUT
< hierarchical_Path_To_The_Block_Instance_In_Formal_Wrapper_For_UNR>
Enables you to provide the hierarchical path in a formal wrapper to the module from which
UNR starts coverage analysis. Specifying the hierarchical path is optional. However, you
must specify the path if -covInput is provided and if the top module for UNR has multiple
instances in the simulation coverage database.
-covEL <List_of_exclusion_files_to_go_with_the_imported_coverage db>
Enables you to list the exclusion files that has to be used along with the imported coverage
database.
To specify multiple exclusion files, use the + separator as shown in the following syntax:
-covEl <elfille1>+<elfile2>+
-covElFilelist
Enables you to specify a file that contains a list of .el files.
Example:
-covElFilelist cov.f

Where, the cov.f file includes the following files:
```
test1.el
test2.el
test3.el
```
-checkEL
Allows you to validate the existing generated exclusions. However, this option does not
run complete unreachability analysis—that is, it does not find new exclusions. It verifies if
the previously generated exclusions are reachable or not. This option must be used with
-covInput and -covEL options.

-save_exclusion <path_to_Save_Exclusion_File/Name>
Allows you to provide the path and file name of an exclusion file in which you want to save
the exclusions.
By default, the exclusion file is always saved as unreachables.el.
-covBbEL <bbElFile>
Allows you to exclude the modules and instances which are added in the exclusion file,
<bbElFile>.
-saveExclusionsIncr <time>
Allows you to save the exclusion file on regular intervals of <time>.
Example: -saveExclusionsIncr 10S .
-tglInput
Enables monitoring of toggle coverage for input ports. By default, input ports are not
monitored for toggle coverage.
-tglUndrivenAsUNR
Enables classifying undriven toggle signals as unreachables. By default, undriven toggle
signals are reported as covered by UNR.
As the initial blocks are non-synthesizable, the formal tool ignores these blocks.
If there is no driver to a signal other than the driver in the initial block, effectually
the signal is considered undriven. Therefore, with the -tglUndrivenAsUNR
option, such signals are marked as uncoverable.
-tglXDrivenAsUNR
Enables classifying X driven toggle signals as unreachables. By default, X driven toggle
signals are reported as covered by UNR.
Signals or “bits of signals” that are driven either by x or driven by constant is
uncoverable with the -tglXDrivenAsUNR option only if the constant value is
same on all paths for each of the bits.
Example:
always_comb
begin
casez(my_sel)

4'b00??: begin
my_reg = 1'b0 ;
end
4'b01??: begin
my_reg = 1'b0 ;
end
4'b101?: begin
my_reg = 1'b0 ;
end
4'b110?: begin
my_reg = 1'b0 ;
end
default: begin
my_reg = 1'bx ;
end
endcase
end
In this example, my_reg is either 0 or x on all paths. Therefore, toggle transitions "1->0"
and "0->1" are uncoverable with the -tglXDrivenAsUNR option for my_reg.
-enableSVA
Enables SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) or Property Specification Language (PSL)
processing. By default, SVA or PSL processing is disabled in UNR.
Unreachability analysis is performed in an unconstrained environment. To make UNR
honor SVA constraints for the unreachability analysis, use the -enableSVA option.
-enableSvaUnr:
Dumps vacuous SystemVerilog Assertions in an exclusion file.
-enableCoverUnr
Runs SVA cover properties from FPV and saves the unreachable ones in exclusion file
The content of dumped exclusion file is as follows:
CHECKSUM: "1889283604"
INSTANCE: traffic.main
ANNOTATION: "VC_COV_UNR"
Assert prop "cover property"
-modTree:
Uses the configuration of the module tree from the input coverage database while running
the VCS UNR flow.
-modExcl:
Enables module-based exclusion dumping for common unreachables across all instances
of a specific module.

-modExclScope <list_of_scope>
Enables you to specify the list of modules or entities for which common unreachables
need to be dumped in an exclusion file. It is used with the -modExcl switch.
Example: -modExclScope {mod_a mod_b} In this example, mod_a and mod_b are two
specified scopes or modules.
-exclusionCrossfeed
Inline assertions in SystemVerilog designs are generally tied to a block of code and
might be deemed as unreachable if the block on which they reside is determined as
unreachable. However, you can use UNR to export this information to an exclusion file
using the -exclusionCrossfeed option. UNR provides the information about the number
of assertions and covers that are excluded.
You can later use this exclusion file either using -save_exclusion in the UNR config file
or the default exclusion file in the UNR mode to improve the assertion coverage numbers.
It is mandatory to use the -enableSVA option to extract the inline assertions
that are unreachable. If this feature is passed in the configuration file without
line coverage being enabled or -enableSVA being included, UNR issues a
warning message.
Example:
assign a = 1'b0;
reg c;
reg y1;

always@(*) begin
if(a)
begin
y1 = y;
A3:assert(1'b0);
CA3:cover(1'b0);
y = (a && b);
end
A1:assert(1'b0);
end
In this example, assertion A3 and coverage goal CA3 are unreachable because the code
block in which these are added is unreachable. If you add -exclusionCrossfeed option,
both of these are marked as unreachable and dumped into the exclusion file.

Limitations:
The following are the limitations with this feature:
• Concurrent inline assertions are not supported.
• Inline assertions in tasks and functions are not supported.
• Inline assertions in any non-synthesizable blocks (for example, initial blocks) are not
supported.
• If there are no statements with an unreachable block, VCS does not extract any goals
for that block. Therefore, any assertions present within that block are not marked as
unreachable.
• Unreachable nested assertions are not reported in exclusion file.
• Unreachable immediate assume statements are not reported in exclusion file.
• VHDL code is not supported.
-enableTopModExcl
Enables dumping of the module based exclusion file for the “top” module instead of the
default instance based dumping.
Module based dumping is enabled only for the “top” module. All the instances underneath
“top” are saved as instance base.
For example, consider a module TB that instantiates the module test as test.t1 and
test.t2. In the config file, top is test and the -covDUT is test.t1.
If you do not pass the -enableTopModExcl option, then the exclusions for module test are
saved only for test.t1. With -enableTopModExcl, however the exclusion is mapped to
test and thus, are applied to both test.t1 and test.t2.
-covergroup
Enables the monitoring of SystemVerilog covergroup coverage. By default, SystemVerilog
covergroup coverage is not monitored.
-verboseReport
Enables verbose reporting in addition to summary reporting. By default, UNR writes only
the summary report.
-appVar <name> <value>
Passes application variables to the formal tool. Use this option to pass an UNR application
variable and its value. Multiple application variables can be passed using multiple -appVar
switches.

The following table provides the list of various coverage-specific appVar variables:
Table 1 appVar Variables
Variable Value Type Default Usage
fml_cov_override_db_opt true Boolean false When this option is set to false
then it overrides the coverage
sub options, which were used
to generate the simulation
database and honors the
coverage sub options provided
in the VCS command line.
fml_cov_tgl_input_port false Boolean false Enables toggle coverage for
input ports.
fml_cov_tgl_only_seq false Boolean false Enables toggle coverage only for
sequential.

branch, and FSM coverage for
VHDL code.

and covers.

in line coverage.

true Boolean false Demotes the severity of

For example, you can use the following option to monitor toggle coverage for input ports
using -appVar as follows:
-appVar fml_cov_tgl_input_port true
where, fml_cov_tgl_input_port is the variable name to enable -tglInput.
If any environment variable is used in the configuration file, then use the Tcl
style environment variable, such as $env(variable_name).

sis

unreachables under
unconstrained analysis
fml_cov_alt_hier_file <hier_file_n
ame>

hier files passed through
the -cm_hier options to
the simulation. To pass the
different cm_hier file, use the
following command: -fmlVar
fml_cov_alt_hier_file
<hier_file_name>

nce

ode

fml_var fca_el_compress true, false Boolean false Enables compression mode

-help
Displays all the options that can be used in the UNR configuration file.
-constraint -expr <expression> |
-type <assert|assume> <Name_id_or_collection_of_properties>
Specifies the constraints. Note that -type and -expr cannot be specified together.
Use the -expr option to define a new expression as a constraint dynamically. Only one
expression can be provided at a time.
Use the -type option to define the existing assert or assume statements present in the
design as a constraint; multiple names, ids or collection of properties can be specified
using the “+” separator.
-buildTop <modulename>

Using VC Formal Coverage Analyzer Tcl Commands With UNR
Enables to perform coverage analysis for a sub-block of the complete design. This is
useful in scenarios, such as the following:
• When only a sub-block of the design needs to be analyzed from the coverage
perspective.
• When there are some unsynthesizable constructs in the elaboration top and you are
required to perform coverage analysis for only the synthesizable sub-blocks.
The -buildTop module name is used as the starting point for synthesis and coverage
goal extraction.
This chapter discusses the following topics:
• Using VC Formal Coverage Analyzer Tcl Commands With UNR
• Automatic Processing of Coverage Sub-Options
• Example
Using VC Formal Coverage Analyzer Tcl Commands With UNR
You can use the VC Formal Coverage Analyzer Tcl commands with VCS UNR by including
the following options in the UNR configuration file:
-preUnrComp
Syntax: -preUnrComp "<specific command>"
Enables you to provide the commands which should be executed before read_file/analyze/
elaborate.
-postUnrComp
Syntax:-postUnrComp "<specific command>"
Example: -postUnrComp "set_abstractions -construct {count = 5 }"
Enables you to provide the commands which should be executed after all the relevant
commands of VCS UNR compile are executed.
-preUnrRun
Syntax: -preUnrRun "<specific command>"
Example: -preUnrRun "report_fv -list" //In case you want to look at the
list of coverage goals extracted by the tool before doing a run
Enables you to provide the commands that must be executed before check_fv.
-postUnrRun

Using VC Formal Coverage Analyzer Tcl Commands With UNR
Syntax: -postUnrRun "<specific command>"
Examples,
-postUnrRun "report_fv -verbose -status unreachable"

-postUnrRun "source user.tcl"
//where user.tcl is a user created a tcl script

-postUnrRun "exec user.proc"
//where user.proc is a tcl proc created by user

-postUnrRun "save_cov_exclusion -file missing_else.el -missing_else"
//where missing_else.el file saves all the MISSING_ELSE
branch coverage properties
Enables you to provide commands which should be executed after all the relevant
commands of VCS UNR run are executed.
-preUnrResetSim
Syntax: -preUnrResetSim "<specific command>"
Example:
-preUnrResetSim "sim_force set -apply l"
To specify multiple commands at a time, separate each command with a semicolon inside
double quotation marks as follows:
-preUnrResetSim "sim_force set -apply l; sim_set_state -apply 0 -all;
sim_run 20 -stable"
The command enables you to control the reset state simulation behavior by forcing some
registers and then, performing simulation run for few clock cycles. Therefore, it enables
you to set multiple sim_force, sim_set_state , and sim_run
You can specify these options multiple times. All the commands provided with these
options should be a valid Tcl command, such as VC Static commands, sourcing Tcl file,
or executing a Tcl process. VCS UNR does not check these Tcl commands, however, it
passes these commands as is to the compile/run script that gets generated by UNR. In
case of any erroneous commands, the error handling happens in VC Static. For more
information about the Tcl commands, see the VC Static Platform Command Reference
Guide.
You cannot modify the check_fv command. If there is a conflict with existing
commands that UNR generates automatically, then you have to resolve the
conflict.

Automatic Processing of Coverage Sub-Options
The command to suppress message is as follows:
Syntax: -preUnrComp "suppress_message <message ID>"
Example: -preUnrComp "suppress_message <PROP_I_RESULT>" .
Enables you to suppress messages from being dumped in the log.
Automatic Processing of Coverage Sub-Options
If you import a simulation coverage database in the UNR flow, UNR automatically extracts
the coverage sub-options and applies these to the tool.
Example
Consider the following example in which the SYNTHESIS macro is used to separate
testbench or verification code from the DUT.
Example 1 Structure of Generic Testbench and DUT
DUT.v
module tb ();
`ifndef SYNTHESIS

//tb code, unsynthesizable
class a ();
`endif

DUT DUT_inst();
endmodule

module DUT (…..);
`ifndef SYNTHESIS
//verif code
`endif

//RTL code
subBlock subBlock_inst (……);
subBlock1 subblock1_inst (……);
endmodule

module subBlock (….);
`ifndef SYNTHESIS
//verif code
`endif

//RTL code
endmodule

Example
The following is the UNR configuration file with imported simulation coverage database:
### Formal top
-top subBlock

### Clocks
-clock clk 100

### Resets
-reset rst 1 10

### Constants
-constant subBlock.test_mode 0

### Blackboxes
-blackBoxes *ram_*
-blackBoxes *rams_*

### Resource limit
-maxTime 24.0
-maxMemory 128G

### Grid options
-grid sge 10
-gridOpts "-P bnormal -l
arch=glinux,os_distribution=redhat,os_version=WS4.0"

### Grid options
-grid RSH 10
### This option enables 10 workers on the current machine

### Exclusion file to be saved
-save_exclusion /home/user/fv/acc/subBlock/subBlock.el

### Start
### Simulation vdb info
-covInput /home/user/tb/simtests/merged.vdb
-covDUT tb.DUT_inst.subBlock_inst
To compile this example, use the following UNR commands:
% vcs -ntb_opts rvm -sverilog tb.v DUT.v -cm line+cond \
-unr=<configFile> +define+SYNTHESIS
% unrSimv -cm line+cond -unr=<configFile>

Performance and Convergence
As VCS UNR reports unreachability issues using exhaustive mathematical techniques, it
works best when applied at the block level. When you perform unreachability analysis on
large-sized blocks (or at a higher level in the design hierarchy, for example, subsystem
level or SoC level), VCS UNR might face capacity and performance challenges.
This chapter provides recommendations to reduce the complexity and improve the runtime
performance. These changes can help you achieve better convergence.
To improve the runtime performance, use a combination of the following techniques:
• Running Selective Coverage Metrics
• Excluding Bind Hierarchies From Coverage
• Partition Runs by Hierarchy Trees Using the -cm_hier Option
• Blackboxing Modules Where Coverage Analysis is Not Required
• Enabling Automatic Abstraction
• Controlling Compute Resources
• Auto Scale Flow
Running Selective Coverage Metrics
In most cases, the property count of toggle and condition metrics is higher than other
coverage types. Condition coverage metrics can make coverage analysis more difficult.
Complexity increases manifold if all the expressions in the design need additional logic to
monitor the coverage of those interesting points.
In many circumstances, for toggle coverage, simulation script has all the possible
switches to test all the design scenarios. However, you must check if the toggle coverage
monitoring from Formal is required for the MDAs. Since MDAs are performance intensive
for toggle coverage, add -cm_tgl mda with caution.
Avoid performing toggle coverage for input ports unless it is required. By default, toggle
coverage for input ports is not monitored by VCS UNR.

Excluding Bind Hierarchies From Coverage
In all the earlier listed cases, it is advised not to run all metrics at the same time. It is better
to run toggle and condition coverage separately.
Excluding Bind Hierarchies From Coverage
Formal Verification testbenches are often bound to the design using SV bind. Such
testbench modules are uninteresting for coverage collection and need to be excluded. Use
the -cm_instr exclude_bind_hierarchies option to enable the tool to automatically
determine such hierarchies, and then exclude the hierarchies with the -cm_hier option at
compile time.
The hierarchies excluded through the -cm_instr exclude_bind_hierarchies option
cannot be included back through +tree/+module rules in the cm_hier file. The option
takes priority over the cm_hier rules.
The other way to ignore bind hierarchies from the coverage is to set
fca_disable_bind_cov true as follows:
-fmlVar fca_disable_bind_cov true
or
-preUnrComp "set_fml_var fca_disable_bind_cov true"
Partition Runs by Hierarchy Trees Using the -cm_hier Option
Before running the unreachability analysis, check the number of coverage goals in all
hierarchies. For faster convergence, create cm_hier files strategically so that the number
of coverage goals is in the range of 50K. It is recommended to use cm_hier files to
partition the coverage goals as any constant propagation can still be carried through the
design.
The following are the steps to partition the coverage goals using the cm_hier files:
1. Open the coverage database with Verdi and identify the blocks/hierarchies which you
want to target.
2. Identify the subblocks within the instance hierarchy. Use the tooltip to find the number
of coverage goals in each subblock.
3. Split up the blocks into smaller manageable chunks based on the number of coverage
goals in each subblock. Then create a -cm_hier file for each one of them.
4. Run each -cm_hier file separately.
5. After the runs are completed, feed all the exclusion files to URG or Verdi Coverage
using -elfiles for reporting and analysis.

Blackboxing Modules Where Coverage Analysis is Not Required
6. During the VCS UNR run, pass the -cm_hier file using the following methods:
◦ When simulation database is not read, pass as an option to the VCS command as:
vcs -f filelist <other options> -cm_hier <hier file>
◦ When simulation database is read and to override the cm_hier file used during
the simulation, pass using the following command: -preUnrComp "set_fml_var
fml_cov_alt_hier_file <hier_file_name>" in the UNR config file.
7. If you want the tool to have both the simulation and alternate hierarchy files applied,
then use the following command:
-preUnrComp "set_fml_var fml_cov_hier_both true"
Syntax for the cm_hier File
The following is the syntax for the cm_hier file:
-/+module: to exclude/include a module in the analysis
-/+tree: to exclude/include the whole instance tree in the analysis
For more details on the cm_hier file syntax, refer to the VCS Coverage Technology User
Guide.
When a simulation coverage database for the full block is available:
Load the coverage database into a coverage viewer like Verdi or URG. Identify the
modules with poor coverage score. Target those modules first for unreachability analysis
using the -cm_hier switch of VCS. Load the exclusion files for each module into the
coverage viewer. Also, load the simulation coverage database. This helps you see the
improved coverage score.
When simulation coverage database is not available:
Avoid running VCS UNR at a full block level. Target subblocks of interest based on the
design knowledge using the -cm_hier switch of VCS.
For best results, perform unreachability analysis at the beginning of design development.
Do this before you start simulation-based verification.
Blackboxing Modules Where Coverage Analysis is Not Required
If your design includes modules that do not need coverage analysis, such as known
memories, analog modules, or DFT logic, you can blackbox these modules. This reduces
the build time.
Use the following command to blackbox:
-preUnrComp "set_blackbox -designs { <list_of_memory_modules> }"

Enabling Automatic Abstraction
or
-blackBoxes -type <design|cell> <Module_Or_InstanceName_to_be_blackboxed>
Enabling Automatic Abstraction
Operators like multipliers and adders increase the complexity and make convergence
difficult. To reduce the design complexity, abstract them selectively using the
set_abstraction command or use auto-abstraction to prune out complex operators all at
one time using the "-postUnrComp set_abstraction -auto on" command.
Using abstractions, the unreachables that are found are still valid. Note that the UNR
results with and without abstraction can be different. The run with abstractions finds fewer
UNRs. However, the sanctity of the UNRs found would still remain.
Controlling Compute Resources
To control the compute resources, do the following steps:
• Choose maximum memory and time
The unreachability analysis on large designs is time consuming. Run the analysis for
an adequate time (at least 24 hours) to get reasonable results. By default, in VCS
UNR the maximum time is 12 hrs. To increase the maximum time, use the following
command:
-maxTime 24H or -preUnrComp "set_fml_var fml_max_time 24H" .
By default, VCS UNR uses max solver memory of 8 GB. In general, solver jobs do not
need a large amount of memory. Avoid requesting 64 GB or higher memory resources
on the grid unless your job specifically needs it. Initially, set the grid for 8/16 GB
resources and in case of memout seen on the solver jobs, you can ask for more. This
can be increased as follows:
-maxMemory 16GB or -preUnrComp "set_fml_var fml_max_mem 16GB"
• Parallelize runs using the grid
If you have access to grid systems such as LSF or SGE, you can run jobs in parallel on
multiple cores. Use the following command to start the runs:
-grid LSF <number of cores> or -gridOpts <resource controlstring for
grid job submission, eg. { qsub -P bnormal -V arch=glinux }>
For the auxiliary worker process, 23 LSF slots are available. Each slot has 8
to 32 GB memory (set_grid_usage -type lsf=23 -control{ bsub -R
rusage[(mem=32]}). Twenty licenses can enable 23 workers.

For the main process, a machine has 8 to 32 GB memory. To launch the main process,
use the following VCS UNR command:
bsub -I -R "rusage[mem=8000]" vcs <> -unr unr_config.txt>
• Run the main and auxiliary worker processes on different machines. It is recommended
to use a dedicated or heavy machine to run auxiliary worker processes.
• Ensure there is no mem outs using the -postUnrRun "report_fml_jobs" command.
If the following warning appears, analyze the UNR runs and improve the grid memory
accordingly.
[Warning] CANT_SOLVE_ALL_GOAL: Some of the goals couldn't be solved.
Please review the status of formal jobs with 'report_fml_jobs' and
try increasing the resource limits or simplifying the verification
problem.
• Ensure the expected number of jobs or workers are run, using the -postUnrRun
"report_fml_hosts -totaltime" command. This command provides the number of
workers assigned during the run.
• It is advised to add -preUnrRun "check_config -worker_stat" command before
the run command so that the workers info is logged automatically.
In the VCS UNR setup, for large designs, handling complexity and large number of
coverage goals is the biggest challenge. To address this issue, the common method
followed is to manually partition the design and perform coverage analysis. Manually
partitioning the designs is not scalable as the iterative process to define partitions for
every design takes a lot of effort. Also, loss of information (for example, constants and
parameters) from the top module adds to the complexity of the setup.
To overcome this issue, VC Formal provides an auto scale flow. This feature helps you
reduce manual work when partitioning large designs for convergence. With auto scale you
can to do the following:
• Instrument coverage goals for simulation coverage holes only.
• Handle design complexity intelligently while maintaining consistency with the UNR
exclusions.
• Target coverage metrics as separate tasks and process them in parallel.

Methodology of Auto scale Flow
Use the auto scale flow when the number of coverage targets is more than 100K. The
following figure shows the methodology to auto scale coverage convergence with VC
Formal VCS UNR.
Enabling Auto Scale in VCS UNR
Use the -autoScale switch in config file to enable the auto scale flow.
Configuring Auto Scale in VCS UNR
Use the -preUnrComp "cov_config <option>" command to configure auto scale.
Syntax
[-line_task <line_task>] [-cond_task <cond_task>] [-branch_task
<branch_task>] [-tgl_task <tgl_task>] [-fsm_task <fsm_task>] [-cg_task
<cg_task>] [-limit <limit>] [-line_limit <line_limit>] [-branch_limit
<branch_limit>] [-tgl_limit <tgl_limit>] [-fsm_limit <fsm_limit>]
[-cond_limit <cond_limit>] [-module <module>] [-task_goal_limit
<goal_limit>] [-start_task_cmd <start_task_cmd>] [-end_task_cmd
<end_task_cmd>] [-start_line_task_cmd <start_line_task_cmd>]
[-start_cond_task_cmd <start_cond_task_cmd>] [-start_branch_task_cmd
<start_branch_task_cmd>] [-start_tgl_task_cmd <start_tgl_task_cmd>]
[-start_fsm_task_cmd <start_fsm_task_cmd>] [-start_cg_task_cmd
<start_cg_task_cmd>] [-exclude_assumes_covdb] [-exclude_bb_signals]

The following are the inputs you can provide:
• [-line_task <line_task>]: Specify the number of parallel tasks for running line
coverage metric.
• [-cond_task <cond_task>]: Specify the number of parallel tasks for running cond
coverage metric.
• [-branch_task <branch_task>]: Specify the number of parallel tasks for running
branch coverage metric.
• [-tgl_task <tgl_task>]: Specify the number of parallel tasks for running tgl
coverage metric.
• [-fsm_task <fsm_task>]: Specify the number of parallel tasks for running fsm
coverage metric
• [-cg_task <cg_task>]: Specify the number of parallel tasks for running cg coverage
metric.
• [-limit <limit>] : Specify the threshold coverage percentage. By default, it is set to
70. If the Any module whose total coverage percentage is greater than the specified
value is ignored by VCS UNR.
• [-line_limit <line_limit>] : Set the threshold value for line cov metric. VCS UNR
ignores any module whose number of uncovered goals for line metric is lesser than the
specified value.
• [-branch_limit <branch_limit>] : Set the threshold value for branch coverage
metric. VCS UNR ignores any module whose number of uncovered goals for branch
metric is lesser than the specified value.
• [-tgl_limit <tgl_limit>] : Set the threshold value for toggle coverage metric. VCS
UNR ignores any module whose number of uncovered goals for toggle metric is lesser
than the specified value.
• [-fsm_limit <fsm_limit>] : Set the threshold value for fsm coverage metric. VCS
UNR ignores any module whose number of uncovered goals for fsm metric is lesser
than the specified value.
• [-cond_limit <cond_limit>] : Set the threshold value for condition coverage metric.
VCS UNR ignores any module whose number of uncovered goals for the condition
metric is less than the specified value.
• [-module <module>] : Specify the scope from where the auto scaling should begin. By
default, auto scaling starts from the top module sent to VC Formal.
• [-task_goal_limit <goal_limit>] : Set the maximum number of coverage goals
per task.

• [-start_task_cmd <start_task_cmd>] : Specify the command to invoke after
individual task creation in the auto scale flow and before invoking check_fv.
• [-end_task_cmd <end_task_cmd>] : Specify the command to invoke after check_fv
is finished for each individual task in the auto scale flow.
• [-start_line_task_cmd <start_line_task_cmd>] : Specify the command to invoke
after task creation of line metric in auto scale flow and before invoking check_fv.
• [-start_cond_task_cmd <start_cond_task_cmd>] : Specify the command to invoke
after task creation of cond metric in auto scale flow and before invoking check_fv.
• [-start_branch_task_cmd <start_branch_task_cmd>] : Specify the command to
invoke after task creation of a branch in auto scale flow and before invoking check_fv.
• [-start_tgl_task_cmd <start_tgl_task_cmd>] : Specify the command to invoke
after task creation of tgl in auto scale flow and before invoking check_fv.
• [-start_fsm_task_cmd <start_fsm_task_cmd>] : Specify the command to invoke
after task creation of fsm in auto scale flow and before invoking check_fv.
• [-start_cg_task_cmd <start_cg_task_cmd>] : Specify the command to invoke after
task creation of cg in auto scale flow and before invoking check_fv.
Auto Scale Variables
The following are the variables available for auto scale:
• To enable auto scale in VCS UNR: -autoScale
• To disable model reduction, set the following variable to false: -preUnrComp
"set_fml_var fml_auto_scale_reduction false -global"
By default, the model reduction is enabled.
• To control the coverage percentage of scopes: -preUnrComp "cov_config -limit
<value_like_60_70_etc>".
By default, the percentage is set to 70.
• To control the number of coverage goals of scopes: -preUnrComp "cov_config
-<metric_type>_limit <value>"
• To set the scope from where to start the auto scaling flow: -preUnrComp "cov_config
-module <module_name>" .
By default, auto scale starts from the VC Formal top.
• To enable abstraction of complex operators: -preUnrComp "set_fml_var
fml_auto_scale_abs true -global"

• To disable parallel processing: -preUnrComp "set_fml_var
fml_auto_scale_disable_parallel true -global" .
The partitioning continues to happen and the tasks run in a sequential mode, one after
the other.
Running Auto Scale
The tool automatically runs the compute_cov command to start auto scale in the VCS
UNR flow. You do not need to add this command to the config file. The tool creates
separate tasks and divides the coverage targets by metric. These tasks run in parallel to
help coverage converge faster.
The number of the tasks is configured using the cov_config -<metric_type>_task
<number of tasks> command. By default eight tasks are created, one each for the
metrics like line, cond, branch, fsm_state, and fsm_trans and the remaining three are
for toggle. The number of tasks can be extended up to 16.
For each task, the compute_cov command:
• Runs unreachability analysis
• Creates an exclusion file
• Combines results back with the master task
Syntax
compute_cov [-run_finish <finishCmds>]
Where,
[-run_finish <finishCmds>]: Specify the set of commands to run when this command
finishes.
The number of toggle tasks should always be greater than or equal to three. It
cannot be configured to any number less than three.
Updating the Coverage Database
In auto scale, cov_config command is used to update the database after all the tasks are
completed:
cov_config -auto_scale -end_task_cmd "save_covdb -name <database name>
-update"
Use Model
The following are the settings in the configuration file that are used to auto scale with VCS
UNR.

-top traffic

-covEL exclorg.el

-covInput simv.vdb

-covDUT TB.T1

-clock clk 100

-reset rst 1

-autoScale

-preUnrComp "cov_config -limit 80"

-preUnrComp "set_fml_var fml_auto_scale_reduction false -global"

-preUnrComp "set_fml_var fml_auto_scale_abs true -global"

Managing Grid Settings in Auto Scale
The settings mentioned in the Controlling Compute Resources section working differently
for auto scale.
If you set the grid option to -preUnrRun "set_grid_usage lsf=5" or -grid lsf 5 , the
tool creates five tasks. Each task uses five workers, so there are 25 workers in total (5
tasks × 5 workers). If the number of tasks is greater than the number of available licenses,
the tool shows an error and stops running.
VCS UNR analysis on a real-world design is compute intensive. The amount of resources
needed depends on the design’s complexity and the number of coverage goals. Make
sure you have enough CPU resources and licenses. For best results, use 20 to 50 workers
for each task.

Limitations
The following is the limitation with the VCS Unreachability solution:
• Partition Compile and Precompile IP flows are not supported.

text:
-covInput <path_To_Simulation_Coverage_Database>
Enables you to import the simulation coverage database. If no database is specified, it
runs the coverage analysis on the entire set of coverage targets. The entire set implies
that the coverage targets inferred for the entire design that is passed to UNR. If an input
simulation database is passed from outside, this simulation database is used to filter the
existing covered targets.
-covInputLoadAt compile|run|both
Tells UNR when to import the simulation coverage database specified with the -covInput
option. You can specify one of the following sub-options with -covInputLoadAt:
• compile - Imports the simulation coverage database specified with the -covInput
option at UNR compile time. This is the default option.
• run - Imports the simulation coverage database specified with the -covInput option at
UNR runtime.
• both - Imports the simulation coverage database specified with the -covInput option
both at UNR compile time and runtime.

To specify the -covInput option along with the -covInputLoadAt option is
mandatory , else an error message is issued.
-covDUT
<hierarchical_Path_To_The_Block_Instance_In_Coverage_Database_For_UNR>
Allows you to provide the hierarchical path in the simulation database to the module from
which UNR starts coverage analysis. It is optional. However, you must specify the path
if -covInput is provided and if the top module for UNR has multiple instances in the
simulation coverage database.
-fvDUT
< hierarchical_Path_To_The_Block_Instance_In_Formal_Wrapper_For_UNR>
Enables you to provide the hierarchical path in a formal wrapper to the module from which
UNR starts coverage analysis. Specifying the hierarchical path is optional. However, you
must specify the path if -covInput is provided and if the top module for UNR has multiple
instances in the simulation coverage database.
-covEL <List_of_exclusion_files_to_go_with_the_imported_coverage db>
Enables you to list the exclusion files that has to be used along with the imported coverage
database.
To specify multiple exclusion files, use the + separator as shown in the following syntax:
-covEl <elfille1>+<elfile2>+
-covElFilelist
Enables you to specify a file that contains a list of .el files.
Example:
-covElFilelist cov.f

Where, the cov.f file includes the following files:
```
test1.el
test2.el
test3.el
```
-checkEL
Allows you to validate the existing generated exclusions. However, this option does not
run complete unreachability analysis—that is, it does not find new exclusions. It verifies if
the previously generated exclusions are reachable or not. This option must be used with
-covInput and -covEL options.

-save_exclusion <path_to_Save_Exclusion_File/Name>
Allows you to provide the path and file name of an exclusion file in which you want to save
the exclusions.
By default, the exclusion file is always saved as unreachables.el.
-covBbEL <bbElFile>
Allows you to exclude the modules and instances which are added in the exclusion file,
<bbElFile>.
-saveExclusionsIncr <time>
Allows you to save the exclusion file on regular intervals of <time>.
Example: -saveExclusionsIncr 10S .
-tglInput
Enables monitoring of toggle coverage for input ports. By default, input ports are not
monitored for toggle coverage.
-tglUndrivenAsUNR
Enables classifying undriven toggle signals as unreachables. By default, undriven toggle
signals are reported as covered by UNR.
As the initial blocks are non-synthesizable, the formal tool ignores these blocks.
If there is no driver to a signal other than the driver in the initial block, effectually
the signal is considered undriven. Therefore, with the -tglUndrivenAsUNR
option, such signals are marked as uncoverable.
-tglXDrivenAsUNR
Enables classifying X driven toggle signals as unreachables. By default, X driven toggle
signals are reported as covered by UNR.
Signals or “bits of signals” that are driven either by x or driven by constant is
uncoverable with the -tglXDrivenAsUNR option only if the constant value is
same on all paths for each of the bits.
Example:
always_comb
begin
casez(my_sel)

In this example, my_reg is either 0 or x on all paths. Therefore, toggle transitions "1->0"
and "0->1" are uncoverable with the -tglXDrivenAsUNR option for my_reg.
-enableSVA
Enables SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) or Property Specification Language (PSL)
processing. By default, SVA or PSL processing is disabled in UNR.
Unreachability analysis is performed in an unconstrained environment. To make UNR
honor SVA constraints for the unreachability analysis, use the -enableSVA option.
-enableSvaUnr:
Dumps vacuous SystemVerilog Assertions in an exclusion file.
-enableCoverUnr
Runs SVA cover properties from FPV and saves the unreachable ones in exclusion file
The content of dumped exclusion file is as follows:
CHECKSUM: "1889283604"
INSTANCE: traffic.main
ANNOTATION: "VC_COV_UNR"
Assert prop "cover property"
-modTree:
Uses the configuration of the module tree from the input coverage database while running
the VCS UNR flow.
-modExcl:
Enables module-based exclusion dumping for common unreachables across all instances
of a specific module.

title: 1 | M4 | 5 | /SCRATCH | RSH | rsh
text:
-modExclScope <list_of_scope>
Enables you to specify the list of modules or entities for which common unreachables
need to be dumped in an exclusion file. It is used with the -modExcl switch.
Example: -modExclScope {mod_a mod_b} In this example, mod_a and mod_b are two
specified scopes or modules.
-exclusionCrossfeed
Inline assertions in SystemVerilog designs are generally tied to a block of code and
might be deemed as unreachable if the block on which they reside is determined as
unreachable. However, you can use UNR to export this information to an exclusion file
using the -exclusionCrossfeed option. UNR provides the information about the number
of assertions and covers that are excluded.
You can later use this exclusion file either using -save_exclusion in the UNR config file
or the default exclusion file in the UNR mode to improve the assertion coverage numbers.
It is mandatory to use the -enableSVA option to extract the inline assertions
that are unreachable. If this feature is passed in the configuration file without
line coverage being enabled or -enableSVA being included, UNR issues a
warning message.
Example:
assign a = 1'b0;
reg c;
reg y1;

always@(*) begin
if(a)
begin
y1 = y;
A3:assert(1'b0);
CA3:cover(1'b0);
y = (a && b);
end
A1:assert(1'b0);
end
In this example, assertion A3 and coverage goal CA3 are unreachable because the code
block in which these are added is unreachable. If you add -exclusionCrossfeed option,
both of these are marked as unreachable and dumped into the exclusion file.

Limitations:
The following are the limitations with this feature:
• Concurrent inline assertions are not supported.
• Inline assertions in tasks and functions are not supported.
• Inline assertions in any non-synthesizable blocks (for example, initial blocks) are not
supported.
• If there are no statements with an unreachable block, VCS does not extract any goals
for that block. Therefore, any assertions present within that block are not marked as
unreachable.
• Unreachable nested assertions are not reported in exclusion file.
• Unreachable immediate assume statements are not reported in exclusion file.
• VHDL code is not supported.
-enableTopModExcl
Enables dumping of the module based exclusion file for the “top” module instead of the
default instance based dumping.
Module based dumping is enabled only for the “top” module. All the instances underneath
“top” are saved as instance base.
For example, consider a module TB that instantiates the module test as test.t1 and
test.t2. In the config file, top is test and the -covDUT is test.t1.
If you do not pass the -enableTopModExcl option, then the exclusions for module test are
saved only for test.t1. With -enableTopModExcl, however the exclusion is mapped to
test and thus, are applied to both test.t1 and test.t2.
-covergroup
Enables the monitoring of SystemVerilog covergroup coverage. By default, SystemVerilog
covergroup coverage is not monitored.
-verboseReport
Enables verbose reporting in addition to summary reporting. By default, UNR writes only
the summary report.

fml_cov_tgl_ignore_reset false Boolean false Causes the application to ignore

coverage analysis.
fml_var fca_el_compress true, false Boolean false Enables compression mode
for exclusion files for toggle
coverage.
When the exclusion file for
toggle coverage is large for
multi-bit signals, say [255:0]
sig, it takes time to load in
Verdi/Coverage database. To
reduce the size, the 256 items of
toggle exclusion are compressed
into one exclusion item.
Under this switch if both the
transitions 0->1 & 1->0 of
all bits of a vector/MDA are
unreachable, then the entire
signal is saved in the exclusion
file as one excluded item instead
of all the bits individually.

-constraint -expr <expression> |
-type <assert|assume> <Name_id_or_collection_of_properties>
Specifies the constraints. Note that -type and -expr cannot be specified together.
Use the -expr option to define a new expression as a constraint dynamically. Only one
expression can be provided at a time.
Use the -type option to define the existing assert or assume statements present in the
design as a constraint; multiple names, ids or collection of properties can be specified
using the “+” separator.
-buildTop <modulename>

title: 1 | M4 | 5 | /SCRATCH | RSH | rsh
text:
Using VC Formal Coverage Analyzer Tcl Commands With UNR
Enables to perform coverage analysis for a sub-block of the complete design. This is
useful in scenarios, such as the following:
• When only a sub-block of the design needs to be analyzed from the coverage
perspective.
• When there are some unsynthesizable constructs in the elaboration top and you are
required to perform coverage analysis for only the synthesizable sub-blocks.
The -buildTop module name is used as the starting point for synthesis and coverage
goal extraction.
This chapter discusses the following topics:
• Using VC Formal Coverage Analyzer Tcl Commands With UNR
• Automatic Processing of Coverage Sub-Options
• Example
Using VC Formal Coverage Analyzer Tcl Commands With UNR
You can use the VC Formal Coverage Analyzer Tcl commands with VCS UNR by including
the following options in the UNR configuration file:
-preUnrComp
Syntax: -preUnrComp "<specific command>"
Enables you to provide the commands which should be executed before read_file/analyze/
elaborate.

To specify multiple commands at a time, separate each command with a semicolon inside

sim_run 20 -stable"
The command enables you to control the reset state simulation behavior by forcing some
registers and then, performing simulation run for few clock cycles. Therefore, it enables
you to set multiple sim_force, sim_set_state , and sim_run
You can specify these options multiple times. All the commands provided with these
options should be a valid Tcl command, such as VC Static commands, sourcing Tcl file,
or executing a Tcl process. VCS UNR does not check these Tcl commands, however, it
passes these commands as is to the compile/run script that gets generated by UNR. In
case of any erroneous commands, the error handling happens in VC Static. For more
information about the Tcl commands, see the VC Static Platform Command Reference
Guide.
You cannot modify the check_fv command. If there is a conflict with existing
commands that UNR generates automatically, then you have to resolve the
conflict.

Automatic Processing of Coverage Sub-Options
The command to suppress message is as follows:
Syntax: -preUnrComp "suppress_message <message ID>"
Example: -preUnrComp "suppress_message <PROP_I_RESULT>" .
Enables you to suppress messages from being dumped in the log.
Automatic Processing of Coverage Sub-Options
If you import a simulation coverage database in the UNR flow, UNR automatically extracts
the coverage sub-options and applies these to the tool.
Example
Consider the following example in which the SYNTHESIS macro is used to separate
testbench or verification code from the DUT.
Example 1 Structure of Generic Testbench and DUT
DUT.v
module tb ();
`ifndef SYNTHESIS

//tb code, unsynthesizable
class a ();
`endif

DUT DUT_inst();
endmodule

module DUT (…..);
`ifndef SYNTHESIS
//verif code
`endif

//RTL code
subBlock subBlock_inst (……);
subBlock1 subblock1_inst (……);
endmodule

module subBlock (….);
`ifndef SYNTHESIS
//verif code
`endif

//RTL code
endmodule

text:
Performance and Convergence
As VCS UNR reports unreachability issues using exhaustive mathematical techniques, it
works best when applied at the block level. When you perform unreachability analysis on
large-sized blocks (or at a higher level in the design hierarchy, for example, subsystem
level or SoC level), VCS UNR might face capacity and performance challenges.
This chapter provides recommendations to reduce the complexity and improve the runtime
performance. These changes can help you achieve better convergence.
To improve the runtime performance, use a combination of the following techniques:
• Running Selective Coverage Metrics
• Excluding Bind Hierarchies From Coverage
• Partition Runs by Hierarchy Trees Using the -cm_hier Option
• Blackboxing Modules Where Coverage Analysis is Not Required
• Enabling Automatic Abstraction
• Controlling Compute Resources
• Auto Scale Flow
Running Selective Coverage Metrics
In most cases, the property count of toggle and condition metrics is higher than other
coverage types. Condition coverage metrics can make coverage analysis more difficult.
Complexity increases manifold if all the expressions in the design need additional logic to
monitor the coverage of those interesting points.
In many circumstances, for toggle coverage, simulation script has all the possible
switches to test all the design scenarios. However, you must check if the toggle coverage
monitoring from Formal is required for the MDAs. Since MDAs are performance intensive
for toggle coverage, add -cm_tgl mda with caution.
Avoid performing toggle coverage for input ports unless it is required. By default, toggle
coverage for input ports is not monitored by VCS UNR.

Excluding Bind Hierarchies From Coverage
In all the earlier listed cases, it is advised not to run all metrics at the same time. It is better
to run toggle and condition coverage separately.
Excluding Bind Hierarchies From Coverage
Formal Verification testbenches are often bound to the design using SV bind. Such
testbench modules are uninteresting for coverage collection and need to be excluded. Use
the -cm_instr exclude_bind_hierarchies option to enable the tool to automatically
determine such hierarchies, and then exclude the hierarchies with the -cm_hier option at
compile time.
The hierarchies excluded through the -cm_instr exclude_bind_hierarchies option
cannot be included back through +tree/+module rules in the cm_hier file. The option
takes priority over the cm_hier rules.
The other way to ignore bind hierarchies from the coverage is to set
fca_disable_bind_cov true as follows:
-fmlVar fca_disable_bind_cov true
or
-preUnrComp "set_fml_var fca_disable_bind_cov true"
Partition Runs by Hierarchy Trees Using the -cm_hier Option
Before running the unreachability analysis, check the number of coverage goals in all
hierarchies. For faster convergence, create cm_hier files strategically so that the number
of coverage goals is in the range of 50K. It is recommended to use cm_hier files to
partition the coverage goals as any constant propagation can still be carried through the
design.
The following are the steps to partition the coverage goals using the cm_hier files:
1. Open the coverage database with Verdi and identify the blocks/hierarchies which you
want to target.
2. Identify the subblocks within the instance hierarchy. Use the tooltip to find the number
of coverage goals in each subblock.
3. Split up the blocks into smaller manageable chunks based on the number of coverage
goals in each subblock. Then create a -cm_hier file for each one of them.
4. Run each -cm_hier file separately.
5. After the runs are completed, feed all the exclusion files to URG or Verdi Coverage
using -elfiles for reporting and analysis.

Blackboxing Modules Where Coverage Analysis is Not Required
6. During the VCS UNR run, pass the -cm_hier file using the following methods:
◦ When simulation database is not read, pass as an option to the VCS command as:
vcs -f filelist <other options> -cm_hier <hier file>
◦ When simulation database is read and to override the cm_hier file used during
the simulation, pass using the following command: -preUnrComp "set_fml_var
fml_cov_alt_hier_file <hier_file_name>" in the UNR config file.
7. If you want the tool to have both the simulation and alternate hierarchy files applied,
then use the following command:
-preUnrComp "set_fml_var fml_cov_hier_both true"
Syntax for the cm_hier File
The following is the syntax for the cm_hier file:
-/+module: to exclude/include a module in the analysis
-/+tree: to exclude/include the whole instance tree in the analysis
For more details on the cm_hier file syntax, refer to the VCS Coverage Technology User
Guide.
When a simulation coverage database for the full block is available:
Load the coverage database into a coverage viewer like Verdi or URG. Identify the
modules with poor coverage score. Target those modules first for unreachability analysis
using the -cm_hier switch of VCS. Load the exclusion files for each module into the
coverage viewer. Also, load the simulation coverage database. This helps you see the
improved coverage score.
When simulation coverage database is not available:
Avoid running VCS UNR at a full block level. Target subblocks of interest based on the
design knowledge using the -cm_hier switch of VCS.
For best results, perform unreachability analysis at the beginning of design development.
Do this before you start simulation-based verification.
Blackboxing Modules Where Coverage Analysis is Not Required
If your design includes modules that do not need coverage analysis, such as known
memories, analog modules, or DFT logic, you can blackbox these modules. This reduces
the build time.
Use the following command to blackbox:
-preUnrComp "set_blackbox -designs { <list_of_memory_modules> }"

Enabling Automatic Abstraction
or
-blackBoxes -type <design|cell> <Module_Or_InstanceName_to_be_blackboxed>
Enabling Automatic Abstraction

Enabling Automatic Abstraction
or
-blackBoxes -type <design|cell> <Module_Or_InstanceName_to_be_blackboxed>
Enabling Automatic Abstraction
Operators like multipliers and adders increase the complexity and make convergence
difficult. To reduce the design complexity, abstract them selectively using the
set_abstraction command or use auto-abstraction to prune out complex operators all at
one time using the "-postUnrComp set_abstraction -auto on" command.
Using abstractions, the unreachables that are found are still valid. Note that the UNR
results with and without abstraction can be different. The run with abstractions finds fewer
UNRs. However, the sanctity of the UNRs found would still remain.
Controlling Compute Resources
To control the compute resources, do the following steps:
• Choose maximum memory and time
The unreachability analysis on large designs is time consuming. Run the analysis for
an adequate time (at least 24 hours) to get reasonable results. By default, in VCS
UNR the maximum time is 12 hrs. To increase the maximum time, use the following
command:
-maxTime 24H or -preUnrComp "set_fml_var fml_max_time 24H" .
By default, VCS UNR uses max solver memory of 8 GB. In general, solver jobs do not
need a large amount of memory. Avoid requesting 64 GB or higher memory resources
on the grid unless your job specifically needs it. Initially, set the grid for 8/16 GB
resources and in case of memout seen on the solver jobs, you can ask for more. This
can be increased as follows:
-maxMemory 16GB or -preUnrComp "set_fml_var fml_max_mem 16GB"
• Parallelize runs using the grid
If you have access to grid systems such as LSF or SGE, you can run jobs in parallel on
multiple cores. Use the following command to start the runs:
-grid LSF <number of cores> or -gridOpts <resource controlstring for
grid job submission, eg. { qsub -P bnormal -V arch=glinux }>
For the auxiliary worker process, 23 LSF slots are available. Each slot has 8
to 32 GB memory (set_grid_usage -type lsf=23 -control{ bsub -R
rusage[(mem=32]}). Twenty licenses can enable 23 workers.

For the main process, a machine has 8 to 32 GB memory. To launch the main process,
use the following VCS UNR command:
bsub -I -R "rusage[mem=8000]" vcs <> -unr unr_config.txt>
• Run the main and auxiliary worker processes on different machines. It is recommended
to use a dedicated or heavy machine to run auxiliary worker processes.
• Ensure there is no mem outs using the -postUnrRun "report_fml_jobs" command.
If the following warning appears, analyze the UNR runs and improve the grid memory
accordingly.
[Warning] CANT_SOLVE_ALL_GOAL: Some of the goals couldn't be solved.
Please review the status of formal jobs with 'report_fml_jobs' and
try increasing the resource limits or simplifying the verification
problem.
• Ensure the expected number of jobs or workers are run, using the -postUnrRun
"report_fml_hosts -totaltime" command. This command provides the number of
workers assigned during the run.
• It is advised to add -preUnrRun "check_config -worker_stat" command before
the run command so that the workers info is logged automatically.
In the VCS UNR setup, for large designs, handling complexity and large number of
coverage goals is the biggest challenge. To address this issue, the common method
followed is to manually partition the design and perform coverage analysis. Manually
partitioning the designs is not scalable as the iterative process to define partitions for
every design takes a lot of effort. Also, loss of information (for example, constants and
parameters) from the top module adds to the complexity of the setup.
To overcome this issue, VC Formal provides an auto scale flow. This feature helps you
reduce manual work when partitioning large designs for convergence. With auto scale you
can to do the following:
• Instrument coverage goals for simulation coverage holes only.
• Handle design complexity intelligently while maintaining consistency with the UNR
exclusions.
• Target coverage metrics as separate tasks and process them in parallel.
